dialogue:
[doctor] good morning , adaeze . i'm doctor underwood . how have you been since the last time ?
[patient] oh , not great , doctor . my stomach has been acting up for about four days now .
[doctor] i'm sorry to hear that . tell me what's going on .
[patient] it's this burning right up under my breastbone . and last night i noticed my stool was black , like tar . that scared me half to death .
[doctor] black stool is important , and i'm glad you came in today . has there been any blood that's bright red ?
[patient] no , no red . just black and sticky . i did n't want to say anything at first , but my neighbor desmond saw it on the bathroom floor and told me to call .
[doctor] i'm glad she told you . when you say burning , is it after you eat ?
[patient] usually about an hour after supper . and it wakes me up at night sometimes . i take a tums and it helps for maybe twenty minutes .
[doctor] any vomiting ?
[patient] i threw up once on tuesday . it was just my supper , no blood , and no coffee grounds that i saw .
[doctor] okay . any dizziness when you stand up ?
[patient] yes , a little . i grabbed the counter this morning . i thought it was just my blood pressure pills .
[doctor] that's a good thing to mention . what medicines do you take for your arthritis ?
[patient] i take naproxen , the big pills , twice a day for my knees . i've been on it for years . my sister said i should switch to tylenol but i never got around to it .
[doctor] okay , that's important . how much naproxen have you been taking lately ?
[patient] the same as always , two in the morning and two at night , five hundred milligrams each . maybe a few extra on the bad days this week , when the knees were flaring .
[doctor] any other medications , any blood thinners ?
[patient] just my lisinopril , and a little vitamin d . i do n't take aspirin , my cardiologist took me off that years ago .
[doctor] good . let me check your vitals . your blood pressure is one eleven over sixty eight sitting , and your pulse is one hundred and four . that's a little fast for you .
[patient] is that bad ?
[doctor] it means your body is working harder , probably because you've lost some blood . your temperature is ninety eight point four . let me listen to your heart and lungs .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] heart is regular , a little fast . lungs are clear . now let me press on your belly . does this hurt ?
[patient] yes , right here at the top . ouch . it's maybe a five out of ten right now .
[doctor] okay . no rebound and no guarding . your belly is a little tender in the upper middle . let's check your blood count and your kidney function today .
[patient] will i need to stay in the hospital ?
[doctor] possibly . i'd like to get labs first and then decide . the nurse is going to start an iv and draw the blood now . the main thing i'm checking is your hemoglobin , which tells me how much blood you've lost .
[patient] oh , i don't like needles .
[doctor] i know . we'll also check your kidney function because of the naproxen . and i want a stool test for blood and a look inside your stomach with a scope .
[patient] a scope , like the camera thing ?
[doctor] yes , a gastroenterologist would do an upper endoscopy . we'll make that referral today and i'll call them myself .
[patient] do you have a number i can call ? my daughter wants to be the one to talk to them .
[doctor] of course . the gastroenterology office number is 953-755-5373 . ask for the scheduling line and tell them it's urgent , black stools .
[patient] 953-755-5373 , okay , i'll write it down .
[doctor] now , i want you to stop the naproxen completely , starting today . no more ibuprofen or aleve either .
[patient] so what do i take for my knees ?
[doctor] tylenol , up to one thousand milligrams three times a day . no more than three thousand in one day .
[patient] okay . and the acid ?
[doctor] i'm starting you on omeprazole , twenty milligrams in the morning before breakfast .
[patient] the little purple pill . my sister took that .
[doctor] right . if the labs come back low on blood we may need to transfuse you . i'll let you know tonight .
[patient] my hands are shaky just thinking about it .
[doctor] i understand . are you safe to drive home ?
[patient] no , my daughter has to come get me . she's in the parking lot now .
[doctor] good . the nurse will get her set up with the discharge papers once we see the results .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Epigastric burning pain and black stools for four days.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Adaeze Mbeki is a 88-year-old female with osteoarthritis of both knees, hypertension, and gastroesophageal reflux who presents with four days of epigastric burning pain and black, tarry stools first noticed last evening. The burning occurs about one hour after meals and occasionally awakens her from sleep, with partial relief from calcium carbonate. She had one episode of non-bloody emesis on Tuesday containing food only, without coffee-ground material. She reports orthostatic lightheadedness this morning on standing. She has been taking naproxen 500 mg twice daily for several years and took additional doses this week during a flare of knee pain. She denies hematemesis, chest pain, or dyspnea. A neighbor, Desmond, first noticed the black stool on the bathroom floor and encouraged her to seek care.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

Osteoarthritis of both knees, hypertension, and gastroesophageal reflux. Previously on aspirin, discontinued by her cardiologist years ago.

MEDICATIONS

Naproxen 500 mg twice daily with additional doses this week, lisinopril daily, vitamin D supplement. Denies current aspirin use. Uses calcium carbonate as needed for heartburn.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Vitals: BP 111/68 seated, HR 104 and regular, temperature 98.4 F. Heart regular and mildly tachycardic. Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. Abdomen with mild epigastric tenderness, no rebound or guarding.

RESULTS

CBC, BMP, and stool occult blood test ordered; results pending at the time of this note.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Melena with suspected upper gastrointestinal bleeding in the setting of chronic NSAID use, consistent with NSAID-associated gastritis with bleeding. Hemodynamically borderline with mild tachycardia and orthostatic symptoms. Discontinue naproxen and avoid all NSAIDs, including ibuprofen and naproxen sodium. Start omeprazole 20 mg daily before breakfast. Check hemoglobin and kidney function; transfusion will be considered if hemoglobin falls. Urgent outpatient gastroenterology referral for upper endoscopy; office contact 953-755-5373.
2. Knee osteoarthritis pain: acetaminophen up to 3 g per day.
3. Hypertension: continue lisinopril.

Long term (current) use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatories (NSAID)

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Epigastric burning pain and black stools for four days.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Lauren Esposito is a 87-year-old female with osteoarthritis of both knees, hypertension, and gastroesophageal reflux who presents with four days of epigastric burning pain and black, tarry stools first noticed last evening. The burning occurs about one hour after meals and occasionally awakens her from sleep, with partial relief from calcium carbonate. She had one episode of non-bloody emesis on Tuesday containing food only, without coffee-ground material. She reports orthostatic lightheadedness this morning on standing. She has been taking naproxen 500 mg twice daily for several years and took additional doses this week during a flare of knee pain. She denies hematemesis, chest pain, or dyspnea. A neighbor, Rania, first noticed the black stool on the bathroom floor and encouraged her to seek care.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

Osteoarthritis of both knees, hypertension, and gastroesophageal reflux. Previously on aspirin, discontinued by her cardiologist years ago.

MEDICATIONS

Naproxen 500 mg twice daily with additional doses this week, lisinopril daily, vitamin D supplement. Denies current aspirin use. Uses calcium carbonate as needed for heartburn.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Vitals: BP 111/68 seated, HR 104 and regular, temperature 98.4 F. Heart regular and mildly tachycardic. Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. Abdomen with mild epigastric tenderness, no rebound or guarding.

RESULTS

CBC, BMP, and stool occult blood test ordered; results pending at the time of this note.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Melena with suspected upper gastrointestinal bleeding in the setting of chronic NSAID use, consistent with NSAID-associated gastritis with bleeding. Hemodynamically borderline with mild tachycardia and orthostatic symptoms. Discontinue naproxen and avoid all NSAIDs, including ibuprofen and naproxen sodium. Start omeprazole 20 mg daily before breakfast. Check hemoglobin and kidney function; transfusion will be considered if hemoglobin falls. Urgent outpatient gastroenterology referral for upper endoscopy; office contact 670-913-4787.
2. Knee osteoarthritis pain: acetaminophen up to 3 g per day.
3. Hypertension: continue lisinopril.

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , gwen . it's good to see you again . how are you feeling at twenty weeks ?
[patient] pretty good , doctor valdivia . the baby is kicking like crazy . my breathing has been okay , mostly .
[doctor] mostly ? tell me what's been going on .
[patient] well , i had a bad night last week . i woke up coughing and my chest felt tight . i used my albuterol twice that night . i think it was the dust at work .
[doctor] where do you work now ?
[patient] i'm an inventory clerk at vantage call center . i'm on the floor of the warehouse a lot , counting pallets , and there's always dust from the cardboard . i told my manager i need to be upstairs at the desk more .
[doctor] that makes sense . when you say tight , is it mostly at night or during the day too ?
[patient] mostly at night and first thing in the morning . during the day it's fine unless i'm in the warehouse for a long time .
[doctor] how often are you using your rescue inhaler ?
[patient] maybe three or four times a week lately . before i got pregnant it was about once a month .
[doctor] okay . are you still using the controller inhaler every day ?
[patient] the one with the steroid ? yes . i take it every morning and rinse my mouth after . i forgot it twice last week .
[doctor] good , that's the right one . we switched you to budesonide because it's one of the safest ones in pregnancy . how did the nurse teach you the technique ?
[patient] the nurse showed me with the spacer . i think i'm doing it right .
[doctor] let's check . your oxygen level is ninety seven percent and your respiratory rate is sixteen . your blood pressure is one ten over sixty six . let me listen to your chest .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] i hear some wheezing at the bottom of both lungs , mostly on the way out . it's mild . no crackles . the baby's heartbeat was one forty when the nurse checked you in .
[patient] that sounds right . they said it was strong .
[doctor] it is . any swelling , headaches , or bleeding ?
[patient] no bleeding . my ankles were puffy after my shift on tuesday but it went down overnight .
[doctor] okay . and your blood pressure at home ?
[patient] it's been normal . the cuff at home says about one twelve over seventy .
[doctor] good . anything new in your life ?
[patient] we moved into a new apartment on the east side of durango last month . it's near the river and i walk along the path at lunch . i try to walk about a mile every day .
[doctor] that's wonderful exercise . do you still play pickleball on the weekends ?
[patient] i stopped in the spring . my husband says i'm not allowed to chase balls anymore . i still coach the team at the riverside rec center on saturdays , though .
[doctor] that's a good call . let's talk about the labs from last visit . your glucose screen came back normal , and your iron is a little low .
[patient] i've been taking the iron pill but it makes me constipated .
[doctor] try a stool softener and more fiber . we can also switch to a different form of iron .
[patient] okay . i'd like that .
[doctor] do you have trouble getting refills at the pharmacy ?
[patient] sometimes . i pick them up at the harbor pharmacy on fenwick road , and they have to order the spacer . i'm usually there on tuesdays after my shift .
[doctor] i'll send the next refill to the harbor pharmacy on fenwick road too , and ask them to hold a spacer for you .
[patient] thank you . my sister has asthma too , and my grandmother did . i think it runs in the family . i'm the youngest of four , so there's always someone around .
[doctor] that's helpful to know . the detailed ultrasound is scheduled for next month . do you know the date ?
[patient] i think it's the twelfth . my mom is coming to the appointment with me .

[patient] thank you . i'd appreciate that .
[doctor] okay . come back in four weeks , or sooner if you need the rescue inhaler more than every other day . if you have chest tightness that doesn't go away , or your lips look blue , go to the emergency room right away .
[patient] i will . thank you , doctor .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Routine follow-up for asthma at 20 weeks gestation with worsening nocturnal symptoms.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Gwen Obrien is a 26-year-old G1P0 female at 20 weeks gestation with mild intermittent asthma who presents for follow-up. She reports a night last week with cough and chest tightness, requiring albuterol twice. Symptoms are worse at night and on waking. Rescue inhaler use has increased to three to four times weekly, compared with about once monthly before pregnancy. She attributes the symptoms to dust exposure at work. She is an inventory clerk at Vantage Call Center, spending much of her shift on the warehouse floor counting pallets among cardboard dust. She reports adherence to daily budesonide, with two missed doses last week.

She denies vaginal bleeding, headache, or visual changes. Ankle edema after long shifts resolved overnight. She recently moved to an apartment on the east side of Durango, where she walks about one mile daily along the riverside path. She stopped playing pickleball this spring and now coaches a recreational team. She is the youngest of four siblings. Her sister and maternal grandmother also have asthma.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

Mild intermittent asthma since childhood. Low iron stores in pregnancy, on oral iron supplementation with constipation. Glucose screening normal.

MEDICATIONS

Budesonide inhaler 160 mcg twice daily, increased today to 220 mcg twice daily. Albuterol HFA as needed. Prenatal vitamin. Oral iron every other day. Refills dispensed at Harbor Pharmacy on Fenwick Road.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Vitals: SpO2 97% on room air, respiratory rate 16, BP 110/66. Lungs with mild expiratory wheezing at both bases, no crackles. Fetal heart rate 140 bpm. No peripheral edema.

RESULTS

One-hour glucose screen within normal limits. Ferritin low. Detailed ultrasound scheduled for next month.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Mild intermittent asthma in pregnancy with worsening nocturnal symptoms and increased rescue use, suggesting suboptimal control. Increase budesonide from 160 mcg to 220 mcg twice daily. Continue albuterol as needed; reassured that albuterol is safe in pregnancy. Occupational dust exposure is a likely trigger. Recommended a respiratory mask on the warehouse floor; employer letter provided.
2. Iron deficiency in pregnancy with constipation: continue oral iron every other day, add stool softener and dietary fiber, consider alternative iron formulation.
3. Routine prenatal care at 20 weeks; detailed ultrasound next month; return in four weeks, sooner if rescue use exceeds every other day or red flag symptoms occur.

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , beatriz . come on in . how have you been since we saw you in the spring ?
[patient] pretty good , doctor contreras . i've been on the new pill every day , i have n't missed one .
[doctor] that's great . any side effects ? stomach trouble , headaches , anything like that ?
[patient] a little nausea the first two weeks , but that's gone . my sleep is better , honestly .
[doctor] good . your liver numbers from last month came back . tell me what you noticed when you got them .
[patient] i saw the enzymes were a little high , the alt was like sixty two ? i was worried it meant the medicine was bad .
[doctor] the alt is a little elevated , but it's not dangerous . we'll repeat it today . is there anything new going on , any alcohol or supplements ?
[patient] i have maybe one glass of wine on weekends . no supplements except a multivitamin . oh , and i started taking turmeric gummies because my roommate swears by them .
[doctor] that might be worth stopping for now , since turmeric can affect the liver . are you still smoking ?
[patient] yes , about half a pack a day . i'm trying to quit . i've got the patch on my arm right now . i had one cigarette this morning on the back step .
[doctor] that's okay , that's progress . the patch is a good start . how many days since your last cigarette ?
[patient] like four days , which is a record for me . the first two were awful . i kept chewing the gum at work .
[doctor] where do you work ?
[patient] i'm a dental assistant at eastgate veterinary clinic . i take the bus down maple street , and then i'm on my feet all day . the break room is the only place i can really step outside to think .
[doctor] that's a hard setting to quit in . what triggers you most ?
[patient] coffee in the morning and my lunch break , when i'm standing outside the back door . my roommate isabel smokes too sometimes , so it's easy to just take one from her .
[doctor] okay . does isabel know about your hepatitis ?
[patient] yes , she knows . she got tested last year , and she's negative , thank god . she got the vaccine too . i made sure of that .
[doctor] that's very good . hepatitis b spreads through blood and sexual contact , so as long as you're taking your medicine and your viral load stays down , the risk is very low . but the vaccine is the best protection for her .
[patient] i'll tell her to keep up on it .
[doctor] let's look at your vitals . your temperature is ninety eight point six , your blood pressure is one hundred and eight over seventy , and your pulse is seventy two . let me feel your belly .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] your liver edge is just barely palpable , and it's not tender . no yellow in your eyes , and no swelling in your legs . good .
[patient] that's a relief .
[doctor] the viral load from last month was undetectable , which is what we want . so the medication is working . the enzymes being a little up can happen from many things , including the turmeric , so we'll see if it settles .
[patient] what's the plan with the medication ?
[doctor] keep taking the tenofovir alafenamide , twenty five milligrams once a day . we want to keep you on it long term . i'll also order an ultrasound of your liver to look at the scarring , and a fibroscan to measure the stiffness .
[patient] an ultrasound and a scan . will those hurt ?
[doctor] no , the fibroscan is a little probe pressed on your ribs for about ten minutes . there's no needle .
[patient] okay . i can do that on a day off .
[doctor] good . now , the nicotine patch : we'll keep the fourteen milligram patch for six weeks , then taper . and let's add gum for cravings .
[patient] will the patch and the gum together be okay ?
[doctor] yes , that's common and safe . i'd like you to call the quitline too . they will call you back within a day or two .
[patient] can i just do it online ?
[doctor] you can do both . i'll write the referral , and the nurse will walk you through the quitline sign-up before you leave .
[patient] the nurse is so nice . last time she helped me get my refill sorted out .
[doctor] i'm glad . what about your weekends ? are you getting outside at all ?
[patient] yes , i hike the trail along the lake at northgate mall when the weather's good . i used to go with my brother , but he moved to pueblo last month . so it's just me and my dog now .
[doctor] that's nice exercise . how's your energy been ?
[patient] pretty good , honestly . i can do the full hike again without stopping , which i could n't do last year .
[doctor] wonderful . so the plan is : continue the tenofovir , repeat the liver labs in six weeks , ultrasound and fibroscan next month , and the quit plan with the patch and gum .
[patient] okay . and if the enzymes go up again ?
[doctor] then we'll look at other causes and maybe get a specialist to weigh in . but i'm not too worried right now .
[patient] thank you , doctor . i'll see you in six weeks .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up for chronic hepatitis B on tenofovir alafenamide and tobacco cessation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Beatriz Cavanaugh is a 28-year-old female with chronic hepatitis B infection on tenofovir alafenamide who returns for follow-up. She reports good adherence without missed doses. She had mild nausea during the first two weeks of therapy, which has resolved. Sleep has improved. Recent liver enzymes showed mild elevation of ALT, approximately 62 U/L. She started turmeric gummies recommended by a roommate and reports one glass of wine on weekends.

She currently smokes about half a pack of cigarettes daily and is using a nicotine patch. She smoked one cigarette this morning. She has been abstinent for four days, the longest period so far, and reports cravings during morning coffee and at her lunch break.

Her roommate, Isabel, is hepatitis B negative and has been vaccinated. She works as a dental assistant at Eastgate Veterinary Clinic, a job involving prolonged standing. She commutes along Maple Street. She hikes the lakeside trail at Northgate Mall when weather permits and reports she can now complete a full hike without stopping, which was not possible last year.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

Chronic hepatitis B infection. Tobacco use disorder.

MEDICATIONS

Tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg by mouth once daily. Nicotine patch 14 mg per 24 hours and nicotine gum as needed. Multivitamin daily. Turmeric supplement.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Vitals: temperature 98.6 F, BP 108/70, pulse 72. Liver edge palpable just below the costal margin, nontender. No scleral icterus. No lower extremity edema.

RESULTS

HBV DNA undetectable on most recent assessment. ALT mildly elevated on prior panel. Repeat hepatic function panel drawn today. Liver ultrasound and transient elastography (FibroScan) ordered.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Chronic hepatitis B, virologically suppressed on tenofovir alafenamide. Mild transaminase elevation, likely multifactorial, possibly related to turmeric supplement; discontinue turmeric. Repeat hepatic panel in six weeks. Liver ultrasound and elastography to assess fibrosis.
2. Nicotine dependence, cigarettes: continue nicotine patch 14 mg for six weeks then taper; add nicotine gum for cravings. Referral to state quitline placed. Counseling provided on smoking cessation and relapse triggers.
3. Household contact: roommate should maintain hepatitis B vaccination; she is hepatitis B negative.
4. Follow-up in six weeks.

[patient] he's right . he's terrible about it , doctor .
[doctor] i'm glad you're here . let's go through the annual checkup , and then we'll talk about the knee . how's the knee been ?
[patient] it's been stiff in the mornings . i can walk to the mailbox fine , but the stairs are a chore now .
[patient] he won't take the cane . i've been telling him for a year .
[doctor] okay , we'll get to the cane . how long has the stiffness been going on ?
[patient] probably three or four years , getting worse slowly . the right one is worse than the left .
[doctor] any locking or buckling ?
[patient] no buckling . it catches sometimes when i get up from the couch .
[doctor] what's your activity like ?
[patient] i still garden , i do the tomatoes and the beans , and i walk the dog around the block . i can't kneel anymore though .
[patient] he hasn't knelt since the spring . he has to use a stool now .
[doctor] that makes sense . any swelling in the knee ?
[patient] a little after a long day , but it goes down overnight .
[doctor] okay . now your blood pressure . how has it been at home ?
[patient] i check it every morning . it's usually around one thirty five over eighty five . the pills aren't doing what they used to .
[doctor] how long have you been on the same medicine ?
[patient] the amlodipine and the lisinopril , both for about six years . i take them every morning with coffee . my wife checks that i took them .
[doctor] good . any headaches , chest pain , or shortness of breath ?
[patient] no , none of that . i get a little dizzy when i stand up too fast sometimes .
[doctor] okay . let's check your cholesterol as well . your last ldl was one sixty , and you're on a statin , correct ?
[patient] atorvastatin , ten milligrams . i keep forgetting to refill it .
[doctor] that's important . the washington guidelines suggest a lower target for someone with your history , so we'll talk about increasing it .
[patient] whatever you think is best . the pharmacy has been slow with my refills lately .
[doctor] i'll send the new prescription to the pharmacy on your side of town . now , your work history . you were at the plant for a long time , right ?
[patient] thirty one years at bayside shipyard , machinist , mostly on the lathes . before that i was at harmon tool and die , which closed in ninety eight .
[doctor] where did you live back then ?
[patient] cedar falls , about forty minutes north . we moved down here when the plant closed , and we've been here ever since .
[doctor] okay . and your hearing and eyes ? any trouble ?
[patient] my hearing is going , i turn the tv up too loud . my eyes are fine , i got new glasses last spring .
[doctor] are you still smoking ?
[patient] quit twenty years ago . i was a pack a day for thirty years .
[doctor] that's a big accomplishment . how about alcohol ?
[patient] two beers on friday , and that's the limit . my wife would kill me .
[doctor] good . let me check your vitals . your blood pressure is one forty over eighty two today . heart rate is seventy six . your weight is two hundred and nine pounds , which is up about six pounds since last year .
[patient] the holidays . the cookies at the church bake sale .
[doctor] mm . i'll pull up your chart , your number is mrn550757 . let me examine your knee . does this hurt when i press here ?
[patient] yeah , on the inside of the knee .
[doctor] there's crepitus when you bend it , and mild tenderness along the joint line . no warmth or redness . your range of motion is about one twenty degrees on the right and one thirty five on the left .
[patient] that sounds about right .
[doctor] your lungs sound clear , and your heart is regular without murmurs . no leg swelling .
[doctor] okay . we got your labs from last week . your a one c is five point eight , which is in the prediabetes range .
[patient] prediabetes , that's the one before sugar diabetes ?
[doctor] right . so we want to focus on diet and walking .
[patient] i can do the walking . the wife says i need to lay off the bread .

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , victor . i'm doctor vance . what brings you in today ?
[patient] i twisted my ankle pretty bad on monday morning . it's the left one . it's swollen like a balloon .
[doctor] i'm sorry to hear that . tell me how it happened .
[patient] i drive a forklift on the night shift , and i'd come off a bad low . my sugar was like fifty two , and i was dizzy , so i got off the forklift to grab some juice from the break room . i stepped down off the dock and my foot just rolled under me .
[doctor] okay . so you were low on sugar at the time . did you pass out or hit your head when you fell ?
[patient] no , i did n't black out . i was just dizzy and shaky . i did n't hit my head , i caught myself on the railing .
[doctor] good . what did you do after you fell ?
[patient] i sat down on the dock , ate two glucose tabs , and then a coworker drove me home . i iced it that night .
[doctor] which coworker was that ?
[patient] imani . he's always looking out for me .
[doctor] okay . how has your diabetes been overall ?
[patient] i've had type two for about nine years . i take glipizide every morning and i check my sugars four times a day . but the night shifts mess everything up , i eat at weird hours .
[doctor] i understand . how often are you having lows ?
[patient] maybe twice a month , more lately since they moved me to nights . i'd say one of them is really bad .
[doctor] i see . let's look at the ankle . is there pain on the outer side ?
[patient] yes , right here , on the outside . it hurts when i put weight on it .
[doctor] let me check . there's swelling and bruising over the lateral malleolus . can you wiggle your toes ?
[patient] yes . the toes move , but it hurts when i point my foot down .
[doctor] okay . your sensation is intact and your pulses are strong . there's no tenderness at the base of the fifth metatarsal . the drawer test is limited by the pain .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] we'll get an x-ray today . it's most likely a sprain , but i want to make sure there's no fracture .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] the x-ray shows no fracture , and the ankle is in good alignment . so i'm diagnosing a sprain of the ligaments on the outside of your ankle . here's the wrap and a walking boot for two weeks .
[patient] two weeks , and then i can go back to work ?
[doctor] i'd rather you not drive a forklift until you can bear full weight without pain . can your supervisor move you to light duty ?
[patient] maybe . i'll ask . i don't want to lose the night differential .
[doctor] the lows matter more right now . your last a one c was eight point four . you're taking the glipizide , and i want to add a continuous glucose monitor .
[patient] like a sensor on the arm ? my cousin has one .
[doctor] yes , it alerts you before the sugar drops . also , keep a glucose tab in your pocket on shift , and eat a snack at the start of your break .
[patient] okay . the washington guidelines say the sugar target is different for people like me ?
[doctor] that's a good question . the general target for most adults is an a one c under seven , but we can talk about something a bit looser given your lows .
[patient] okay , i'd like that .
[doctor] i'm also going to reduce your glipizide dose to five milligrams . and i'll check your kidney function today .
[patient] any side effects with the lower dose ?
[doctor] possibly more sugar swings , but the sensor should help . let's come back in four weeks to look at the sensor data .
[patient] will do . my wife will be happy about the sensor .
[doctor] good . any questions ?
[patient] just one . can i take a shower in the boot ?
[doctor] no , keep the boot dry and use a plastic bag . the wrap can come off at night .
[patient] okay . thanks , doctor .
[doctor] see you in four weeks . if your foot turns numb or cold , or the swelling gets worse , come in right away .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left ankle pain and swelling after a fall during a hypoglycemic episode.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Victor Ortega is a 36-year-old male with type 2 diabetes mellitus on glipizide who presents with left ankle pain and swelling following an inversion injury on January Fourteenth. He works as a forklift operator on the night shift at a distribution center. He developed symptomatic hypoglycemia with a reported glucose of 52 mg/dL and dizziness, stepped down from the loading dock, and his left foot rolled under him. He caught himself on a railing and did not lose consciousness or strike his head. He sat, ingested glucose tablets, and was driven home by a coworker. He applied ice that evening.

He reports recurrent hypoglycemia about twice monthly, worse since transitioning to night shifts with irregular meals.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

Type 2 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed in 2020.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Left ankle: swelling and ecchymosis over the lateral malleolus with tenderness to palpation. Able to move toes; pain with plantarflexion. Neurovascularly intact distally. No tenderness over the base of the fifth metatarsal. Anterior drawer limited by pain.

RESULTS

Radiographs of the left ankle show no fracture and an intact mortise.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Sprain of the lateral ligaments of the left ankle, initial encounter, following a fall on the same level. No fracture. RICE protocol, lace-up ankle wrap, walking boot for two weeks, weight-bearing as tolerated. Advised against operating a forklift until he can bear full weight without pain; discussed light duty with supervisor.
2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus with recurrent hypoglycemia, most recent A1c 8.4%. Reduce glipizide to 5 mg daily. Start continuous glucose monitor. Glucose tablets to be carried on shift. Individualized A1c target discussed given hypoglycemia risk. Renal function to be checked.
3. Follow-up in four weeks for review of continuous glucose monitor data.

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , tamara . i'm doctor delgado , thanks for coming in on the referral . what's been going on ?
[patient] hi , doctor . my family doctor thinks it's my thyroid . i've been losing weight even though i'm eating like a horse , and my heart races all the time .
[doctor] tell me more . when did it start ?
[patient] about four months ago . i lost about twelve pounds , and my hands shake when i'm holding a whisk . i'm a pastry chef at allied waste services , so my hands are everything .
[doctor] that's a difficult job with a tremor . what's a typical day look like ?
[patient] i'm in the kitchen at four in the morning . i'm on my feet ten hours and around the ovens all day . it's hot and i sweat through my shirts . i've been drinking way too much coffee to get through it .
[doctor] i see . how about sleep ?
[patient] i wake up at three and can't get back to sleep . my fitbit says my resting heart rate is around one ten , even when i'm sitting still .
[doctor] that's helpful data . do you notice your heart pounding at night ?
[patient] yes , sometimes i can feel it in my neck . and i'm always too warm , even when everyone else is cold .
[doctor] okay . any changes in your bowel habits ?
[patient] i'm going to the bathroom more , yes . loose stools two or three times a day .
[doctor] any eye changes , like grittiness or bulging ?
[patient] my eyes feel dry sometimes , and my husband says they look a little wider . i don't think they stick out though .
[doctor] okay . let's look . any family history of thyroid disease ?
[patient] my mother had her thyroid out after she had something like this . the doctors called it an autoimmune thing . she's on levothyroxine now .
[doctor] that's useful . the thyroid test your family doctor sent over was from 10/27/2021 . it showed a very low tsh and a high free t4 .
[patient] what does that mean ?
[doctor] your thyroid is making too much hormone . the most likely cause is graves' disease , an autoimmune condition where antibodies make the thyroid overactive .
[patient] graves . i've heard of it . is it curable ?
[doctor] it's manageable . there are medicines that slow the thyroid down , and there are treatments that can reduce the thyroid's activity for good .
[doctor] let me examine your neck . the thyroid is diffusely enlarged and firm , without distinct nodules . there's a fine tremor when you hold your arms out . your reflexes are brisk .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] your pulse is one oh four , your blood pressure is one thirty four over seventy eight , and your temperature is ninety eight point eight . no fever .
[patient] i'm always warm .
[doctor] let's get the antibody test today , the tsh receptor antibody . i also want your full thyroid panel and a complete blood count .
[patient] any blood work i should be worried about ?
[doctor] no , it's standard . what medicines are you taking now ?
[patient] just tylenol for the headaches , and the multivitamin . oh , and my family doctor started methimazole last month , ten milligrams in the morning .
[doctor] good . are you taking it every day ?
[patient] yes , every morning with my coffee . i did miss two doses because i was working a double shift .
[doctor] that's okay , but missing doses matters with methimazole . set an alarm on your phone . i'll continue the methimazole at the same dose and start propranolol to control your heart rate .
[patient] propranolol . is that going to make me tired at work ?
[doctor] at a low dose , it can cause some tiredness at first . take it with food .
[patient] okay . i'll try .
[doctor] i'd also like you to get a radioiodine uptake scan to help decide between medicine and radioactive iodine treatment . it's a quick test where you swallow a small capsule and we measure how much iodine your thyroid picks up .
[patient] will it hurt ?
[doctor] no , it doesn't hurt . the radiation dose is low . the scheduling team will send the paperwork .
[patient] radioactive iodine . that sounds scary .
[doctor] it's very common and well tolerated , and we'd go through the details before any decision . one thing : if you're planning to get pregnant in the next year , we need to avoid radioiodine and adjust the methimazole .
[patient] we're not planning that right now . my husband and i are just busy with the business .
[doctor] good . and about your work : the heat and the caffeine will make the symptoms worse , so try to cut the coffee to one cup before noon .
[patient] that's going to be hard . i'll try .
[doctor] also , if you get a fever , a sore throat , or a rash on methimazole , call us right away . methimazole can lower your white blood cell count .
[patient] okay . i'll call the number on the sheet .
[doctor] good . come back in six weeks with the blood test results . take care , tamara .
[patient] alright , thank you .

She denies eye pain or diplopia.

She works as a pastry chef at Allied Waste Services, starting shifts around 4 a.m. and spending about ten hours on her feet near ovens with significant heat exposure. She has increased her caffeine intake to cope with fatigue.

Family history is notable for her mother, who had autoimmune thyroid disease treated with thyroidectomy and is now on levothyroxine.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

Headaches managed with acetaminophen as needed.

MEDICATIONS

Methimazole 10 mg by mouth every morning, started last month by primary care; two doses missed during a recent double shift. Multivitamin daily. Acetaminophen as needed.

Vitals: HR 104, BP 134/78, temperature 98.8 F.
Neck: thyroid diffusely enlarged and firm, no discrete nodules. Fine bilateral tremor with arms extended. Reflexes brisk. No proptosis appreciated; mild lid retraction noted.

RESULTS

TSH markedly suppressed and free T4 elevated on outside thyroid panel dated 10/27/2021. TSH receptor antibody, complete thyroid panel, and complete blood count ordered.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Graves' disease with hyperthyroidism, diagnosed in 2021, with symptomatic tachycardia and weight loss. Continue methimazole 10 mg daily; counseled on adherence. Start propranolol at low dose for adrenergic symptoms. Radioactive iodine uptake scan to guide definitive treatment. Discussed pregnancy planning implications.
2. Occupational heat and caffeine exposure likely aggravating symptoms; advised limiting caffeine to one cup before noon.
3. Return in six weeks with laboratory results. Return precautions for fever, sore throat, or rash on methimazole.

[patient] hi , doctor radcliffe . better than last year , i think . my husband came along , he likes to check on the medicines .
[patient] somebody has to . she forgets her evening pill when the house is busy .
[doctor] that's always the hard part . how many episodes of the racing heartbeat have you had since we last talked ?
[patient] three that i noticed . the last one was about two weeks ago , in the middle of a shift . my heart went from normal to racing in a minute and a half , and i had to sit down on the floor of the hallway .
[doctor] tell me about the shift . what do you do for work ?
[patient] i'm a respiratory therapist at riverbend pharmacy , mostly nights in the emergency department . it's intense , and i was doing three codes that week . i think the adrenaline has something to do with it .
[doctor] that's very plausible . how long did the episode last ?
[patient] maybe forty minutes before it settled on its own . i checked my watch the whole time . the watch recorded the strip , and i sent the printout to the portal .
[doctor] yes , i saw it . it's an irregular rhythm at about one hundred and sixty with no clear p waves , which fits atrial fibrillation .
[patient] i was scared because my mom had a stroke at fifty-six .
[doctor] that's important family history . let's talk about the blood thinner . are you taking the apixaban twice a day ?
[patient] the eliquis , yes , five milligrams in the morning and at night . i have n't missed one in the last month . my husband sets up the pill box every sunday .
[doctor] good . any bleeding , bruising , or blood in the urine ?
[patient] i bruise easily on my shins from the bed frame , but that's been the same for years . no blood in the urine .
[doctor] okay . and the metoprolol ?
[patient] fifty milligrams twice a day . i get tired on it , especially in the afternoons , and my hands are cold when i'm on my feet all shift .
[doctor] that's a known side effect . how about your heart rate at rest ?
[patient] usually sixty something when i'm not at work . i rode my bike here today , actually , it was only four miles .
[doctor] wonderful . i'm glad you're getting exercise . what kind of exercise do you do ?
[patient] i swim at five forty five every morning at the rec pool , and on weekends i restore vintage motorcycles in my garage . my husband thinks it's a fire hazard .
[patient] it's a fire hazard . we have a fire extinguisher right next to the workbench .
[doctor] okay , and how old are the kids now ?
[patient] they're about four months . we just adopted them in the spring . it's been a whirlwind .
[doctor] congratulations . that's a lot for anyone , especially with your schedule . how are you sleeping ?
[patient] poorly , honestly . i wake up every two hours for the babies , and sometimes the monitor triggers the palpitations , or maybe it's the caffeine .
[doctor] the sleep disruption is certainly a trigger . let's cut back on caffeine after noon and keep the evening routine steady .
[patient] i'll try . the pot of coffee at work is the problem .
[doctor] i understand . let me listen to your heart . your rhythm is regular today , at seventy two . there's a soft click in the middle of the chest and a small late systolic murmur , which fits the mitral valve prolapse we saw on the echo .
[patient] is that serious ?
[doctor] it's common and usually mild . the echo showed only mild regurgitation , and your left ventricle is a normal size with normal pumping function .
[patient] okay . that's a relief .
[doctor] your blood pressure today is one eighteen over seventy four . your lungs are clear , and there's no swelling in your ankles .
[patient] good .
[doctor] your cholesterol panel from last month looks good , with an ldl of ninety six . your a one c is normal .
[patient] i was worried about my weight . i'm at one forty , and my husband says i should be at one thirty .
[doctor] a healthy weight is a reasonable goal to work on . the most important thing right now is the rhythm and the stroke prevention . our target for your blood pressure is under one thirty , based on the washington guidelines .
[patient] right . what about the ablation ? my coworker had one and she said it was life changing .
[doctor] that's an option for people with frequent symptomatic episodes despite medicine . we can refer you to our electrophysiologist for a discussion . given how infrequent your episodes are , i'd like to see the monitoring data first .
[patient] the monitoring is the patch thing ?
[doctor] yes . i'd like to order a seven day patch monitor to capture how often the rhythm happens during normal life and during your shifts . we'll decide about the ablation after that .
[patient] the patch won't get wet in the pool , right ?
[doctor] it's water resistant , but i'd ask you to skip the pool while it's on . take it off for showers .
[patient] okay . i'll tell the other nurses too .
[doctor] also , keep a symptom diary with the time , the activity , and how long each episode lasts . bring it to the next visit .
[patient] i'm good at lists . my husband will help with the times .
[doctor] perfect . if you get chest pain , fainting , or a racing heartbeat that doesn't settle within an hour , go to the emergency room . don't drive yourself .
[patient] i understand . thank you .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and mitral valve prolapse on anticoagulation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Yasmin Ortega is a 31-year-old female who presents for cardiology follow-up accompanied by her husband, who assists with medication management. She reports three episodes of palpitations since her last visit. The most recent occurred about two weeks ago during an intense night shift, with abrupt onset of rapid heartbeat and lightheadedness requiring her to sit down. The episode lasted approximately 40 minutes and resolved spontaneously. A wearable device recorded an irregular rhythm around 160 bpm without clear P waves, consistent with atrial fibrillation.

She works as a respiratory therapist at Riverbend Pharmacy, primarily in the emergency department on nights. She notes that stressful shifts and adrenaline may precipitate episodes. Her mother had a stroke at age 56.

She reports intermittent sleep disruption since adopting twin infants this spring, with waking every two hours, and wonders whether caffeine intake from work coffee contributes to palpitations. She swims at 5:45 each morning and restores vintage motorcycles in her garage on weekends. She cycled to clinic today.

She denies syncope or chest pain. She reports easy bruising on the shins from contact with the bed frame; she denies hematuria or melena.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

Nonrheumatic mitral valve prolapse with mild regurgitation on echocardiogram. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation diagnosed this year.

MEDICATIONS

Apixaban 5 mg by mouth twice daily. Metoprolol tartrate 50 mg twice daily, with fatigue in the afternoons and cold extremities. Caffeine, as above.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Vitals: BP 118/74, heart rate 72 and regular at the time of exam. Cardiac exam: midsystolic click with late systolic murmur at the apex. Lungs clear. No peripheral edema.

RESULTS

ECG today: sinus rhythm. Transthoracic echocardiogram from prior evaluation: mitral valve prolapse with mild regurgitation, normal left ventricular size and systolic function. Lipid panel: LDL 96 mg/dL. Hemoglobin A1c within normal limits. Weight 140 lb.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with symptomatic episodes, triggered by stress, sleep disruption, and caffeine. Continue apixaban 5 mg twice daily; adherence reviewed. Continue metoprolol. Seven-day patch monitor ordered to quantify burden. Electrophysiology referral if episodes remain frequent; catheter ablation discussed as an option.
2. Nonrheumatic mitral valve prolapse with mild regurgitation; surveillance echocardiogram per schedule.
3. Hypertension prevention: blood pressure target under 130/80 per the Washington guidelines; current 118/74 is at goal.
4. Lifestyle: limit caffeine after noon, maintain sleep routine, weight reduction goal discussed. Symptom diary to be kept with times, activity, and episode duration.
5. Return precautions reviewed: chest pain, syncope, or sustained palpitations lasting over one hour warrant emergency evaluation.

[doctor] good . any bleeding , bruising , or blood in the urine ?

[patient] good .

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , hamid . what happened to your nose ?
[patient] i took a fall during a pickup game on tuesday night . my nose hit the floor pretty hard , and it's been bleeding on and off since .
[doctor] okay . where were you playing ?
[patient] at saint mark's church gym on the east side . the floor was wet from somebody's water bottle , and i slipped going up for a rebound .
[doctor] any loss of consciousness or headache ?
[patient] no , i stayed up . i was dizzy for a minute . my brother bogdan drove me to urgent care .
[doctor] good . what did they do there ?
[patient] they took an x-ray and said to come see an ear nose and throat doctor . so here i am .
[doctor] okay . let's look . any trouble breathing through your nose ?
[patient] it's totally blocked . i ca n't breathe through either side .
[doctor] i'm going to look inside with a light . the nose is swollen and there's dried blood in both nostrils . the septum looks pushed to the left , and i see a small clot on the right side . there's no bulging of the wall , so it's not a septal hematoma . good .
[patient] that's good news , right ?
[doctor] yes . the x-ray shows a nasal bone fracture , which is what we expected . it's displaced a little to one side .
[patient] will i need surgery ?
[doctor] possibly , but we usually wait five to seven days until the swelling goes down , and then we can do a closed reduction in the office .
[patient] like putting it back in place ?
[doctor] exactly . we'd numb the inside of the nose and gently realign the bones . it's usually quick and not too bad .
[patient] okay . i'm a tow truck driver , so i need my breathing to be right .
[doctor] that's important . how do you manage the work with a blocked nose ?
[patient] i'm on the road a lot , and i sleep in the truck sometimes . the dust from the highway does n't help .
[doctor] let's make sure you avoid heavy lifting for two weeks , and use a saline spray . no blowing your nose for at least a week .
[patient] i sneeze and it's terrible . my wife says i'll have to keep a box of tissues in the truck .
[doctor] that's fine , just sneeze with your mouth open . ice packs for twenty minutes at a time in the first two days .
[patient] and no ibuprofen ? i usually take it for everything .
[doctor] ibuprofen is okay for pain , but it can increase bleeding , so acetaminophen is better for the first few days . how much bleeding is there today ?
[patient] just a little bit this morning . it's mostly stopped now .
[doctor] okay . your blood pressure is one twenty four over seventy , and your pulse is seventy eight . let me check your eyes too .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] your eyes are fine , with no bruising under them besides the swelling . no bruise behind the ears either . good .
[patient] my dad had bell's palsy years ago . he could not close one eye for months . i'm glad mine is fine .
[doctor] that's reassuring . your facial movement looks normal on both sides . i'll put your mrn mrn326718 on the referral for the ent surgeon .
[patient] thanks . do i need a tetanus shot ?
[doctor] your record shows your last tetanus booster was four years ago , so you're still up to date .
[patient] good . i'll come back in one week for the reduction .
[doctor] perfect . come back sooner if you have a fever , severe pain , bleeding that won't stop , or any changes in your vision .
[patient] got it . thank you , doctor .

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , rashad . i'm doctor hernandez , one of the physicians on tonight . the nurse said your heart doctor sent you over . how are you feeling ?
[patient] hi , doctor hernandez . honestly , i feel a little wobbly . my heart doctor said the monitor picked up something irregular and he wanted me checked out today .
[doctor] okay . tell me what you've been noticing .
[patient] it started about four days ago . i'd be sitting down after supper and my heart would start racing , like it was running a marathon without me . then i'd get lightheaded , like the room was tilting a little .
[doctor] how long do the episodes last ?
[patient] usually ten minutes , maybe fifteen . then it just stops on its own . last tuesday it happened twice in one afternoon , which is what scared me enough to call the office .
[doctor] did you pass out at any point , or come close to it ?
[patient] no , i never went all the way down . i grabbed the kitchen counter a couple of times though .
[doctor] any chest pain or pressure with it ?
[patient] no chest pain . i get a little short of breath while it's racing , but it eases off when the rhythm settles .
[doctor] okay . what are you taking for your heart right now ?
[patient] i take eliquis twice a day , and the lisinopril for blood pressure . they started the eliquis two years ago after the first irregular rhythm showed up . i also take metformin for my sugar .
[doctor] and how have the sugars been running ?
[patient] fasting around one twenty five , so not great . my fitbit says i'm sitting too much in the evenings , which i already know .
[doctor] are you active otherwise ?
[patient] oh , i'm pretty active , honestly . i restore vintage motorcycles in my garage , so i'm on my feet out there for hours most nights . and i swim at five forty five every morning , no matter what the weather is .
[doctor] that's impressive . and how are things at home ?
[patient] busy . we just adopted twins last spring , so the nights are short . my wife keeps saying i should slow down , and she's probably right .
[doctor] congratulations . okay , let's get an ekg and check your blood work . the nurse is putting you on the monitor now .
[patient] okay . the nurse already clipped something on my finger .
[doctor] good . let me listen to your heart and lungs . your heart is irregular right now , a little fast , maybe one ten . lungs sound clear . any leg swelling ?
[patient] no swelling . my ankles are fine .
[doctor] okay . your ekg shows an irregular rhythm without clear p waves , which fits with atrial fibrillation . your potassium and kidney numbers came back normal . i'm going to give you a dose of metoprolol to slow the rate , and we'll watch you on the monitor for a few hours .
[patient] will i need a cardioversion ?
[doctor] possibly , if it doesn't settle on its own or keeps coming back . let's see how the rate responds first .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] your blood pressure is one forty over eighty eight , a little high . keep taking the lisinopril . don't skip the eliquis , even on the days you feel fine .
[patient] i never skip it . i set an alarm on my phone .
[doctor] good . i want you to keep a log of when the racing happens , how long it lasts , and what you were doing before it started .
[patient] i can do that . i'm pretty organized with spreadsheets , actually .
[doctor] perfect . the nurse will write down the best number to reach you at , in case the results come back after you leave .
[patient] sure . it's on the form already .
[doctor] okay . we'll get you an appointment with the heart rhythm clinic within two weeks .
[patient] thank you , doctor hernandez . i was worried this was something serious .
[doctor] it's serious enough that we want to watch it closely , but you're doing the right things . let's see how you feel after the metoprolol .

[patient] hi , doctor donnelly . honestly , i feel a little wobbly . my heart doctor said the monitor picked up something irregular and he wanted me checked out today .
[doctor] okay . tell me what you've been noticing .
[patient] it started about four days ago . i'd be sitting down after supper and my heart would start racing , like it was running a marathon without me . then i'd get lightheaded , like the room was tilting a little .
[doctor] how long do the episodes last ?
[patient] usually ten minutes , maybe fifteen . then it just stops on its own . last tuesday it happened twice in one afternoon , which is what scared me enough to call the office .
[doctor] did you pass out at any point , or come close to it ?
[patient] no , i never went all the way down . i grabbed the kitchen counter a couple of times though .
[doctor] any chest pain or pressure with it ?
[patient] no chest pain . i get a little short of breath while it's racing , but it eases off when the rhythm settles .
[doctor] okay . what are you taking for your heart right now ?
[patient] i take eliquis twice a day , and the lisinopril for blood pressure . they started the eliquis two years ago after the first irregular rhythm showed up . i also take metformin for my sugar .
[doctor] and how have the sugars been running ?
[patient] fasting around one twenty five , so not great . my fitbit says i'm sitting too much in the evenings , which i already know .
[doctor] are you active otherwise ?
[patient] oh , i'm pretty active , honestly . i restore vintage motorcycles in my garage , so i'm on my feet out there for hours most nights . and i swim at five forty five every morning , no matter what the weather is .
[doctor] that's impressive . and how are things at home ?
[patient] busy . we just adopted twins last spring , so the nights are short . my wife keeps saying i should slow down , and she's probably right .
[doctor] congratulations . okay , let's get an ekg and check your blood work . the nurse is putting you on the monitor now .
[patient] okay . the nurse already clipped something on my finger .
[doctor] good . let me listen to your heart and lungs . your heart is irregular right now , a little fast , maybe one ten . lungs sound clear . any leg swelling ?
[patient] no swelling . my ankles are fine .
[doctor] okay . your ekg shows an irregular rhythm without clear p waves , which fits with atrial fibrillation . your potassium and kidney numbers came back normal . i'm going to give you a dose of metoprolol to slow the rate , and we'll watch you on the monitor for a few hours .
[patient] will i need a cardioversion ?
[doctor] possibly , if it doesn't settle on its own or keeps coming back . let's see how the rate responds first .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] your blood pressure is one forty over eighty eight , a little high . keep taking the lisinopril . don't skip the eliquis , even on the days you feel fine .
[patient] i never skip it . i set an alarm on my phone .
[doctor] good . i want you to keep a log of when the racing happens , how long it lasts , and what you were doing before it started .
[patient] i can do that . i'm pretty organized with spreadsheets , actually .
[doctor] perfect . the nurse will write down the best number to reach you at , in case the results come back after you leave .
[patient] sure . it's on the form already .
[doctor] okay . we'll get you an appointment with the heart rhythm clinic within two weeks .
[patient] thank you , doctor donnelly . i was worried this was something serious .
[doctor] it's serious enough that we want to watch it closely , but you're doing the right things . let's see how you feel after the metoprolol .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Palpitations and lightheadedness for four days.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Terrence Pemberton is a 60-year-old male with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on apixaban, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes who presents on referral from his cardiologist after a monitor picked up an irregular rhythm. He reports four days of palpitations at rest, with episodes lasting ten to fifteen minutes that resolve spontaneously. He had two episodes in one afternoon last Tuesday. He describes lightheadedness during the episodes and has steadied himself on the kitchen counter. He denies syncope and chest pain or pressure. He reports mild shortness of breath during the episodes that resolves when the rhythm settles. He denies orthopnea.

SOCIAL HISTORY

He is very active. He restores vintage motorcycles in his garage most evenings and swims at 5:45 every morning. He and his wife recently adopted twins. He tracks his activity with a fitness watch. Callback number: 206-924-3340.

MEDICATIONS

Apixaban twice daily, lisinopril, and metformin. Apixaban was started about two years ago after the first documented irregular rhythm.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Heart rate 110 and irregularly irregular. Blood pressure 140/88. Lungs are clear to auscultation. No lower extremity edema.

RESULTS

ECG shows atrial fibrillation without clear P waves. Potassium and creatinine are within normal limits. Fasting glucose approximately 125 per patient report.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Start metoprolol for rate control. Continue apixaban without interruption. Monitor on telemetry. Consider cardioversion if rhythm persists or recurs. Referral to heart rhythm clinic within two weeks.
2. Essential hypertension, borderline elevated today. Continue lisinopril.
3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Continue metformin.
4. Dizziness with arrhythmia, improving with rate control. Symptom log requested.

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , latoya . i'm doctor ashby . the nurse said it's been burning when you pee . how are you feeling ?
[patient] hi , doctor ashby . yes , since monday . it burns so much i was scared to go to the bathroom at work .
[doctor] where do you work ?
[patient] i'm at harvest moon diner , i do their payroll . i'm usually at my desk all day , which is why i ca n't stand the urge .
[doctor] okay . is anyone with you today ?
[patient] yes , wendy drove me over . she's in the waiting room with my bag .
[doctor] tell her hi from me . how far along are you now ?
[patient] twenty four weeks on tuesday . this is my second pregnancy , and my first one went totally smooth , so i was not expecting this .
[doctor] okay , that's helpful . any fever or chills ?
[patient] i had a low fever last night , maybe one hundred point two , and i got the chills around midnight . it passed by morning .
[doctor] any pain in your back or your side ?
[patient] a little ache in my lower back on the right . it's not bad though . i'd say it's a three out of ten at most .
[doctor] any vomiting , or trouble keeping fluids down ?
[patient] no vomiting . i'm just peeing every twenty minutes , which is the worst part .
[doctor] okay . any bleeding , or leaking of fluid ?
[patient] no bleeding . no leaking . the baby has been moving like crazy , which is probably the only good news .
[doctor] that's great to hear . how has your blood pressure been at your prenatal visits ?
[patient] it's been good , around one ten over seventy . my last appointment was normal , and the sugar test was fine too .
[doctor] good . any allergies to medicines ?
[patient] penicillin , when i was a kid . i got hives all over my arms .
[doctor] thank you . let's take a look at you . the nurse is going to get your urine sample and check your vitals .
[patient] okay . the nurse already took my blood pressure , i think it was one twelve over seventy four .
[doctor] okay . your temperature is ninety nine point eight , which is nearly normal . heart rate is ninety six . let me do the exam . does it hurt when i press here ?
[patient] yes , on the right side . a bit more than on the left .
[doctor] okay . no rebound tenderness . the fundal height matches your dates , and the baby's heart rate looks reassuring on the monitor .
[patient] that's a relief . is it an infection ?
[doctor] i think so . the urine dipstick shows white cells and nitrites , so it looks like a urinary tract infection . we'll send a culture to see which bacteria it is .
[patient] will it hurt the baby ?
[doctor] an infection that's left alone is more risky than one that's treated . that's why we're starting treatment today , without waiting for the culture .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] i'd like to start you on cephalexin five hundred milligrams twice a day for seven days . it's considered safe in pregnancy . finish the whole course , even if you feel better after two days .
[patient] okay . i'll stop at the pharmacy on the way home . the riverside pharmacy on dunmore road is closest to us .
[doctor] good , they'll have it ready . now , you mentioned a trip . where did you go recently ?
[patient] we drove down to the lake house in north carolina for a long weekend two weeks ago . i was fine there . it was the nine hour drive back that started the burning .
[doctor] okay . did you drink enough water on the trip ?
[patient] honestly , no . i was in the car forever and barely drank anything . i know , i know .
[doctor] that's very common . any history of kidney stones or urinary infections before ?
[patient] i had one in my twenties , when i was in college . i took the antibiotics for a week and it cleared right up .
[doctor] okay . any blood in your urine ?
[patient] no , it's just cloudy and it smells bad .
[doctor] alright . let me ask about the rest of your life for a minute , so i know what's going on . where did you grow up ?
[patient] durango . my parents are still there , which is why wendy is here so much . she's basically my second set of hands right now .
[doctor] that's wonderful . and you still work full time ?
[patient] yes , until the end of next month . then i'm going on leave . i'm excited and terrified about that .
[doctor] that's a normal feeling . how is your sleep these days ?
[patient] bad . i get up to pee three times a night and the baby kicks like a soccer player .
[doctor] i can imagine . any headaches , vision changes , or swelling in your face or hands ?
[patient] no headaches . my ankles are a little puffy by the end of the day , but that's been happening for a while .
[doctor] okay . we'll keep an eye on the blood pressure as well . i'd like you to check it at home twice a day this week .
[patient] i have a cuff at home , my husband bought it when we started trying .
[doctor] perfect . now , let's go over the plan again . we'll treat the infection , and i want you back in the clinic in two days to review the culture . go straight to labor and delivery if you have a fever over one hundred point five , vomiting , bleeding , or back pain that keeps getting worse .
[patient] got it . should i drink more water ?
[doctor] yes , aim for about ten cups a day , and empty your bladder every few hours . avoid caffeine for now , because it irritates the bladder .
[patient] i do like my morning coffee . that's going to be hard .
[doctor] i know . half a cup might be a reasonable compromise . the nurse will go over the rest of the instructions with you .
[patient] thank you . i'm also going to ask my church group to cover my choir practice this month , i can't stand for that long .
[doctor] that's a good idea . take care of yourself , and don't lift anything heavy .
[patient] okay . thank you , doctor ashby .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Dysuria and urinary frequency for four days.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Latoya Novak is a 31-year-old G2P1 female at 24 weeks' gestation who presents with dysuria, urinary frequency, and low-grade fever. Symptoms began on Monday, roughly two weeks after a long car trip to the lake house in north carolina. She reports a low-grade fever to 100.2 F last night with chills that resolved by morning. She reports a dull ache in the right lower back. She denies vomiting, nausea, vaginal bleeding, or leakage of fluid. She reports nocturia three times nightly. Fetal movement is active. She reports ankle swelling by evening, unchanged. She denies headache, visual changes, or gross hematuria. Urine is cloudy and malodorous. Prior history notable for a urinary tract infection in her twenties treated with a week of antibiotics. During the nine-hour drive she did not drink much fluid.

SOCIAL HISTORY

She works full time for Harvest Moon Diner, doing payroll, and plans to begin leave at the end of next month. She grew up in Durango, where her parents still live. Her mother, Wendy, accompanied her today and is helping at home. She drinks caffeinated coffee each morning.

ALLERGIES

Penicillin (urticaria).

PHYSICAL EXAM

Temperature 99.8 F. Heart rate 96. Blood pressure 112/74. Mild right costovertebral angle tenderness. Abdomen soft and nontender with no rebound tenderness. Fundal height consistent with dates. Fetal heart rate reassuring on monitoring. Mild ankle edema.

RESULTS

Urine dipstick positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Urine culture sent.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Urinary tract infection in pregnancy, second trimester, at 24 weeks' gestation. Start cephalexin 500 mg twice daily for 7 days. Follow up in 2 days to review culture.
2. Dysuria secondary to the infection. Increase oral fluids. Caffeine reduction counseled.
3. Home blood pressure monitoring twice daily this week. Preeclampsia precautions reviewed.
4. Return precautions reviewed: fever over 100.4 F, vomiting, bleeding, or worsening back pain should prompt presentation to labor and delivery.

The prescription will be filled at the riverside pharmacy on dunmore road.

Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Dysuria
24 weeks gestation of pregnancy

Dysuria and urinary frequency for four days.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Priya Mendoza is a 38-year-old G2P1 female at 24 weeks' gestation who presents with dysuria, urinary frequency, and low-grade fever. Symptoms began on Monday, roughly two weeks after a long car trip to the lake house in north carolina. She reports a low-grade fever to 100.2 F last night with chills that resolved by morning. She reports a dull ache in the right lower back. She denies vomiting, nausea, vaginal bleeding, or leakage of fluid. She reports nocturia three times nightly. Fetal movement is active. She reports ankle swelling by evening, unchanged. She denies headache, visual changes, or gross hematuria. Urine is cloudy and malodorous. Prior history notable for a urinary tract infection in her twenties treated with a week of antibiotics. During the nine-hour drive she did not drink much fluid.

SOCIAL HISTORY

She works full time for Lakeview Hospital, doing payroll, and plans to begin leave at the end of next month. She grew up in Fort Collins, where her parents still live. Her mother, Marisol, accompanied her today and is helping at home. She drinks caffeinated coffee each morning.

Penicillin (urticaria).

Temperature 99.8 F. Heart rate 96. Blood pressure 112/74. Mild right costovertebral angle tenderness. Abdomen soft and nontender with no rebound tenderness. Fundal height consistent with dates. Fetal heart rate reassuring on monitoring. Mild ankle edema.

RESULTS

Urine dipstick positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Urine culture sent.

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , tomas . i'm doctor weatherby . i see you're back with us again . how have you been since your last flare ?

[doctor] that makes sense . and the mesalamine ?
[patient] every morning , like clockwork . i'm pretty good about my pills . my wife sets them out in the little box every sunday night .
[doctor] that's helpful . are you taking the iron ?
[patient] the ferrous sulfate , yes . it turns my stool dark , which scared me the first time . i take it with orange juice like you said .
[doctor] good . how's your energy been ?
[patient] terrible . i'm tired all day . i was up at five for work and by two o'clock i'm falling asleep at my desk .
[doctor] where do you work now ?
[patient] i'm a dispatcher at dunmore public library . twelve hour shifts , some nights , which is hard on the stomach , honestly .
[doctor] i can imagine . any trouble with dizziness or getting short of breath ?
[patient] a little dizzy when i stand up fast . no chest pain . i get winded on the stairs , but that's been going on for a while .
[doctor] okay . let's look at you . the nurse will get your vitals and draw some blood .
[patient] okay . the nurse already has the cuff on my arm .
[doctor] good . your blood pressure is one twenty eight over seventy six . heart rate is ninety two . temperature is ninety eight point six . lie back for me . does your belly hurt when i press here ?
[patient] yes , right there , low on the right . it's sore .
[doctor] okay . there's some tenderness in the right lower quadrant , no rebound and no guarding . bowel sounds are active . let me check your legs for swelling .
[patient] no swelling , i don't think .
[doctor] your legs look fine . your skin is a little pale , which fits with the anemia . let's look at the labs . your hemoglobin is eleven point two , which is up from nine last spring , so the iron is helping .

[doctor] perfect . we'll talk again after the scan .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Recurrent right lower abdominal cramping with diarrhea for three weeks.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Tomas Brennan is a 52-year-old male with Crohn's disease, iron deficiency anemia, and long-term prednisone use who presents for follow-up of a flare. He reports three weeks of right lower quadrant cramping with four to five loose stools daily and intermittent blood in stool, small in volume. He reports night sweats and an unintentional six pound weight loss. He denies fever. Symptoms worsened after prednisone was tapered from 40 mg to 5 mg daily. He reports fatigue and orthostatic lightheadedness when standing quickly. He reports exertional dyspnea climbing stairs and denies chest pain.

SOCIAL HISTORY

He works as a dispatcher at Dunmore Public Library on twelve-hour shifts, including overnights. He lives with his wife, who helps manage his medication schedule. He rings handbells every Thursday night with a group of eleven people at Saint Mark Lutheran. He has a three-legged rescue dog at home.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

Crohn's disease diagnosed several years ago. Colonoscopy in March showed patchy inflammation in the terminal ileum. Iron deficiency anemia treated with ferrous sulfate.

ALLERGIES

Sulfa antibiotics (rash).

MEDICATIONS

Mesalamine daily. Prednisone 5 mg daily. Ferrous sulfate daily.

PHYSICAL EXAM

BP 128/76, HR 92, Temp 98.6 F. Skin pale. Abdomen with tenderness in the right lower quadrant without rebound or guarding. Bowel sounds active. No lower extremity edema.

RESULTS

Hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, up from 9.0 last spring. Elevated C-reactive protein and fecal calprotectin, consistent with active inflammation. CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast ordered to exclude abscess or obstruction.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Crohn's disease, active flare involving the terminal ileum. Obtain CT abdomen and pelvis. Discuss biologic therapy with gastroenterology to limit steroid exposure.
2. Iron deficiency anemia, improving on oral iron. Continue ferrous sulfate.
3. Long-term systemic steroid use. Taper plan to be revised by gastroenterology.
4. Orthostatic lightheadedness. Hydration encouraged.
5. Food diary requested for one week.

Iron deficiency anemia, unspecified
Long term (current) use of systemic steroids

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , thibodeaux . i'm doctor pemberton . your primary care office sent me your file . how can i help you today ?
[patient] hi , doctor pemberton . thanks for seeing me . my chest has been tight at work for about two months , and my inhaler is not doing much anymore .
[doctor] okay . tell me about the tightness . when does it come on ?
[patient] usually a couple hours into the shift . i spray foam insulation for coastal wind energy , mostly in crawl spaces . by the afternoon i'm wheezing and coughing and i have to step outside .
[doctor] and when you're away from work , how is your breathing ?
[patient] much better . weekends are fine . my chest feels normal by monday morning , then it starts again on tuesday .
[doctor] that pattern is important . what chemicals do you work with ?
[patient] the foam is a two part thing , the isocyanate side and the polyol side . we mix them in the gun . the safety sheets say you need a respirator with organic vapor cartridges .
[doctor] do you wear one ?
[patient] most days . honestly , not every day . in the summer the crawl spaces get so hot i take it off when the boss is not looking .
[doctor] that's understandable , but it's dangerous . what inhaler are you using ?
[patient] albuterol , the rescue one . i use it about five times a week now . it used to be about once a month .
[doctor] okay . any cough at night ?
[patient] sometimes , yes . i wake up a few times a month with my chest tight .
[doctor] have you ever had asthma diagnosed ?
[patient] not that i remember . i had bronchitis a couple of times as a kid , and my mom was always treating my wheezing with a steam tent .
[doctor] okay . any other medical problems ?
[patient] no , i'm pretty healthy . i run on weekends with my dog . but i do get a runny nose at work , and my eyes get itchy .
[doctor] any smoking ?
[patient] i quit three years ago . i smoked about a pack a day for ten years before that .
[doctor] okay . and alcohol ?
[patient] a beer or two on friday . nothing more .
[doctor] any family history of asthma or allergies ?
[patient] my brother has asthma . my dad had hay fever .
[doctor] okay . let me examine you . breathe in for me . your lungs have some wheezing on the right side when you breathe out . the rest sounds clear .
[patient] that's the same thing i hear at work .
[doctor] your oxygen is ninety six percent on room air , and your peak flow is about seventy percent of your predicted value . that is lower than i'd like .
[patient] what does that mean ?
[doctor] it means your airways narrow when you're exposed to something . the pattern fits with work related asthma from the isocyanates .
[patient] so it's the foam .
[doctor] it's very likely part of it . we'll do a spirometry test today to measure how much air you can move out . and i'd like a chest x-ray to rule out other problems .
[patient] okay . my coworker farah has the same cough , and his wife says he wakes up at night too .
[doctor] that's worth telling him to see someone . the nurse will set you up for the breathing test now .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] while we wait , the guidelines say a cholesterol check should start at age thirty five for men , so that's a good time to check yours .
[patient] i'm 33 , so i guess i'm due for that .
[doctor] and pneumonia vaccines become a bigger deal over the age of sixty five , but that's far off for you .
[patient] good . i'm far from that .
[doctor] here's what i recommend . first , the most important thing is less exposure . can you talk to your supervisor about a different job for a few weeks , or at least use supplied air every shift ?
[patient] i can try . he's pretty set on production , though .
[doctor] i'll write a letter to your employer recommending a temporary change in your duties . i'd also like you to start a low dose inhaled steroid , twice a day , every day .
[patient] okay . and the albuterol ?
[doctor] keep it for rescue . if you need it more than twice a week , or if you wake up at night with it , call us .
[patient] got it .
[doctor] i'm also going to refer you to the occupational health clinic on hillcrest avenue . they can look at your workplace and your respirator fit .
[patient] that's close to where my sister works . she's a nurse there , actually .
[doctor] good , then you'll have someone to ask . where did you grow up ?
[patient] spokane . my family is still there , and i go back for christmas every year . the drive is brutal but worth it .
[doctor] okay . let's see you in four weeks with repeat peak flow and spirometry . sooner if the wheezing gets worse .
[patient] thank you , doctor pemberton . i was worried this was going to be a big deal .
[doctor] it's a serious problem , but it's very treatable when we catch it early and reduce the exposure .
