dialogue:
[doctor] hi , mei . i'm doctor xiong . your family doctor sent you over about some bleeding . how are you doing today ?
[patient] hi , doctor xiong . i'm all right , i suppose . i'm eighty one and i wasn't expecting any bleeding at my age .
[doctor] i understand . tell me what you've noticed .
[patient] a little spotting , like pink on the toilet paper . it started about three weeks ago . then last week it was a bit more , maybe the size of a quarter on my underwear .
[doctor] okay . when was your last period ?
[patient] goodness . i've been past that for almost twenty years . i went through the change at about fifty one .
[doctor] okay . are you taking any hormones ?
[patient] no , not for years . i stopped the estrogen cream when i was about sixty five , because it made my breasts sore .
[doctor] that's helpful . any pain in your belly or pelvis ?
[patient] not really . i have a heavy , dragging feeling down there sometimes , like something is sitting low . especially when i've been on my feet all morning .
[doctor] okay . does it bother you when you pass urine or have a bowel movement ?
[patient] sometimes i have to push a little to empty out . and i leak a bit when i sneeze . nothing too terrible .
[doctor] any blood in your urine , or burning ?
[patient] no burning . no blood that i can see .
[doctor] okay . let's go over your other health . what medicines are you taking ?
[patient] amlodipine every morning , five milligrams for my blood pressure , and atorvastatin at night for my cholesterol . and a baby aspirin , eighty one milligrams . my son says i'm a walking pharmacy .
[doctor] that's a good list . any allergies ?
[patient] penicillin makes me break out . that's the only one .
[doctor] okay . any blood thinners besides the aspirin ?
[patient] no . just the aspirin , for my heart .
[doctor] good . let's talk about you . where do you live now ?
[patient] alone in the house i've had since nineteen seventy eight . my daughter hector calls every single day , she worries about me .
[doctor] that's lovely . what do you do with your days ?
[patient] i keep bees in the back yard , about six hives . i still do that every spring , even though my knees are not what they were .
[doctor] wow . and any stings ?
[patient] oh , plenty . i'm used to it .
[doctor] okay . were you ever in the service ?
[patient] yes , i was a navy veteran . i served on a destroyer for four years , from nineteen sixty one .
[doctor] thank you for your service . let's examine you . the nurse is going to check your blood pressure first .
[patient] okay . the nurse is very gentle .
[doctor] your blood pressure is one thirty eight over seventy six , which is pretty good for your age . heart rate is seventy four . let me look at your belly first .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] your abdomen is soft , no tenderness . now i'm going to do a pelvic exam . take a deep breath and bear down for me .
[patient] okay . oh , there it is , that bulge .
[doctor] i see it . there's a cystocele , the bladder is dropping into the front wall of the vagina . the cervix is small and looks normal . there's a little bit of pinkish blood at the opening .
[patient] that's what i saw this morning .
[doctor] okay . we'll do a transvaginal ultrasound to measure the lining of the uterus , and i'd like to take a small sample of the lining in the office today .
[patient] does that hurt ?
[doctor] it's a quick pinch , maybe ten seconds of discomfort . i'll give you a moment after .
[patient] okay . please go slow .
[doctor] i will . the hemoglobin from the blood drawn earlier was twelve point one , which is fine . your kidney numbers are normal , and your cholesterol is a little high on the atorvastatin , so we'll recheck it .
[patient] okay . what about the bulge ?
[doctor] for the bulge we can try a pessary , a small device that fits inside the vagina and holds things up . many women find it very comfortable .
[patient] i don't want surgery . i'm too old for that kind of thing .
[doctor] i agree , a pessary is a good first step . let's get the ultrasound and the biopsy results first .
[patient] okay . how long until i hear back ?
[doctor] the biopsy usually takes about a week . i'll call you myself with the results , and the nurse will set up the ultrasound for next week .
[patient] good . my daughter wants to come with me to the next visit .
[doctor] that's fine . please ask her to bring your medication list .
[patient] she'll love that . she likes to keep track of everything .
[doctor] one more thing . if the bleeding gets heavier , or you have clots or dizziness , call us right away . don't wait for next week .
[patient] i will . thank you , doctor xiong .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Postmenopausal spotting for three weeks.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mei Ueda is a 88-year-old female, postmenopausal since age 51, referred by her family physician for evaluation of postmenopausal vaginal bleeding. She reports spotting for approximately three weeks, with a larger episode last week about the size of a quarter. She discontinued vaginal estrogen cream around age 65 because of breast tenderness and has not used hormone therapy since. She reports pelvic heaviness and dragging, worse after prolonged standing, with incomplete emptying requiring straining and leakage with sneezing. She denies dysuria, hematuria, or abdominal pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

Hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both controlled on medication.

MEDICATIONS

Amlodipine 5 mg daily. Atorvastatin nightly. Aspirin 81 mg daily.

ALLERGIES

Penicillin (rash).

SOCIAL HISTORY

Lives alone in the same home since 1978. Daughter, Hector, calls daily and will accompany her to future visits. She keeps bees in her backyard, approximately six hives, and is a navy veteran who served on a destroyer from 1961 for four years.

PHYSICAL EXAM

BP 138/76. HR 74. Abdomen soft and nontender. Pelvic examination with grade 2 anterior vaginal wall prolapse consistent with cystocele. Cervix small and unremarkable. Small amount of blood at the introitus.

RESULTS

Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL. Renal function within normal limits. LDL elevated on current statin therapy; repeat lipid panel planned.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Postmenopausal bleeding, evaluate for endometrial pathology. Transvaginal ultrasound to measure endometrial thickness. Office endometrial biopsy today.
2. Cystocele with stress urinary incontinence symptoms. Trial of pessary; surgery deferred per patient preference.
3. Essential hypertension, controlled on amlodipine.
4. Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin, recheck lipids.
5. Aspirin for cardiovascular prevention; no other anticoagulants.

Return precautions reviewed: heavy bleeding, clots, or dizziness.

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , thuy . i'm doctor haddad . your family doctor sent you over about some bleeding . how are you doing today ?
[patient] hi , doctor haddad . i'm all right , i suppose . i'm eighty one and i wasn't expecting any bleeding at my age .
[doctor] i understand . tell me what you've noticed .
[patient] a little spotting , like pink on the toilet paper . it started about three weeks ago . then last week it was a bit more , maybe the size of a quarter on my underwear .
[doctor] okay . when was your last period ?
[patient] goodness . i've been past that for almost twenty years . i went through the change at about fifty one .
[doctor] okay . are you taking any hormones ?
[patient] no , not for years . i stopped the estrogen cream when i was about sixty five , because it made my breasts sore .
[doctor] that's helpful . any pain in your belly or pelvis ?
[patient] not really . i have a heavy , dragging feeling down there sometimes , like something is sitting low . especially when i've been on my feet all morning .
[doctor] okay . does it bother you when you pass urine or have a bowel movement ?
[patient] sometimes i have to push a little to empty out . and i leak a bit when i sneeze . nothing too terrible .
[doctor] any blood in your urine , or burning ?
[patient] no burning . no blood that i can see .
[doctor] okay . let's go over your other health . what medicines are you taking ?
[patient] amlodipine every morning , five milligrams for my blood pressure , and atorvastatin at night for my cholesterol . and a baby aspirin , eighty one milligrams . my son says i'm a walking pharmacy .
[doctor] that's a good list . any allergies ?
[patient] penicillin makes me break out . that's the only one .
[doctor] okay . any blood thinners besides the aspirin ?
[patient] no . just the aspirin , for my heart .
[doctor] good . let's talk about you . where do you live now ?
[patient] alone in the house i've had since nineteen seventy eight . my daughter santiago calls every single day , she worries about me .
[doctor] that's lovely . what do you do with your days ?
[patient] i keep bees in the back yard , about six hives . i still do that every spring , even though my knees are not what they were .
[doctor] wow . and any stings ?
[patient] oh , plenty . i'm used to it .
[doctor] okay . were you ever in the service ?
[patient] yes , i was a navy veteran . i served on a destroyer for four years , from nineteen sixty one .
[doctor] thank you for your service . let's examine you . the nurse is going to check your blood pressure first .
[patient] okay . the nurse is very gentle .
[doctor] your blood pressure is one thirty eight over seventy six , which is pretty good for your age . heart rate is seventy four . let me look at your belly first .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] your abdomen is soft , no tenderness . now i'm going to do a pelvic exam . take a deep breath and bear down for me .
[patient] okay . oh , there it is , that bulge .
[doctor] i see it . there's a cystocele , the bladder is dropping into the front wall of the vagina . the cervix is small and looks normal . there's a little bit of pinkish blood at the opening .
[patient] that's what i saw this morning .
[doctor] okay . we'll do a transvaginal ultrasound to measure the lining of the uterus , and i'd like to take a small sample of the lining in the office today .
[patient] does that hurt ?
[doctor] it's a quick pinch , maybe ten seconds of discomfort . i'll give you a moment after .
[patient] okay . please go slow .
[doctor] i will . the hemoglobin from the blood drawn earlier was twelve point one , which is fine . your kidney numbers are normal , and your cholesterol is a little high on the atorvastatin , so we'll recheck it .
[patient] okay . what about the bulge ?

[patient] i don't want surgery . i'm too old for that kind of thing .
[doctor] i agree , a pessary is a good first step . let's get the ultrasound and the biopsy results first .
[patient] okay . how long until i hear back ?

[doctor] that's fine . please ask her to bring your medication list .
[patient] she'll love that . she likes to keep track of everything .

[patient] i will . thank you , doctor haddad .

Annual physical examination; chronic low back pain and anxiety symptoms.

SOCIAL HISTORY

MEDICATIONS

Acetaminophen as needed, heating pad. No prescription medications.

PHYSICAL EXAM

BP 111/72. HR 76. Weight stable. Lumbar paraspinal tenderness without midline spinal tenderness. Straight leg raise negative bilaterally. Strength and reflexes normal and symmetric.

RESULTS

No laboratory studies today. Vaccine record reviewed.

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , hannah . i'm doctor zielinski . how are you feeling two weeks after your hernia repair ?
[patient] hi , doctor zielinski . mostly good , but there's something new that worried me this morning .
[doctor] tell me about it .
[patient] there's a lump under the incision , kind of soft and squishy , and it hurts when i bend or cough . it wasn't there last tuesday .
[doctor] okay . is the skin red or warm over it ?
[patient] a little pink , but not hot . the stitches look fine , i think .
[doctor] any drainage from the incision ?
[patient] a little clear fluid on the bandage yesterday . no pus , no smell .
[doctor] any fever or chills ?
[patient] no fever . i took my temperature twice . it was ninety eight point four both times .
[doctor] good . are you able to eat and move your bowels ?
[patient] eating fine . bowels are a bit slow , but i'm passing gas . i had a normal bowel movement on sunday .
[doctor] that's reassuring . any nausea or vomiting ?
[patient] no vomiting . i feel a little queasy when i take the pain pills , though .
[doctor] what are you taking for pain ?
[patient] tylenol during the day , and one of the oxycodone tablets at night if i need it . i'm trying to use fewer every day .
[doctor] good . how many did you take last night ?
[patient] just one , around ten . i slept okay after that .
[doctor] okay . let's go over your history . you had the hernia repair two weeks ago , and you have high blood pressure , right ?
[patient] yes , i take the amlodipine every morning . my blood pressure has been running about one thirty over eighty .
[doctor] okay . when did you first notice the hernia ?
[patient] about two years ago , when i was lifting my grandson . i felt a bulge in the middle of my stomach . it got bigger over the months .
[doctor] i see . and before the surgery , were you able to do your hobbies ?
[patient] i grow ghost peppers in my greenhouse , and i play mandolin in a bluegrass band on tuesday nights . the bulge made it hard to hold the instrument .
[doctor] that sounds lovely . has the greenhouse been too much for you lately ?
[patient] not much , my husband has been doing the watering . i'm supposed to keep the lifting down .
[doctor] right . where did you grow up ?
[patient] lafayette . my family still lives there , and we went to iceland last summer for my sister's birthday . the waterfalls were something else .
[doctor] that's wonderful . okay , let me look at you . the nurse is going to take your vitals first .
[patient] okay . the nurse has a nice cuff , it doesn't pinch .
[doctor] your blood pressure is one twenty eight over seventy eight , and your temperature is ninety eight point four . heart rate is eighty . let me look at the incision .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] the incision is healing well . there's a soft fluid collection under the skin , about the size of a walnut . there's no spreading redness , and the skin is not tender to touch .
[patient] it's tender when you press in the middle .
[doctor] i see that . that fluid is likely a seroma , which is a collection of normal fluid after surgery . it usually goes away on its own over a few weeks .
[patient] so nothing needs to be cut open ?
[doctor] right . we'll watch it . if it gets bigger , hurts more , or starts to drain pus , we'd need to drain it in the office .
[patient] okay . and no more heavy lifting , i promise .
[doctor] good . i'd like you to see us again in one week to recheck the size . we'll also get a basic blood count today to make sure there's no infection .
[patient] okay . what about the pain pills ?
[doctor] keep using the tylenol as the first choice . cut back on the oxycodone , and stop it entirely if you can . no driving while you take it .
[patient] i don't drive at night anyway , so that's easy .
[doctor] good . and keep wearing the binder for the next two weeks .
[patient] the binder is so hot in the summer . but fine .
[doctor] i know . thank you for coming in . call us if you develop fever over one hundred one , more drainage , or redness spreading beyond the incision .
[patient] i will . thanks , doctor zielinski .

Hypertension, controlled on amlodipine.

Return precautions: fever >101 F, increasing drainage, or spreading redness.

[doctor] any drainage from the incision ?
[patient] a little clear fluid on the bandage yesterday . no pus , no smell .
[doctor] any fever or chills ?
[patient] no fever . i took my temperature twice . it was ninety eight point four both times .
[doctor] good . are you able to eat and move your bowels ?
[patient] eating fine . bowels are a bit slow , but i'm passing gas . i had a normal bowel movement on sunday .
[doctor] that's reassuring . any nausea or vomiting ?
[patient] no vomiting . i feel a little queasy when i take the pain pills , though .
[doctor] what are you taking for pain ?
[patient] tylenol during the day , and one of the oxycodone tablets at night if i need it . i'm trying to use fewer every day .
[doctor] good . how many did you take last night ?
[patient] just one , around ten . i slept okay after that .
[doctor] okay . let's go over your history . you had the hernia repair two weeks ago , and you have high blood pressure , right ?
[patient] yes , i take the amlodipine every morning . my blood pressure has been running about one thirty over eighty .
[doctor] okay . when did you first notice the hernia ?
[patient] about two years ago , when i was lifting my grandson . i felt a bulge in the middle of my stomach . it got bigger over the months .
[doctor] i see . and before the surgery , were you able to do your hobbies ?
[patient] i grow ghost peppers in my greenhouse , and i play mandolin in a bluegrass band on tuesday nights . the bulge made it hard to hold the instrument .

[doctor] right . where did you grow up ?

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , denise . i'm doctor ramirez . it's been three weeks since your bunion surgery . how's the foot doing ?
[patient] hi , doctor ramirez . much better than i expected , honestly . the throbbing has calmed down a lot .
[doctor] good . let me see the dressing in a moment . tell me how you've been managing the pain .
[patient] i take the tylenol in the morning and at night , and i ice it when i can . i'm a seven out of ten in the morning and maybe a three by evening .
[doctor] okay . are you still using the walking boot ?
[patient] yes , i wear the boot whenever i'm up . i've been sneaking off it to get my mail , i admit that .
[doctor] i'd like you to keep it on for two more weeks . what's your daily activity like ?
[patient] i work part time as a hairdresser , so i'm on my feet a lot . i sit on a stool when i can , and my assistant has been covering the heavy stuff .
[doctor] good . and how is your diabetes doing ? i know your sugars have been higher since the surgery .
[patient] they've been a little high , around one eighty fasting . i'm eating a bit more carbs than i should because i'm not walking as much .
[doctor] that's understandable . keep an eye on your numbers and let me know if they stay high . are you still on metformin ?
[patient] yes , metformin twice a day . i also have a glucose meter , my brother bought it for me when i was diagnosed in 2021 .
[doctor] okay . let's look at the foot now . the nurse is going to take the dressing down .
[patient] okay . the nurse is very gentle , thank you .
[doctor] the incision looks good . there's no redness spreading , no drainage , and the sutures are intact . the swelling is going down .
[patient] it's still puffy at the end of the day .
[doctor] that's normal . let me check the circulation . your pulses are palpable and the toes are warm . can you wiggle your toes ?
[patient] yes , i can move them . the big toe is a bit stiff .
[doctor] okay . there's mild tenderness along the incision , which is expected . no signs of infection .
[patient] good . when can i go back to the gym ?
[doctor] not for another six weeks . the treadmill is out until the bone heals . the calf stretches are great though , keep doing them .
[patient] okay . i've been doing the calf stretch every morning , and my achilles tendon still feels tight .
[doctor] that's normal after time in the boot . keep doing it twice a day .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] let's review the x-ray from 03/14/2021 . the bone is lined up nicely , and the screws are holding well . i'm happy with the alignment .
[patient] good . the surgery was on march fourteenth , right ? i still can't believe it's been that long .
[doctor] yes , it was march fourteenth . your bone should be healing well by now .
[patient] okay . i was worried about the x-ray .
[doctor] the x-ray looks good . let's plan the next visit . i'd like to see you again in two weeks , and we'll remove the sutures then .
[patient] wait , the sutures are still in ?
[doctor] yes . the inside stitches dissolve on their own , but the outside ones come out at the two week visit . the nurse will show you how to care for the dressing at home .
[patient] okay . i pick up my prescriptions at wildcat youth soccer on tarrant street , by the way . can they refill the cephalexin when the course runs out ?
[doctor] yes , just call them . the course is seven days , and you should finish it .
[patient] i'll finish it . i'm very good at finishing things .
[doctor] good . any numbness in your toes , or any trouble with your balance ?
[patient] no numbness , i'm just a little clumsy with the boot .
[doctor] okay . the boot is for protection , so take it slow . make sure you're not standing for hours at a time .
[patient] i'll try . thank you , doctor ramirez .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Postoperative follow-up three weeks after right first metatarsal osteotomy for hallux valgus.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Thuy Zhang is a 48-year-old female who presents for postoperative follow-up. Surgery was performed on September Ninth. Pain has improved, rated 7/10 in the morning and 3/10 by evening. She takes acetaminophen twice daily and applies ice. She has been partially non-adherent to the postoperative walking boot. She reports morning stiffness of the great toe. She denies fever, calf pain, or new numbness.

She works part time as a hairdresser and spends much of the day on her feet.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

Type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed in 2019, managed with metformin. Fasting glucose reported around 180 mg/dL since surgery.

MEDICATIONS

Metformin twice daily. Acetaminophen as needed. Cephalexin 500 mg, seven-day course, started at surgery.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Picks up prescriptions at Allied Waste Services on Tarrant Street.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Incision healing with no erythema beyond the margins and no drainage. Sutures intact. Mild swelling. DP and PT pulses palpable bilaterally. Capillary refill brisk. Hallux with mild stiffness at the MTP joint. Mild tenderness along incision.

RESULTS

Radiographs of the right foot taken on 08/09/2019 show the first metatarsal osteotomy in good alignment, with screw fixation intact and early callus formation.

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , siobhan . i'm doctor nguyen . the nurse said you've been gaining weight and your ankles are swollen . how are you feeling today ?
[patient] hi , doctor nguyen . honestly , i'm not doing so well . i feel heavy all over , and my shoes don't fit anymore .
[doctor] tell me about the weight . how much have you gained ?
[patient] about six pounds in the last five days . i weigh myself every morning on the bathroom scale right after i go to the bathroom .
[doctor] good habit . what was your weight at your last visit ?
[patient] at my last visit on february fifth i was about one fifty four . so i'm back up near one sixty .
[doctor] okay . any shortness of breath ?
[patient] when i climb the stairs to my bedroom , yes . i stop at the landing and catch my breath . i used to do the whole thing without thinking .
[doctor] do you need extra pillows to sleep ?
[patient] two pillows , yes . and i wake up coughing a few nights a week .
[doctor] okay . any chest pain or fainting ?
[patient] no chest pain . no fainting . just tired .
[doctor] are you taking your water pill ?
[patient] the furosemide , forty milligrams in the morning . i took it this morning . and the carvedilol twice a day , and my blood pressure pill , the lisinopril .
[doctor] have you missed any doses this week ?
[patient] i missed one furosemide on tuesday , because i was at my sister's house and didn't want to be up all night going to the bathroom . that was a mistake , i know .
[doctor] that's understandable , but please take it on schedule even when you travel . how much salt are you eating ?
[patient] i try to watch it . i cook most of my meals , but my son brings over the frozen pizzas on sundays .
[doctor] that's the salt . any alcohol or fluids ?
[patient] a glass of wine with supper , and i drink about eight cups of water a day .
[doctor] okay . let's check you over . the nurse will take your vitals and weigh you on our scale .
[patient] okay . the nurse has cold hands , i'll tell you that .
[doctor] your blood pressure is one forty over eighty eight . heart rate is ninety six and a little irregular . oxygen is ninety one percent on room air . let me listen to your chest .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] i hear crackles at the bases of both lungs , and your neck veins are a bit distended . your ankles have pitting edema , about two plus . your abdomen is soft .
[patient] that matches how i feel .
[doctor] your weight on our scale is one fifty nine point four pounds . that's up about five pounds since your last visit .
[patient] that's close to my home number .
[doctor] your labs from this morning are back . your potassium is a little low at three point three , and your kidney function is stable . the heart ultrasound from 2024 showed an ejection fraction of about thirty five percent .
[patient] i remember that . they said my heart pumps weaker than it should .
[doctor] right . so your heart failure is flaring up from the extra fluid . we need to give you more diuretic and watch your potassium .
[patient] okay . should i double the furosemide ?
[doctor] for three days , yes , forty milligrams twice a day , then back to the usual dose . and add potassium chloride ten milliequivalents daily while we're on the extra dose .
[patient] okay . will i need to come back ?
[doctor] yes , i want you back in the clinic within three days to recheck your weight and your potassium . if you feel worse before then , go to the emergency room .
[patient] okay . i'll call my son to drive me . he's the one who takes me to everything .
[doctor] good . we also want to talk about how you're keeping busy . what do you do for fun ?
[patient] i raise rare heritage chickens and sell the eggs at the farmers' market . i'm one of nine children , so we always had a full house growing up .
[doctor] that's wonderful . have you been able to do the market lately ?
[patient] not since the spring . i can't stand for hours with the fluid in my legs . my daughter handles the stall now .
[doctor] that makes sense . when you feel up to it , the chickens will still be there .
[patient] they're my reason to get up in the morning .
[doctor] i'm glad to hear that . we'll repeat the heart ultrasound in three months .
[patient] three months is a long time from now .
[doctor] it is . that's why i want to see you in three days . and i'd like you to take your blood pressure at home each morning , and bring the log .
[patient] i can do that . i have the cuff in the closet .
[doctor] perfect . any questions for me ?
[patient] just one . is the salt the main reason this happened ?
[doctor] it's a big part of it . missed doses and the salt together , yes . don't blame yourself , just tighten things up .
[patient] okay . thank you , doctor nguyen .

Weight gain, lower extremity edema, and exertional dyspnea.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction diagnosed in 2024, with ejection fraction about 35 percent on echocardiogram. Hypertension.

MEDICATIONS

Furosemide 40 mg each morning. Carvedilol twice daily. Lisinopril daily.

PHYSICAL EXAM

BP 140/88. HR 96, irregular. SpO2 91% on room air. Bibasilar crackles. Jugular venous distension mild. 2+ pitting edema bilateral lower extremities. Abdomen soft.

4. Return to the emergency department for dyspnea at rest, chest pain, or syncope.

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , yasmin . i'm doctor sorensen . good to see you at thirty weeks . i see you brought someone with you today .
[patient] hi , doctor sorensen . yes , this is my husband , felix . he took the afternoon off so he could come to the ultrasound .
[patient] hi , doctor sorensen . nice to meet you . i'm the one who keeps asking her questions in the car .
[doctor] that's exactly what we like to hear . so how are you feeling ?
[patient] tired , honestly . i've had a headache on and off for about four days . it's a dull one behind my eyes , and tylenol takes the edge off .
[doctor] okay . is it worse in the mornings , or when you bend over ?
[patient] mostly in the evening , after a long shift . i drive a city bus on the night shift , so i'm up and down the steps all night .
[doctor] that's a demanding job at this stage . any vision changes , like spots or blurry vision ?
[patient] no spots . once i saw a little flicker when i stood up too fast , but it passed .
[doctor] okay . any pain under your right ribs ?
[patient] no , nothing there . my feet are puffier than usual by the end of a shift , though . my wedding ring was tight this week .
[doctor] that's common , but i want to check it . let's go through your home readings . what's your blood pressure been ?
[patient] i check it at home every morning before my shift , with the cuff my sister lent me . it's been about one thirty eight over eighty eight most days .
[doctor] okay . and your blood sugars ?
[patient] i wear a dexcom on my arm . fasting has been around ninety six , and about an hour after lunch it climbs to one fifty , sometimes one sixty .
[doctor] that's a little high after meals . how are you managing your food ?
[patient] i've cut back on rice and bread . i eat more eggs and vegetables . the hard part is the night shift , i end up grabbing whatever's in the depot vending machine .
[patient] yes , i'm the one who packs the lunches now . she drives a city bus on the night shift , and she's been very good about it , but the vending machine is a problem .
[doctor] okay . we'll look at options . are you taking your medicines every day ?
[patient] yes . the labetalol twice a day , and the baby aspirin , and the prenatal vitamins . i set alarms on the phone for all three .
[doctor] that's good . and the metformin ? i don't see it on the list you brought .
[patient] no metformin . the doctor said my numbers were fine with diet alone , which is why i'm so careful about the food part .
[doctor] right , diet controlled . let's check your blood pressure and the baby now . the nurse will take your vitals .
[patient] okay . the nurse did my last blood test in the spring , and she was very gentle .
[doctor] your blood pressure is one forty two over ninety on this arm , which is higher than i'd like . heart rate is eighty four . temperature is ninety eight point six . let me check your weight and your belly .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] your weight is up about one pound this week . fundal height is thirty centimeters , which matches your dates . the baby's heart rate is one forty eight on the monitor , which is reassuring .
[patient] that's the one i wanted to hear .
[doctor] your urine dipstick shows a trace of protein . that's something we need to keep an eye on . your reflexes are a little brisk , but there's no clonus .
[patient] what does a trace mean ?
[doctor] it means a small amount of protein in the urine , which can happen with high blood pressure in pregnancy . it doesn't tell us the whole story , so we'll send blood work today .
[patient] okay . will i need to go to the hospital ?
[doctor] not today . the blood work will check your platelets , your liver tests , and your kidney function . if the numbers look fine , you can go home .
[patient] okay . felix , can you write this down , please ?
[patient] i'm writing it down . blood work , trace protein , labetalol still the same .
[doctor] good , thank you . i'd like to increase the labetalol from one hundred to two hundred milligrams twice a day . the lower dose has not been enough .
[patient] okay . two hundred . and the dizziness when i stand , is that from the labetalol ?
[doctor] possibly . stand up slowly , and sit down if you feel lightheaded . and don't drive the bus when you feel dizzy .
[patient] i'd have to call in sick . that's my main worry , the bills .
[doctor] i understand . we can write a note for your supervisor . where is the depot ? is it near your neighborhood ?
[patient] it's over on indian river lagoon , by the river . so it's about ten minutes from our house in knoxville .
[doctor] okay . let's plan the next steps . i'd like an ultrasound in three weeks to check the baby's growth , and weekly visits starting at thirty six weeks .
[patient] okay . we're going to cape cod in two weeks for a family wedding . is that okay ?
[doctor] short trips are fine . just keep up with the blood pressure checks , bring your home log , and take the labetalol with you .
[patient] of course . we're driving up , and i'll pack a cooler with fresh fruit and the rest of the food .
[doctor] perfect . if you have a bad headache that doesn't go away with rest , vision changes , belly pain under the ribs , or shortness of breath , call labor and delivery right away .
[patient] got it . my sister has the number for the birth center on speed dial .
[doctor] good . and kick counts every day . if the baby moves less than ten times in two hours , come in .
[patient] i do the kick counts while i'm on break . the baby is very active at night .
[doctor] that's reassuring . do you have any questions for me today ?
[patient] just one . is the dexcom reading going to be accurate after the blood work ? the sensor is due for a change .
[doctor] yes , it's fine . change the sensor on schedule , and bring the readings to the next visit . we'll review them together .
[patient] thank you . this has been a lot , but it helps to know what to watch for .
[doctor] you're doing a great job . take care of yourself , and see you in one week .
[patient] thank you , doctor sorensen .

Routine follow-up at 30 weeks for chronic hypertension and diet-controlled gestational diabetes, with intermittent headache.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Yasmin Salazar is a 43-year-old G2P1 female at 30 weeks of gestation with pre-existing essential hypertension on labetalol and diet-controlled gestational diabetes. Accompanied today by her husband, Felix. She reports an intermittent dull frontal headache for approximately four days, mostly in the evening after shifts, partially relieved by acetaminophen. She denies scotomata or blurred vision. She reports one transient flicker of vision on standing quickly, which resolved. She denies right upper quadrant pain. She reports increased evening ankle and foot swelling; her wedding ring was tight this week. Home blood pressures average 138/88 most mornings. Home glucose fasting around 96 mg/dL; postprandial 150 to 160 mg/dL one hour after lunch, using a continuous glucose sensor. She has decreased refined carbohydrates, with limited adherence during night shifts due to vending machine access. Medication adherence is good: labetalol, low-dose aspirin, and prenatal vitamins. No metformin.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Works as a bus operator on the night shift for Lone Pine Sawmill, with limited access to meals at the depot. Lives in Knoxville. The depot is located at Indian River Lagoon near the river. Her husband packs her lunches. Family trip to Cape Cod planned in two weeks for a wedding; no contraindication identified.

OBSTETRIC HISTORY

G2P1. Prior uncomplicated vaginal delivery.

PHYSICAL EXAM

BP 142/90 right arm. HR 84. Temp 98.6 F. Weight increased by 1 lb since last visit. Fundal height 30 cm, consistent with dates. Fetal heart rate 148 bpm, reactive. Reflexes 3+ without clonus. Mild pitting edema at ankles. No RUQ or epigastric tenderness.

RESULTS

Urine dipstick: trace protein. CBC with platelets, hepatic function panel, and creatinine drawn today; results pending.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Chronic (pre-existing) essential hypertension in pregnancy, third trimester, with mild elevation today. Increase labetalol to 200 mg twice daily. Home BP log. Evaluate for superimposed preeclampsia with labs given trace proteinuria. Return precautions reviewed.
2. Gestational diabetes mellitus, diet-controlled. Continue dietary modification; CGM review at next visit; postprandial targets reviewed.
3. Fetal growth surveillance: growth ultrasound in 3 weeks. Weekly visits from 36 weeks. Kick counts daily.
4. Dizziness with standing, possibly related to labetalol. Counseled on slow positional changes; no driving if dizzy. Work note offered.
5. Travel to Cape Cod permitted with home monitoring and an adequate medication supply.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Intermittent left hand numbness and recurrent headaches.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Zoltan Lombardi is a 23-year-old male with a long-standing history of migraine who presents with about four episodes of left hand numbness over the past month. He works as a forklift operator on the night shift at the warehouse. Migraine diagnosis was made in 2025. Each episode is preceded by approximately twenty minutes of visual aura described as wavy lines in the left visual field, followed by numbness of the left fingers and then a unilateral throbbing headache lasting several hours. He denies facial droop, dysarthria, or focal weakness of the leg. He takes sumatriptan roughly twice a month and ibuprofen intermittently. He reports five hours of sleep on his night shift schedule and drinks approximately four energy drinks per shift. He quit smoking last year and drinks two beers on weekends.

Family history is notable for a grandmother with stroke in her seventies and a mother with migraine. His last physical was on 07/12/2025.

PHYSICAL EXAM

BP 126/78, pulse 72. Neurological examination shows full extraocular movements, symmetric strength, and intact speech. Sensation to light touch is mildly decreased in the left fingers. Reflexes are symmetric and gait is normal.

RESULTS

MRI brain with contrast scheduled. Basic labs and ECG ordered.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Migraine with aura with transient left hand paresthesia. Differential includes migraine aura versus transient ischemic event given family history, though the age and aura pattern favor migraine. Imaging was selected in line with the Washington guidelines for new-onset headache with focal symptoms. MRI brain with and without contrast, ECG, and basic labs ordered. Advised to hold operation of heavy equipment until workup is complete; work note provided.

2. Recurrent headache with frequent acute medication use. Limit sumatriptan to no more than two days per week and ibuprofen to avoid medication overuse headache. Start headache diary tracking dates and triggers.

3. Sleep disruption and caffeine use on night shift. Counseled on sleep hygiene and reducing energy drink intake.

Return precautions reviewed, including persistent arm weakness, slurred speech, or a sudden worst headache, with instruction to call 911.

Paresthesia of skin
Headache, unspecified
Family history of stroke

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Intermittent left hand numbness and recurrent headaches.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Gordon Eriksen is a 26-year-old male with a long-standing history of migraine who presents with about four episodes of left hand numbness over the past month. He works as a forklift operator on the night shift at the warehouse. The first episode occurred around November Twelfth while he was operating equipment; he pulled over and symptoms resolved in about ten minutes. He continued working that night.

Migraine diagnosis was made in 2020. Each episode is preceded by approximately twenty minutes of visual aura described as wavy lines in the left visual field, followed by numbness of the left fingers and then a unilateral throbbing headache lasting several hours. dialogue:
[doctor] hi , kevin . i'm doctor ueda . how have you been since your gallbladder surgery ?
[patient] honestly , it's been a weird three weeks . the incisions healed fine , but i've got this bulge right above my belly button that wasn't there before .
[doctor] okay . tell me when you first noticed it .
[patient] about ten days after surgery . i was doing my usual routine and i felt a pop , and then this lump showed up . it's soft when i lie down and it pushes out when i stand up .
[doctor] does it hurt ?
[patient] it's sore . i'd say about a four out of ten most of the time , but when i cough or strain it gets like a seven out of ten .
[doctor] okay . where exactly is it ? is it at one of the old port sites or in the middle ?
[patient] it's right at the top edge of the big incision , the one under my ribs .
[doctor] what were you doing when you felt the pop ?
[patient] i was trying to lift a heavy engine block in my garage . i restore vintage motorcycles in my garage , and i was hauling a cylinder head onto the bench . my wife was yelling at me to get help , and of course i did n't .
[doctor] that's the kind of thing we tell people to avoid for a while . how much does the bulge change ?
[patient] it comes and goes . sometimes i can push it back in , sometimes it stays out . it's bigger when i'm on my feet all day .
[doctor] okay . are you working right now ?
[patient] i'm on leave from work right now , so i'm mostly at home . but last weekend i went out and played pickleball with my brother svetlana , and i think that was too much too soon .
[doctor] okay . did anything change after the pickleball ?
[patient] the bulge got bigger that night . it hurt more when i got up from the couch .
[doctor] any nausea , vomiting , or trouble passing gas ?
[patient] no , i'm eating fine . i had some constipation from the pain medicine but that cleared up with some prune juice .
[doctor] good . any fever or redness over the bulge ?
[patient] no fever . the skin looks normal . it's just a little warm when i press it .
[doctor] okay . let's look . can you lie back for me ? i'm going to press gently here on the bulge and ask you to cough .
[patient] okay . ow , that's sore . it's pushing out more now .
[doctor] i can feel a soft defect in the fascia right under the old incision . when you cough , it bulges . the skin is intact and there's no redness . it's reducible , so i can push it back in .
[patient] oh , that's better .
[doctor] the bowel does not seem to be trapped . your abdomen is soft and not tender everywhere . your temperature is ninety eight point six and your pulse is seventy six .
[patient] okay , that's good . what is it ?
[doctor] it sounds like an incisional hernia . that means some tissue has pushed through the muscle wall where the incision was closed . it happens in a small number of people after gallbladder surgery , especially after heavy lifting or straining .
[patient] so it's not from the surgery itself ?
[doctor] it's a complication of healing , but it's not your fault . what matters now is we keep it from getting stuck or strangled .
[patient] okay . so what do we do ?
[doctor] we'll start with a ct scan of your abdomen to see how big the defect is and what's inside . then i'd like you to see the hernia clinic for a repair decision . in the meantime no lifting more than ten pounds .
[patient] ten pounds , that's nothing . my motorcycle projects are going to sit for a while .
[doctor] i know it's frustrating . you could wear an abdominal binder when you're up and moving .
[patient] my wife bought one already . she's been on me to take it easy . yes , we just adopted twins in may , they're eighteen months now . so i'm chasing two toddlers all day . it's hard to sit still .
[doctor] how are you managing the pain ? are you taking anything ?
[patient] just tylenol at night and some ibuprofen when the pain is bad . i'm trying not to take too much .
[doctor] that's reasonable . i'd avoid ibuprofen for now if you're still having the pain . keep taking tylenol as needed , up to three grams a day .
[patient] okay . how long until i can go back to the gym ?
[doctor] probably not until the repair is planned . we'll revisit that after your scan .
[patient] that's a bummer . my brother keeps telling me i'm getting soft .
[doctor] tell him to be patient . and the gallbladder pathology report came back . it showed chronic cholecystitis with gallstones and no cancer .
[patient] good . so that's done .
[doctor] yes . i'll see you back in two weeks after the ct . if the bulge becomes hard , red , or painful , or you have vomiting , go to the emergency room right away .
[patient] got it . thanks , doctor ueda .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Bulge at the upper incision three weeks after cholecystectomy.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kevin Zimmerman is a 37-year-old male who is three weeks status post laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic cholelithiasis and presents with a new bulge at the superior edge of the subcostal incision. He first noticed the bulge approximately ten days after surgery, after lifting a heavy cylinder head in his garage. He restores vintage motorcycles in his garage. The bulge is soft when recumbent and protrudes with standing and coughing. He describes discomfort as 4/10 at rest and 7/10 with coughing or straining.

He played pickleball last weekend, after which the bulge enlarged and became more painful when rising from a seated position. He denies nausea, vomiting, fever, or obstipation. He reports transient constipation related to pain medication, now resolved. He has been taking acetaminophen nightly and occasional ibuprofen. He is on leave from work. He recently adopted twins in May and is caring for two toddlers daily. His wife has been encouraging restriction of activity.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Temp 98.6 F, pulse 76. Abdomen soft, nontender except over the bulge. A soft reducible defect is palpated in the fascia beneath the superior incision that expands with cough. Skin over the defect is intact without erythema. No signs of incarceration or strangulation.

RESULTS

Surgical pathology from the cholecystectomy: chronic cholecystitis with cholelithiasis; no malignancy.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Incisional hernia at the subcostal port site following laparoscopic cholecystectomy, reducible, without obstruction or strangulation. Activity restriction with no lifting more than 10 pounds and use of an abdominal binder for activity. CT abdomen and pelvis ordered to define defect size and contents. Referral to hernia clinic for repair planning. Return precautions reviewed for a firm, red, or painful bulge, vomiting, or fever, with emergency department evaluation if these occur.

2. Postoperative pain. Acetaminophen up to 3 grams daily. Avoid NSAIDs for now.

3. Status post cholecystectomy with pathology reviewed and benign.

4. Constipation, resolved.

Acquired absence of other specified parts of digestive tract
Generalized abdominal pain
Encounter for surgical aftercare following surgery on the digestive system

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , fiona . i'm doctor eriksen , i'm a geriatrician . thanks for coming in . your primary care doctor sent me a letter about your balance and your memory .
[patient] oh , that letter . she's worried about me , i know . i'm not as steady as i used to be and i forget where i put things .
[doctor] tell me about the balance first . when did you start noticing it ?
[patient] maybe the last few months . i stumbled in the kitchen last month , just reaching for the cabinet , and i grabbed the counter . i did n't hit the floor .
[doctor] that's important that you caught yourself . were you dizzy at the time , or did your legs just give out ?
[patient] neither . my feet just didn't do what i told them . i'm not dizzy , i don't spin .
[doctor] okay . do you use anything to walk ?
[patient] i have a walker in the closet that my daughter bought me , but i only use it at night when i'm going to the bathroom . my daughter kwame keeps saying i should use it all the time .
[doctor] that sounds like good advice . how is your vision and your hearing ?
[patient] my eyes are fine with my glasses . i have a little trouble with the phone , but that's probably the hearing .
[doctor] okay . tell me about your work history , since you mentioned it when we talked on the phone .
[patient] i was a pastry chef for thirty six years . i stood on my feet twelve hours a day . i would lift those big sheet pans and bags of flour . my knees and my back paid for that .
[doctor] and you're retired now ?
[patient] since 2023 . i still bake for my grandkids on sundays , but nothing like before .
[doctor] that's nice . how about your memory ? what do you notice ?
[patient] i misplace things all the time . keys , my glasses . once my purse went missing for two days and it was in the refrigerator . my daughter thinks it's worse than i do .
[doctor] that's a common concern . have you had trouble with things you used to do easily , like following a recipe or paying bills ?
[patient] the recipes , yes . i used to make puff pastry from memory and now i have to write every step down . i don't like it .
[doctor] i understand . do you get lost driving , or forget conversations ?
[patient] i stopped driving last year . my daughter takes me to the grocery store , and that's fine .
[doctor] when was the last time your bone density was checked ?
[patient] i think january twenty third . the doctor said i had thin bones and started me on a pill . i think it's called alendronate .
[doctor] right . when was the scan that showed the thin bones ?
[patient] 2023 , the year i turned sixty five . they said my spine and hip were thin .
[doctor] okay . are you still taking the alendronate every week ?
[patient] most weeks . sometimes i forget that too .
[doctor] that's important to address . how about blood pressure pills ?
[patient] lisinopril for the pressure , every morning . it's been fine .
[doctor] good . let's do a quick exam . can you stand up from this chair without using your hands ?
[patient] it takes me a few tries . there , okay .
[doctor] your blood pressure sitting is one thirty eight over eighty , heart rate sixty eight . let me check your gait . walk to the door and back for me .
[patient] okay . i'm slow but i'm getting there .
[doctor] your gait is wide based and short steps . when you turn you take a few small steps . i'd like to do a quick cognitive screen . can you name as many animals as you can in one minute ?
[patient] dogs , cats , horses , cows , pigs . um . goats . chickens .
[doctor] good . can you tell me what day and month it is ?
[patient] it's october , and it's a friday . the date i'm not sure of , maybe the seventeenth .
[doctor] very close . can you remember three words i'll say ? apple , table , penny .
[patient] apple , penny , and ... table .
[doctor] good , you got all three . the score on the screen is about twenty three out of thirty , which suggests mild impairment . we'll need blood work and maybe a brain scan .
[patient] okay . i'm scared of the brain scan .
[doctor] it's just an mri , no needles . let's check thyroid and vitamin b twelve , which can both cause memory trouble and are easy to treat .
[patient] good .
[doctor] for the falls , i'd like physical therapy for balance and strength . and a home safety check . and we'll review your sleep medications , since i see you take a sleeping pill at bedtime .
[patient] just one half of a pill . for my sleep .
[doctor] that medication can worsen balance and memory , so i'd like to taper it slowly .
[patient] okay , i'll do what you say .
[doctor] you could also use a pill organizer , so you don't double up or skip the alendronate .
[patient] my daughter already bought one of those . she picks up my pills at the pharmacy anyway . i'll use it .
[doctor] wonderful . and take the alendronate first thing in the morning with a full glass of water , and stay upright for thirty minutes .
[patient] stay upright , got it .
[doctor] i'll see you back in six weeks with the labs and the mri results . if you fall and hit your head , or you get new weakness or confusion , call right away .
[patient] thank you , doctor eriksen . you've been very patient with me .

Referral for gait instability, falls risk, and memory complaints.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Fiona Agarwal is a 88-year-old female referred by her primary care physician for evaluation of progressive unsteadiness and subjective memory decline. She stumbled in the kitchen last month while reaching for a cabinet and caught herself on the counter without falling to the floor. She denies vertigo and lightheadedness. She uses a walker only at night for bathroom trips. Her daughter, Kwame, is concerned about her safety and manages her transportation since she stopped driving last year.

She reports misplacing objects frequently and an episode in which her purse was misplaced for two days and was found in the refrigerator. She has difficulty following recipes she previously prepared from memory. She retired after working as a pastry chef for 36 years and continues to bake for her grandchildren on Sundays. She reports standing for long periods and lifting heavy sheet pans and flour bags throughout that career, with chronic knee and back pain.

A bone density evaluation in 2023 established a diagnosis of osteoporosis. She takes alendronate weekly but reports missing doses. Her daughter picks up medications at the pharmacy. She takes lisinopril daily for hypertension and a half tablet of a sleep aid at bedtime.

PHYSICAL EXAM

BP 138/80 seated, heart rate 68. Sit-to-stand requires multiple attempts without arm support. Gait is wide-based with short steps and multiple small steps on turning. Romberg not performed given balance concerns.

COGNITIVE SCREEN

Animal naming: 6 in one minute. Orientation: correct month and day of week, approximate date. Three-word recall: 3 of 3 after delay. Overall score approximately 23/30.

RESULTS

Labs pending for thyroid function and vitamin B12. MRI brain ordered.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Gait instability with a recent near-fall, likely multifactorial, including age-related deconditioning, sleep medication effect, and possible sensory decline. Physical therapy referral for balance and strengthening. Home safety evaluation requested.

2. Mild cognitive impairment, subjective and objective, of uncertain etiology. Thyroid function and vitamin B12 ordered. MRI brain to exclude structural causes. Taper sleep medication slowly.

3. Age-related osteoporosis on ongoing alendronate therapy. Counseled on administration, including taking it on an empty stomach with a full glass of water and remaining upright for 30 minutes. Pill organizer recommended.

4. Essential hypertension, controlled on lisinopril.

Return precautions reviewed, including head strike with a fall, new weakness, or acute confusion.

Mild cognitive impairment of uncertain or unknown etiology
Essential (primary) hypertension

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right ankle pain and swelling after a fall.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Zainab Yilmaz is a 30-year-old female who presents with right ankle pain and swelling after a trip and fall on a cracked sidewalk in Silver Lake last Tuesday around six in the evening while walking her dog. She went down onto her right side and attempted to break her fall with her hand; her wrist is not injured. She denies head strike or loss of consciousness. Her mother, Victor, accompanied her and noticed limping after she got home. She has been taking acetaminophen and applying ice. She reports pain localized to the lateral ankle. She had a prior right ankle sprain two years ago during volleyball that healed fully.

She works as a dental hygienist and is on her feet and bending over patients for most of the day. She is currently off work and states she has not had a leave of this length before.

SOCIAL HISTORY: She fosters rescue greyhounds, currently has four, and is the youngest of seven siblings. She lives alone. Her fitness tracker recorded approximately 8,000 steps the day prior to the injury.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Right ankle with moderate lateral swelling and ecchymosis. Tenderness over the anterior talofibular ligament. No tenderness over the base of the fifth metatarsal. Pain 6/10 at rest. Distal sensation intact, toes pink, capillary refill brisk. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses are 2+.

RESULTS

X-ray of right ankle and foot: no fracture or dislocation. Findings consistent with lateral ligament sprain.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right ankle sprain, lateral ligament, grade II, closed, initial encounter, following a trip and fall on a sidewalk. Weight bearing as tolerated with lace-up brace and crutches for one week. RICE protocol. Acetaminophen up to 3 g daily; avoid NSAIDs for the first few days. Physical therapy referral. Return to work after one week off, with brace.

dialogue:

[patient] my nurse , pilar , is on the phone line in case the video drops . she's the one who set up the screen share for me .
[doctor] wonderful . hi , pilar . i'll ask her to call my office if we lose the connection .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so , tell me how the eye drops have been going . you're using the latanoprost at bedtime ?
[patient] yes , one drop in each eye every night . i'm pretty consistent . the timolol in the morning , i forget sometimes .
[doctor] that's the most common issue with drops . how's your vision in general ?
[patient] it's blurry in the evening . the lights at night look like they have halos around them . i notice it when i'm driving home from work .
[doctor] okay . how far do you drive for work ?
[patient] not far . i work the front desk at blue harbor foods , it's about ten minutes . i'm usually on the road right around dusk .
[doctor] got it . any eye pain , redness , headaches , or nausea ?
[patient] no pain . my eyes feel dry most of the day , like sand in them . i use the artificial tears every hour or two .
[doctor] okay . what about the halos . are they new in the last few months ?
[patient] they've been slowly getting worse since the spring . my glasses don't help much anymore .
[doctor] i understand . let's talk about the pressure first . your last measurements in the clinic were about fifteen and sixteen . is that right ?
[patient] i think so . i don't remember the numbers .

[patient] so it's getting worse ?

[patient] okay .
[doctor] now let's look at the cataracts . when we last checked in july first , the lens clouding was moderate . do you still have trouble reading small print ?

[patient] that's exactly the problem . i'm slower to drive at night .

[doctor] that's reasonable . i want to see you before then though .
[patient] okay , july first works for me if the schedule allows .
[doctor] i'll ask the front desk to hold it . now the dry eye . are you using warm compresses ?

[doctor] that's a good reminder . keep using the artificial tears , and consider preservative free ones if you use them more than four times a day .
[patient] okay , i'll switch .
[doctor] your nearsightedness is also stable . the glasses from last year still correct your distance vision reasonably well .
[patient] they're fine for driving during the day .
[doctor] good . let's talk about the pharmacy . where do you pick up your drops ?
[patient] the walgreens on fifth street , they always have them in stock . they text me when the refill is ready .
[doctor] perfect . i'll send the new timolol prescription there today .
[patient] thank you . i'd rather not have another bottle sitting unopened in the fridge .
[doctor] that's common . label the bottles with the date you opened them . and don't take the latanoprost more than once a day .
[patient] okay . i'll write it on the box with a marker .

[doctor] okay . and your blood pressure is controlled , right ?

[doctor] alright , i'll see you in six weeks . call the office if you get sudden eye pain , a severe headache , or a sudden drop in vision .
[patient] will do . bye .

Telehealth follow-up for glaucoma, cataract, and dry eye.

Her nurse, Pilar, assisted with the connection from the patient's home. Video quality was intermittently degraded, so the examination is limited to history and visual inspection by video.

She reports adherence to latanoprost nightly and timolol in the morning, with occasional missed doses. She reports evening blurring of vision with halos around lights, worse since spring and most noticeable while driving home from work at dusk. She works at the front desk of Blue Harbor Foods, approximately ten minutes away. She reports constant dryness and grittiness, using artificial tears every one to two hours. She denies ocular pain or redness. She reports difficulty with near tasks and needs bright light for reading.

Clinic intraocular pressures were approximately 15 and 16 mmHg on prior visits. Optic nerve changes on last year's OCT are more pronounced compared with prior imaging.

SOCIAL HISTORY: She restores pianos and rings handbells on Tuesday nights. She keeps fourteen chickens and a rescued three-legged cat. She is the oldest of five children. She uses a fitness tracker and reports about 6,000 steps per day. She takes low-dose aspirin every other day, vitamins, and fish oil. Her blood pressure is managed by her primary care physician. Her pharmacy is the walgreens on fifth street, which sends refill notifications.

PHYSICAL EXAM (VIDEO)

Limited by video. Visual inspection shows symmetric lid position without obvious ptosis. Conjunctival injection not appreciated. Pupils appear equal. Patient reports blurred near vision.

RESULTS

Most recent clinic IOP approximately 15 and 16 mmHg. Optic nerve changes on last year's OCT more pronounced compared with prior imaging. Lens clouding graded as moderate at the last in-person visit on July First.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Primary open-angle glaucoma, bilateral, mild stage, with progressive optic nerve changes on imaging. Continue latanoprost nightly and timolol each morning. Adherence reinforced, with bottles labeled with open dates. Lower target IOP strongly recommended. Plan OCT of the optic nerve and automated visual field testing before surgical planning.

2. Nuclear cataract, bilateral, with symptomatic glare and night driving difficulty. Cataract surgery discussed; patient prefers to defer until after the holiday season. Surgical planning to address glaucoma at the same time.

3. Dry eye syndrome, bilateral. Preservative-free artificial tears up to four times daily. Warm compresses daily. Lid hygiene encouraged.

4. Myopia, bilateral, stable. Current spectacles adequate for daytime distance vision.

Refill of timolol to be sent to the pharmacy today. Counseled to avoid night driving if halos worsen, to protect eyes from wind, and to call for sudden eye pain, severe headache, or sudden vision loss. Return visit in six weeks.

Age-related nuclear cataract, bilateral
Dry eye syndrome of bilateral lacrimal glands
Myopia, bilateral

[doctor] hi , kwame . i'm doctor iverson . what's going on with the knee ?
[patient] hey doctor iverson . my right knee blew up on me about four days ago . it's swollen in the back , behind the kneecap , and it feels tight .
[doctor] okay . did you injure it or twist it ?
[patient] not really . i was up on a ladder all day wiring a panel , and i think i just kept kneeling on the concrete . my coworker jacqueline said i looked like i was walking on stilts .
[doctor] ha . what do you do for work ?
[patient] i'm a licensed electrician . i'm up and down ladders and crawling into crawl spaces all day . my knees take a beating .
[doctor] that's a physical job . does the knee hurt when you bend it ?
[patient] yes , especially when i bend all the way down . when i straighten it , the back of the knee pulls .
[doctor] okay . any fever , redness , or warmth ?
[patient] no fever . it's a little warm when i touch it , but not red .
[doctor] good . did you have any locking or the knee giving out ?
[patient] no locking . it just feels full .
[doctor] okay . let me look . can you stand for me ? straighten your leg .
[patient] okay . it's kind of stiff .
[doctor] i see a soft swelling behind the knee , in the popliteal area . it's tender to touch . the calf is not swollen , and there's no redness . let me check your pulses .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] pulses are strong in both feet . the calf is soft with no tenderness . the joint itself has some fluid , and your range of motion is about one hundred ten degrees .
[patient] so it's not a blood clot ?
[doctor] i don't think so , but it's important to ask . you have no swelling in the calf and no shortness of breath .
[patient] no , no breathing problems .
[doctor] good . from what you've told me this sounds like a baker's cyst , which is a fluid-filled bulge behind the knee that often comes from arthritis or irritation .
[patient] baker's cyst . is that bad ?
[doctor] usually not , it's common . but we want to rule out other causes . how long have you had knee arthritis ?
[patient] they said it was arthritis in the right knee about five years ago . i take ibuprofen when it flares up .
[doctor] okay . are you taking anything else ?
[patient] my blood sugar has been high lately . i've been on metformin for two years , five hundred twice a day .
[doctor] good , that's helpful . your sugars matter for healing . what was your most recent a1c ?
[patient] i think it was seven point four in the spring . my wife keeps reminding me to go back for the lab .
[doctor] i'd like to check it again today . and your blood pressure . let's see . it's one thirty four over eighty six .
[patient] that's been running high , they say i need a new pill for it .
[doctor] right . are you on anything for the pressure right now ?
[patient] yes , it was amlodipine , i think . i take it every night .
[doctor] okay . do you have any family history of arthritis , or any neurologic conditions ?
[patient] my dad had parkinson's , and my mom had bad arthritis in her hands .

[patient] fine .

[patient] okay , i'll mix it up .

[patient] got it . thanks , doctor iverson .

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , simon . i'm doctor szymanski . how's school going ? i saw you're 14 now .
[patient] hi doctor szymanski . yeah , i'm 14 . school is fine , i guess . the asthma has been kind of annoying though .
[doctor] tell me about it . how often are you using the rescue inhaler ?
[patient] like twice a week ? more when the pollen is bad . i have a spacer that my brother bogdan made me use after i kept messing up the inhaler .
[doctor] that's a helpful brother . did you have any nighttime coughing ?
[patient] a couple nights , yeah . it wakes me up and then i can't get back to sleep .
[doctor] how many nights a week is that ?
[patient] maybe once a week . i think it's worse in september when the ragweed goes crazy .
[doctor] okay . are you taking the controller inhaler every day ?
[patient] most days . i forget on the weekends when i'm at the farm .
[doctor] at the farm ? tell me about that .
[patient] i'm one of four boys in our house , so we all have chores . i raise quail for the county fair , and i have forty birds in the barn right now .
[doctor] that's a lot of birds . is there dust or feathers in the barn ?
[patient] yeah , a lot of dust when i clean the coops . i wear a mask but sometimes i don't .
[doctor] okay , let's talk about that . any limits in sports , or coughing during practice ?
[patient] i play soccer and i get winded at the end of the halves . the coach asked if i'm okay .
[doctor] good , i'm glad you're asking for help . have you been wheezing during the games ?
[patient] sometimes . i use the rescue inhaler before warm ups now .
[doctor] that's the right approach . how's your allergy situation ? sneezing , itchy eyes ?
[patient] yes , constant in the fall . my eyes itch and my nose is running all day .
[doctor] i'd like to check the focus too , since you're on the adhd medication . how is that going ?
[patient] the medicine helps me focus in class . but i can't eat much lunch and i'm grumpy by the end of the day .
[doctor] that's a common side effect . are you still taking it every morning ?
[patient] yes . i take it before breakfast and then i eat a big snack after school .
[doctor] good idea . how's your sleep on the medicine ?
[patient] it's okay . i fall asleep around eleven . my mom says i'm up at six thirty every morning .
[doctor] screen time at night ?
[patient] a little . i play games on my phone until midnight sometimes . i know .
[doctor] okay . let's check your lungs and your vitals . take a deep breath in and out for me .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] your lungs are clear today , with no wheezing right now . your oxygen level is ninety eight percent and your pulse is eighty six . blood pressure is one eleven over sixty eight .
[patient] good .
[doctor] your nose has some swelling and clear discharge . your throat is a little red , but i don't see any infection .
[patient] okay . so what's the plan ?
[doctor] first , we'll increase the controller inhaler to a twice daily dose for the next month and recheck your peak flow .
[patient] twice a day ? i'll forget that .
[doctor] set an alarm on your phone , and use the spacer every time . i'll also start a nasal steroid spray for the allergies , one spray in each nostril every morning .
[patient] okay . my brother will remind me anyway .
[doctor] good . for the attention medicine , i'm not changing the dose yet , but i want to check your weight and appetite in one month . we can move the dose later in the day if it helps .
[patient] that might help . i don't mind the medicine , i just hate being grumpy .
[doctor] i understand . let's also talk about screen time . try to stop your phone an hour before bed .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] your flu shot is due this fall . screening starts at forty five for some other things , but the vaccine schedule for teenagers is different . and the guidelines say adults over the age of sixty five need extra vaccines , which is not you right now .
[patient] i already had my flu shot last year at school .
[doctor] perfect . then we'll just check your records for it .
[patient] ha , good , i'd hate to need extra shots .
[doctor] okay . the rescue inhaler stays with you at all times , including at soccer and at the farm . if you need it more than three times in a week , or you can't speak full sentences , call the office or go to the emergency room .
[patient] got it . thanks , doctor szymanski . see you in a month .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up of asthma with seasonal allergic symptoms and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder on stimulant therapy.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Simon Ueda is a 14-year-old male with asthma, seasonal allergic rhinitis, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder presenting for routine follow-up. He uses albuterol approximately twice weekly, more with high pollen. He reports nocturnal cough and awakening about once weekly, worse in September with ragweed exposure. He takes an inhaled corticosteroid daily but misses doses on weekends. He uses a spacer, introduced by his older brother, Bogdan.

He is one of four boys in the household and helps with chores. He raises quail for a county fair project, with approximately forty birds housed in a barn. He reports dust exposure during coop cleaning and inconsistent mask use. He reports winding down at the end of halves in soccer and has used albuterol before warm-ups. He reports constant itchy eyes and rhinorrhea during the fall.

He takes a stimulant medication each morning for ADHD, which is effective in class but causes lunch-time appetite suppression and irritability by late afternoon. He sleeps around 11 PM with a parent-reported wake time of 6:30 AM. He uses his phone until midnight at times.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Vitals: SpO2 98 percent on room air, heart rate 86, BP 111/68. Lungs clear to auscultation without wheezing at rest. Nasal mucosa with edema and clear discharge. Oropharynx mildly erythematous without exudate.

RESULTS

Peak flow measurement to be repeated at next visit.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Mild persistent asthma, uncomplicated, with exercise-related symptoms and nocturnal awakenings. Increase inhaled corticosteroid to twice daily for one month. Continue albuterol as needed, including before exercise. Spacer technique reviewed. Recheck peak flow at follow-up.

2. Seasonal allergic rhinitis due to pollen. Start intranasal corticosteroid spray daily. Environmental counseling regarding dust and quail coop cleaning with mask use.

3. Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, combined presentation, on stimulant. No dose change today. Monitor weight and appetite; consider moving the dose later in the day if appetite suppression persists. Sleep hygiene and limits on screen time before bed discussed.

Influenza vaccine given at school last year, per record. Return precautions reviewed, with rescue inhaler use more than three times weekly or inability to speak full sentences prompting an urgent call or emergency care.

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , santiago . i'm doctor zamora . you've been traveling , i hear ? what happened to your hand ?
[patient] hi doctor zamora . yeah , we just got back from a two week trip to portugal . i cut my hand open on a broken wine glass in a cafe in kalamazoo .
[doctor] oh no . tell me exactly what happened .
[patient] we were having dinner on the second night . the waiter knocked a full bottle off the edge of the table , and it shattered on the tile . i reached down to grab the stem of my glass without thinking , and the glass broke in my right hand .
[doctor] ouch . which hand did you cut ?
[patient] my right hand , across the palm and the base of my thumb . there was a lot of blood , and the staff wrapped it in a towel .
[doctor] okay . did you go to a clinic or a hospital there ?
[patient] a small clinic near the hotel . they cleaned it , put in stitches , and gave me a tetanus shot . the stitches are a little tight now .
[doctor] did they give you any paperwork or a note about the antibiotics ?
[patient] they gave me a prescription for antibiotics in portuguese . i got it filled at the pharmacy near the hotel , the first one i found , and i've been taking one tablet twice a day .
[doctor] okay . do you have any fevers , redness , or drainage ?
[patient] no fever . a little pink around the stitches on the second day but it's better now . no drainage .
[doctor] good . what is your job , by the way ? you seem like you're used to using your hands .
[patient] i'm a marine surveyor . i climb around cargo ships and inspect the hulls , so my hands are in everything , and i get cut a lot .
[doctor] that makes sense . when do you usually work ?
[patient] usually weekdays on the water at the port . on weekends i volunteer as a lifeboat crewman . we've got a little boat , and it's a rare hobby , i know , but i love it .
[doctor] that's impressive . okay , let's look at the hand . can you make a fist for me ?
[patient] i can make a fist but it's tight across the palm .
[doctor] good . i see a clean laceration about five centimeters across the palm and a smaller one at the base of the thumb , both with sutures in place . there's no active bleeding and no pus .
[patient] that's good .
[doctor] how's your sensation ? can you feel my touch on each finger ?
[patient] yes , all of them . the thumb is numb on the very tip but that's been since the day after .
[doctor] okay . the sensation is intact in the other fingers . your capillary refill is brisk . can you spread your fingers ?
[patient] yes , a bit slow but yes .
[doctor] good . now , i see on your list that you take eliquis for atrial fibrillation . when did you last take it ?
[patient] this morning , with breakfast . i don't miss it , i take it every twelve hours .
[doctor] good . that's important because it can make bleeding worse , and that's why the hand was bleeding so much .
[patient] i know , i told the clinic that too .
[doctor] also , do you take aspirin or tylenol , or anything else for pain ?
[patient] just tylenol . no aspirin . i took two with dinner .
[doctor] okay . let's clean this area again and check the wound edges . this might sting a little .
[patient] ow . okay .
[doctor] the wound looks clean . i'll remove the stitches in about ten days , and i want you to keep the hand dry for another few days .
[patient] i can do that . i have a fitbit and i'm supposed to keep walking , so i'll walk on the treadmill instead of outside .
[doctor] that's a good plan . keep the hand elevated and move your fingers every hour .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] we'll check your tetanus status since the clinic gave you a shot already . i'll keep it on record .
[patient] thank you .
[doctor] i'll also get an x-ray of the right hand to make sure there's no glass left behind . glass can show up on x-ray or not , so we'll look .
[patient] there was no glass that i saw .
[doctor] okay , good . any other travel problems ? any diarrhea , vomiting , or fever since you got back ?
[patient] no , nothing like that . i had an upset stomach on the flight but it's gone .
[doctor] good . and do you have any trouble breathing , chest pain , or dizziness ?
[patient] no , none of that .
[doctor] okay . let's plan the follow up . i want to see you again after the stitches come out , and sooner if the hand gets hot , red , or starts draining .
[patient] yes , i'll come back . my wife says i need to stop trying to do everything with one hand anyway .
[doctor] she's right . finish the antibiotics and bring the bottle next time .
[patient] okay . thanks , doctor zamora .
note:

Right palm and thumb lacerations sustained while traveling abroad; suture check and wound care.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

He reports one episode of upset stomach during the flight, now resolved. He denies diarrhea, vomiting, dyspnea, or chest pain.

He takes apixaban (Eliquis) twice daily for atrial fibrillation, last dose this morning. He uses acetaminophen for pain and denies aspirin use.

SOCIAL HISTORY: He works as a marine surveyor, inspecting ship hulls on cargo vessels at the port. He volunteers as a weekend lifeboat crewman.

PHYSICAL EXAM

BP and pulse stable. Right palm laceration approximately 5 cm with sutures in place, with no active bleeding or purulence. Smaller laceration at the base of the right thumb with sutures in place. Mild residual tightness with fist formation. Sensation intact to light touch in all digits, with decreased sensation at the distal thumb pulp. Capillary refill brisk. Wounds cleaned and edges checked, without signs of infection.

RESULTS

Right hand radiographs ordered to exclude retained foreign body.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

2. Long-term anticoagulation with apixaban for atrial fibrillation. Counseled that anticoagulation may increase bleeding; the bleeding from the injury was consistent with this.

3. Tetanus status updated per clinic record. Complete antibiotic course; bring bottle to next visit.

4. Travel-related gastrointestinal symptoms resolved.

Return precautions reviewed for redness, warmth, drainage, or fever.
