dialogue:
[doctor] hi , dolores . i'm doctor vukovic . how are you feeling today ?
[patient] honestly not great , doctor . i woke up looking like a balloon this morning . my lips and my eyelids are puffy and i have hives all over my arms .
[doctor] i'm sorry to hear that . is that your sister with you ?
[patient] yes , this is renata . she took the morning off work to drive me here . she said i should come in right away because the swelling was getting worse .
[doctor] that was the right call . so tell me when this started .
[patient] it started about two days ago . i had a tooth pulled on september ninth at riverside rowing club for an abscess , and the dentist sent me home with amoxicillin . i took the first pill that night . by the next morning my lips were swollen .
[doctor] okay . had you ever taken amoxicillin or penicillin before ?
[patient] i do n't think so . i had a rash from sulfa pills when i was a teenager , but that's the only thing i remember .
[doctor] okay . any trouble breathing , or any tightness in your throat or your voice changing ?
[patient] no , my throat feels a little funny , like something is sitting there , but i can swallow . i can breathe fine .
[doctor] good . and how is the itching ?
[patient] the hives itch like crazy . i scratched my forearms raw last night . on a scale of one to ten the itch is about an eight .
[doctor] okay . and the pain in the tooth ?
[patient] that's better , actually . the dentist did a good job .
[doctor] let me take a look at you . your blood pressure is one twenty four over seventy six and your pulse is ninety . your temperature is normal . your lips and eyelids are swollen but your tongue looks normal . i can see raised welts across both forearms and up your back .
[patient] that's what it looks like .
[doctor] your lungs sound clear , no wheezing . so this looks like an allergic reaction to the amoxicillin . the swelling of the lips and eyelids is called angioedema , and the hives are urticaria .
[patient] so i ca n't have penicillin anymore ?
[doctor] that's right . we'll stop the amoxicillin today , and i'll add penicillin and amoxicillin to your allergy list so no one prescribes them again .
[patient] will that be a problem for my other antibiotics ?
[doctor] it can be . which other medicines do you take regularly ?
[patient] i take one fifty of levothyroxine every morning for my thyroid . and i use a nasal spray in the spring .
[doctor] is the spray for seasonal allergies ?
[patient] yes , i've had hay fever since 2020 . every april and may my eyes itch and i sneeze all day long .
[doctor] okay . do you have asthma or eczema ?
[patient] no asthma . i get dry patches on my hands in the winter , but that's mostly from the cold .
[doctor] okay . i'd like to draw a blood test to check your tryptase level . i'm going to give you prednisone and an antihistamine .
[patient] how much prednisone ?
[doctor] forty milligrams once a day for five days . take cetirizine ten milligrams every night , and use tylenol for the pain in your tooth .
[patient] okay . the tylenol is what i've been taking for the tooth , yeah .
[doctor] good . i'm also going to prescribe an epinephrine auto injector . if your throat starts to feel tight or you have trouble breathing , you use it right away and call nine one one .
[patient] okay . i'll keep it in my purse , and renata will keep one in her car .
[doctor] perfect . i'd like to refer you to our allergy clinic for testing , and the nurse will call you to schedule within the next two weeks .
[patient] can you please send the prescriptions to northgate pharmacy so they know about the penicillin ?
[doctor] yes , i'll send them to northgate pharmacy downtown . come back if the swelling spreads to your mouth or you start to feel dizzy .
[patient] got it . thank you , doctor vukovic .

dialogue:
[doctor] good morning , nadine . i'm doctor rinaldi . what brings you in today ?
[patient] morning , doctor rinaldi . i've been bleeding between my periods for about three weeks now , and there's this heavy pressure low in my belly .
[doctor] okay . is your daughter here with you today ?
[patient] yes , this is ximena . she's home from college for the weekend and she insisted on driving me .
[patient] hi . she made me come , honestly . she's been reading about this stuff online and she was scared .
[doctor] i'm glad you did . tell me more about the bleeding .
[patient] well , i still get my period , but now i'm spotting in the middle of the month too . last tuesday i soaked through a pad in about two hours . that was new .
[doctor] that sounds frightening . how long does each period last ?
[patient] usually four or five days . this month it went on for almost ten days , and it's been on and off since .
[doctor] are you using any pads or liners to measure it ?
[patient] pads , yes . i go through a super pad every few hours on the heavy days .
[doctor] okay . any clots , big ones like grapes ?
[patient] a few , yes . some the size of a quarter .
[doctor] that's helpful . and the pressure low in your belly , when did that start ?
[patient] about two weeks ago . it feels like someone is sitting on me . it's worse when i stand up for a long time .
[doctor] and you work standing up , right ?
[patient] i'm a pastry chef at a bakery downtown . i work the overnight shift , so i'm on my feet for about ten hours and i lift fifty pound sacks of flour all night . my back and my pelvis have been killing me .
[doctor] okay . i'd like to ask you about your history . are you still having hot flashes ?
[patient] oh yes , every night . i wake up soaked . that's been going on for almost three years now .
[doctor] that's common around this time . any other medical problems ?
[patient] i had a thyroid problem that was diagnosed in 2019 , a goiter , and they put me on a pill for it . and my mother had graves' disease , so my doctor always watches my thyroid .
[doctor] okay . are you taking anything for the hot flashes ?
[patient] no , i tried one of those black cohosh things and it upset my stomach .
[doctor] got it . have you had a pap smear or a mammogram recently ?
[patient] my last pap was on november fourth at the clinic , and it was normal . i had a mammogram about a year ago , also normal .
[doctor] good . and what medicines do you take every day ?
[patient] just the levothyroxine in the morning . and a calcium pill with my lunch .
[doctor] okay , let's check your vitals . your blood pressure is one twenty eight over seventy eight . your pulse is ninety six . your temperature is ninety eight point four .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] i'm going to examine your abdomen now . does it hurt when i press here ?
[patient] a little , it's a dull ache . it's not sharp .
[doctor] okay . i'm going to do a pelvic exam . i'll be gentle .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] the uterus feels enlarged , about the size of a twelve week pregnancy , and it's a bit firm on this side . there's no tenderness when i move the cervix .
[patient] what does that mean ?
[doctor] i'd like to get an ultrasound of your pelvis , and we'll check your blood count . i'm also going to order a hemoglobin level , because you've been losing a lot of blood . i want to make sure you are not anemic .
[patient] okay , yes . i'm tired all the time anyway .
[doctor] i know . the ultrasound will tell us whether there's a fibroid or a polyp in the lining . if it's a fibroid , they are usually benign .
[patient] what is a fibroid exactly ?
[doctor] it's a noncancerous growth in the muscle wall of the uterus . many women have them and never know . but they can cause heavy bleeding and pressure like you're describing .
[patient] okay . and the hot flashes ?
[doctor] for the hot flashes , we can talk about options after the ultrasound . for now i don't want you on any hormones until we know what's going on .
[patient] fine . when can i get the ultrasound ?
[doctor] our imaging team can see you on november fourth , which is early next week . the front desk will call you .
[patient] i'm on the overnight shift until then . can they call me during the day ?
[doctor] of course . what's the best number to reach you at ?
[patient] it's 895-568-1598 . that's my cell . please leave a message if i do n't pick up , because i sleep during the day .
[doctor] got it . i'll also ask the nurse to write that down . and i want you to keep a bleeding diary , writing down how many pads you change each day .
[patient] i can do that . my daughter has an app for it .
[patient] mom , just write it on your phone , it's easier .
[doctor] that works . and if you soak through a pad every hour for two hours in a row , or you feel dizzy or faint , go straight to the emergency room .
[patient] okay . should i take anything to slow the bleeding ?
[doctor] i'd rather not start anything until the ultrasound is back . tylenol is fine for the pelvic ache , up to one thousand milligrams three times a day .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] we'll see you back in two weeks , or sooner if the bleeding gets worse . and please ask your manager about lifting less during the next few weeks .
[patient] i'll try . the bakery is short staffed right now , so it's hard to say no .
[doctor] i understand . take care of yourself , nadine .
[patient] thank you , doctor rinaldi .

[doctor] hi , luis , i'm doctor radcliffe . it's nice to meet you . what's going on today ?
[patient] hey . i'm a roofer , and i fell off a ladder at work . my ankle is a mess . my regular doctor also wanted me to come in , because i think my psoriatic arthritis is flaring .
[doctor] okay . tell me what happened with the ladder first .
[patient] on november seventh i was on a twenty foot extension ladder at a house we were reroofing . i was carrying a bundle of shingles up , and the ladder slid sideways on the gutter . i came down on my right side , and my right foot twisted under me .
[doctor] oh no . did you hit your head ?
[patient] no , i landed on my shoulder and then my hip . my helmet was in the truck . i'm lucky .
[doctor] you are lucky . did you pass out at all , or feel dizzy ?
[patient] no , i was totally awake . i was just in a lot of pain .
[doctor] okay . where does it hurt most ?
[patient] the outside of my right ankle , and my shoulder a bit . the ankle is swollen up like a balloon .
[doctor] can you put any weight on it ?
[patient] barely . i hopped in on one foot . the guys from meridian bank drove me to urgent care , and they told me to come see you .
[doctor] okay . let me pull up your chart . your medical record number is mrn221891 , is that right ?
[patient] yes , that's me .
[doctor] good . you were seen at urgent care yesterday , correct ?
[patient] yeah . they took x-rays and said it's not broken , just a bad sprain . they gave me a boot and some ibuprofen .
[doctor] okay . now , how have your joints been over the last few weeks ?
[patient] they've been bad for about three weeks . my fingers are puffy in the morning , and my lower back is stiff for like an hour after i get up .
[doctor] when were you first diagnosed with psoriatic arthritis ?
[patient] in 2019 , i think . i had the skin patches on my elbows for years before that , and then the joints started .
[doctor] got it . are you on any medicine for it ?
[patient] i take a shot every two weeks . it's a biologic , the one with the pen .
[doctor] that's probably adalimumab . do you ever miss doses ?
[patient] sometimes , when we're working out of town and i'm sleeping in a motel .
[doctor] okay . any fevers , night sweats , or weight loss ?
[patient] no fevers . i've lost a little weight , but i think that's from being on the crew all summer .
[doctor] that's reasonable . any rashes or itchy patches right now ?
[patient] some on my elbows and behind my ears . nothing like before .
[doctor] okay , let me examine you . your blood pressure is one twenty two over seventy four and your heart rate is seventy six . your temperature is normal .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] i see swelling on the outside of the right ankle , with some bruising . press here , does it hurt ?
[patient] yes , right there , that's the spot .
[doctor] okay . the ligaments on the outside feel tender , but i don't feel a deformity . your achilles tendon feels fine , no pain there . can you wiggle your toes ?
[patient] yes .
[doctor] good . feel that ?
[patient] yes , it's all there .
[doctor] now raise your arm for me . does your shoulder hurt ?
[patient] a little , especially behind the shoulder .
[doctor] okay . make a fist for me .
[patient] they're tight . my pinky and my ring finger are swollen , they look like little sausages .
[doctor] i see that . dactylitis is what we call it when a whole finger swells like that . now bend forward for me .
[patient] it pulls a bit , but it's not terrible .
[doctor] okay . the x-ray from urgent care shows no fracture , just some soft tissue swelling .
[patient] that's good news , right ?
[doctor] it is . i'm going to diagnose you with a sprain of the ligaments on the outside of your right ankle , from the fall . for the joints , i want to check some labs , a c reactive protein and an esr . i'd also like a repeat x-ray of your hands .
[patient] okay . what do i do about the ankle ?
[doctor] keep the boot on , use crutches for a few days , and ice it twenty minutes at a time with the foot elevated above your heart . you'll start physical therapy in two weeks .
[patient] is it okay to keep taking ibuprofen ?
[doctor] for a short time , yes . i'd rather you use tylenol for the pain when you can , because ibuprofen can bother your stomach .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] and i'll increase your injection to every week for the next month , to see if we can calm the flare down .
[patient] every week ? that's going to be rough .
[doctor] i know . we'll see how you do . come back in four weeks , or sooner if the swelling gets worse or the foot goes numb .
[patient] got it . thanks , doctor radcliffe .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right ankle pain and swelling after a fall from an extension ladder, with recent worsening of psoriatic arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Luis Sandoval is a 23-year-old male with psoriatic arthritis on adalimumab who presents for evaluation of a right ankle injury and a flare of inflammatory arthritis. He was referred by his primary rheumatology clinic.

On November Seventh, he fell approximately 20 feet from a twenty foot extension ladder while carrying shingles at a residential reroofing job site. The ladder slid sideways on the gutter. He landed on his right side with the right foot inverted beneath him. He denies head strike or loss of consciousness. He was evaluated at urgent care the following day, where radiographs showed no fracture and he was given a walking boot and ibuprofen. [doctor] you are lucky . did you pass out at all , or feel dizzy ?
[patient] no , i was totally awake . i was just in a lot of pain .
[doctor] okay . where does it hurt most ?

[patient] barely . i hopped in on one foot . the guys from greenfield farms drove me to urgent care , and they told me to come see you .

[patient] yes , that's me .

[patient] yeah . they took x-rays and said it's not broken , just a bad sprain . they gave me a boot and some ibuprofen .
[doctor] okay . now , how have your joints been over the last few weeks ?

[patient] sometimes , when we're working out of town and i'm sleeping in a motel .
[doctor] okay . any fevers , night sweats , or weight loss ?
[patient] no fevers . i've lost a little weight , but i think that's from being on the crew all summer .

[doctor] okay . tell me what happened on the way .
[patient] i was almost at the courts when i stepped on a wet patch of concrete and my foot just shot out from under me . i went down hard on my right side . my knee twisted when i landed , and i heard a loud pop .
[doctor] oh no . did you hit your head ?
[patient] no , i put my hands out first . my palms are scraped up too , but my head is fine .
[doctor] did you pass out or feel dizzy at all ?
[patient] no . i was awake the whole time .
[doctor] okay . where is the pain now ?
[patient] inside the knee , mostly . it's really swollen . i could barely walk back to my car , and my friend had to drive me home .
[doctor] were you able to put weight on it after the fall ?
[patient] a little , but it felt like the knee was going to give out . it buckled a couple times when i went down the stairs at home .
[doctor] that's a classic sign . which knee is it ?
[patient] the right one . i've never had anything wrong with this knee before .
[doctor] okay . let me look at your chart . your medical record number is mrn472156 , correct ?
[patient] yes .
[doctor] good . i'll examine you now . your blood pressure is one eighteen over seventy and your pulse is seventy two .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] the knee is swollen with fluid , and there's a scrape on the front of your knee and on both palms . bend your knee for me . does it hurt ?
[patient] yes , it hurts a lot .
[doctor] okay . i'm going to press on the front of your shin and see if it slides forward .
[patient] ouch . yes , it moves .
[doctor] that's the anterior drawer test , and it's positive , which means the anterior cruciate ligament is likely torn . the lachman test is also positive .
[patient] the acl ? is that serious ?

[patient] will i need surgery ?

[patient] okay . i'm supposed to play in the tournament in aldervale next month .
[doctor] you'll need to skip that one . let's focus on getting you healthy .
[patient] ugh , okay .
[doctor] for pain you can use tylenol , one thousand milligrams up to three times a day . ice it twenty minutes at a time and keep it elevated .
[patient] will the crutches help ?
[doctor] yes , use crutches until you can walk without a limp . i'd also like you to wear a knee brace whenever you're on your feet .
[patient] okay . i grew up in aldervale and i still go back there to visit my parents every month . that's just down the road . could the mri be done there ?
[doctor] the mri can be done here in our imaging center , so you don't need to drive back there . i'll place the order today .
[patient] thank you . i'm also taking the bus from yakima to work , so the crutches are going to be a pain .
[doctor] i understand . i can give you a work note for two weeks , and we'll check your range of motion at the follow-up .
[patient] okay . thanks , doctor obrien .

[patient] hi . okay , so on january second it was raining pretty hard in the morning , but i still walked over to the courts at vista ridge to play pickleball with my team . the sidewalk was soaking wet .
[doctor] okay . tell me what happened on the way .
[patient] i was almost at the courts when i stepped on a wet patch of concrete and my foot just shot out from under me . i went down hard on my right side . my knee twisted when i landed , and i heard a loud pop .
[doctor] oh no . did you hit your head ?
[patient] no , i put my hands out first . my palms are scraped up too , but my head is fine .
[doctor] did you pass out or feel dizzy at all ?
[patient] no . i was awake the whole time .
[doctor] okay . where is the pain now ?
[patient] inside the knee , mostly . it's really swollen . i could barely walk back to my car , and my friend had to drive me home .
[doctor] were you able to put weight on it after the fall ?
[patient] a little , but it felt like the knee was going to give out . it buckled a couple times when i went down the stairs at home .
[doctor] that's a classic sign . which knee is it ?
[patient] the right one . i've never had anything wrong with this knee before .
[doctor] okay . let me look at your chart . your medical record number is mrn679118 , correct ?
[patient] yes .
[doctor] good . i'll examine you now . your blood pressure is one eighteen over seventy and your pulse is seventy two .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] the knee is swollen with fluid , and there's a scrape on the front of your knee and on both palms . bend your knee for me . does it hurt ?
[patient] yes , it hurts a lot .
[doctor] okay . i'm going to press on the front of your shin and see if it slides forward .
[patient] ouch . yes , it moves .
[doctor] that's the anterior drawer test , and it's positive , which means the anterior cruciate ligament is likely torn . the lachman test is also positive .
[patient] the acl ? is that serious ?
[doctor] it's a significant injury , but it's very treatable . we'll get an mri and an orthopedic consult .
[patient] will i need surgery ?
[doctor] possibly . if you want to return to pivoting sports like pickleball , a reconstruction is often recommended . but first we want the swelling down , and i'd like to see the mri .
[patient] okay . i'm supposed to play in the tournament in aldervale next month .
[doctor] you'll need to skip that one . let's focus on getting you healthy .
[patient] ugh , okay .
[doctor] for pain you can use tylenol , one thousand milligrams up to three times a day . ice it twenty minutes at a time and keep it elevated .
[patient] will the crutches help ?
[doctor] yes , use crutches until you can walk without a limp . i'd also like you to wear a knee brace whenever you're on your feet .
[patient] okay . i grew up in aldervale and i still go back there to visit my parents every month . that's just down the road . could the mri be done there ?
[doctor] the mri can be done here in our imaging center , so you don't need to drive back there . i'll place the order today .
[patient] thank you . i'm also taking the bus from billings to work , so the crutches are going to be a pain .
[doctor] i understand . i can give you a work note for two weeks , and we'll check your range of motion at the follow-up .
[patient] okay . thanks , doctor goldberg .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right knee pain and swelling after a slip on a wet sidewalk.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Marisol Achebe is a 25-year-old female who presents with right knee pain and swelling after a fall on January Second. She was walking to the courts at Vista Ridge to play recreational pickleball when she slipped on a wet sidewalk. She landed on her right side and felt her knee twist with an audible pop. She did not strike her head and denies loss of consciousness. She sustained abrasions to both palms. She was able to bear weight only partially and reports a sense of giving way, with two episodes of buckling on stairs at home.

She plays pickleball regularly, several times per week, and has no prior knee injuries.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

No prior knee injuries or surgeries. No chronic medical conditions.

MEDICATIONS

Acetaminophen as needed. Oral contraceptive.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Grew up in Aldervale and returns to visit her parents monthly. Commutes by bus from Billings to work.

IDENTIFICATION

Medical record number: mrn679118

PHYSICAL EXAM

Vitals: BP 118/70, HR 72, afebrile. Right knee with moderate effusion and abrasion over the anterior knee. Bilateral palm abrasions. Positive anterior drawer and Lachman tests on the right; no varus or valgus instability. Posterior drawer negative. Distal neurovascular status intact. Pain with flexion.

RESULTS

Plain radiographs of the right knee ordered to exclude fracture. MRI of the right knee ordered.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Suspected complete anterior cruciate ligament tear of the right knee from a slip-and-fall on a wet sidewalk. Abrasions of the right knee and both palms, cleansed and dressed.
2. MRI of the right knee and radiographs. Orthopedic sports medicine consultation after imaging.
3. Pain management with acetaminophen 1000 mg up to three times daily, ice, and elevation. Hinged knee brace and crutches until gait normalizes.
4. Work note for two weeks. Advised to avoid pickleball and pivoting activities pending evaluation.
5. Tetanus status to be confirmed given palm abrasions.

Return in one week for MRI review.

icd10_codes.description: Sprain of anterior cruciate ligament of right knee, initial encounter
Abrasion, right knee, initial encounter
Fall on same level from slipping, tripping and stumbling without subsequent striking against object, initial encounter
Sidewalk as the place of occurrence of the external cause
Other external cause status

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , simon . good to see you again . how have you been since the last visit ?
[patient] hey , doctor salazar . honestly , not as good as i want . i've been using the cpap about half the nights .
[doctor] okay . tell me more about that . what gets in the way ?
[patient] i travel a lot for work , and when i'm at a hotel the mask leaks and i wake up and take it off . and i'm so tired by the time i get home that i fall asleep on the couch without it .
[doctor] that's very common . what do you do for work ?
[patient] i'm a software engineer at evergreen assisted living , so most of my week is on video calls . it's not very physical .
[doctor] okay . how many hours do you actually sleep ?
[patient] maybe five and a half on a good night . on weekends i try to catch up , but then i feel worse .
[doctor] i see . do you nap during the day ?
[patient] sometimes in the car on the way home . i have to pull over once in a while . that scared me a little .
[doctor] that's important to tell me . please don't drive when you're drowsy . is your partner still noticing the snoring ?
[patient] yes . we just adopted twins , so now i'm up at night with the babies , and my wife says the snoring is still bad .
[doctor] congratulations . that's a big change . how loud is the snoring ?
[patient] loud . she says i stop breathing sometimes . she videoed me on her phone .
[doctor] that's helpful . let me ask about your routine . do you exercise ?
[patient] i swim at 5:45 every morning at the pool near our apartment in cheyenne , before work . it's the only time i get to myself .
[doctor] wow , that's early . how are you doing it on five hours ?
[patient] i do n't know . coffee . a lot of coffee .
[doctor] okay . let's look at your numbers . your blood pressure today is one thirty four over eighty six . that's a little higher than last time . and your weight is up two kilos since last year .
[patient] yeah , i've been eating out more since the new job .
[doctor] okay . your neck circumference looks larger than before . let me check your mouth and throat . any pain there ?
[patient] no pain .
[doctor] alright . the cpap download i got shows you're averaging about four hours a night . the apnea hypopnea index on your last study was twenty four , which is moderate , and the oxygen dropped to eighty six percent at the lowest .
[patient] that's bad , right ?
[doctor] it's moderate sleep apnea . the good news is it's very treatable , and we have options . your epworth score today is fourteen , which means you're quite sleepy during the day .
[patient] yeah . okay .
[doctor] let's go over your options . we can keep working on the cpap . we can change the mask to a nasal pillow mask , and i'd like you to try the humidifier at setting four . we can also repeat the sleep study as a titration study if the symptoms don't improve .
[patient] i've been trying the full face mask . it's uncomfortable .
[doctor] that's a good reason to switch . i'll send a referral to our sleep technician to refit the mask this week .
[patient] okay . do you have anything to help me sleep ?
[doctor] for insomnia , a short course of medicine can help . but i'd rather not give you a sedative with your sleep apnea . so we'll try cognitive behavioral therapy first . do you know what that involves ?
[patient] i think so . it's the sleep diary and the rules about getting out of bed ?
[doctor] exactly . and we can try melatonin at three milligrams , thirty minutes before bed . no alcohol after dinner .
[patient] i'll try the melatonin . i'm not much of a drinker anyway , maybe one beer on the weekend .
[doctor] okay . i also want to check your family history . any sleep problems or other conditions run in the family ?
[patient] my grandfather had parkinson's , and my dad has high blood pressure like me .
[doctor] okay . and your hobbies ? you seem like a busy person .
[patient] i restore vintage motorcycles in my garage . it's a fun escape . i'm working on a seventy one honda right now .
[doctor] that sounds like a lot of late nights . i'd like you to keep a sleep diary for two weeks , and bring the cpap data card to the next visit . we'll see you back in four weeks , and sooner if the snoring gets worse or you feel unsafe driving .
[patient] got it . i'm planning a trip to lisbon next month , is it okay if i bring the machine ?
[doctor] of course , bring it . just make sure you have the right adapter for the outlets there .
[patient] will do . thanks , doctor salazar .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up for obstructive sleep apnea with suboptimal CPAP adherence and insomnia symptoms.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Simon Bjornsson is a 26-year-old male with obstructive sleep apnea on CPAP and insomnia who presents for follow-up. He reports using CPAP about half of nights. Mask leak occurs when traveling for work, and the full face mask is uncomfortable, so he removes it during sleep. He falls asleep on the couch after returning home late.

He estimates five and a half hours of sleep on a good night. He has had episodes of drowsy driving, once requiring him to pull over, which he finds concerning. His partner reports loud snoring with witnessed apneas, recorded on video. He swims at 5:45 each morning before work. Weight has increased by approximately 2 kg since last year, which he attributes to restaurant meals since starting a new job. He denies pain in the neck or throat.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

Obstructive sleep apnea diagnosed on polysomnography. Insomnia. No known cardiac disease.

FAMILY HISTORY

Grandfather with Parkinson's disease. Father with hypertension.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Software engineer, primarily on video calls. Lives in Cheyenne with his wife and recently adopted twins. Alcohol: occasional, one beer on weekends. Restores vintage motorcycles as a hobby in his garage. Recent travel for work. Plans international travel to Lisbon next month.

MEDICATIONS

CPAP therapy nightly. Melatonin 3 mg, to start.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Vitals: BP 134/86. Neck circumference increased. Oropharynx examined, no pain.

DATA

CPAP download reviewed: average use approximately four hours per night. Most recent polysomnography apnea-hypopnea index 24 events per hour (moderate), with nadir oxygen saturation 86 percent. Epworth Sleepiness Scale score 14 today.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Moderate obstructive sleep apnea with suboptimal CPAP adherence and mask intolerance. Referral to sleep technician for mask refitting to nasal pillow interface. Humidifier increased to setting four. Repeat titration study if symptoms persist.
2. Insomnia. Referral for cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia, sleep hygiene education, and a two-week sleep diary. Melatonin 3 mg 30 minutes before bed. Avoid sedative hypnotics given untreated sleep apnea.
3. Hypertension, elevated today at 134/86; monitor at home.
4. Sleep deprivation with daytime sleepiness and drowsy driving; counseled to avoid driving when drowsy.
5. Weight gain of about 2 kg since last year, counseled on nutrition.

Return in four weeks with CPAP data card, sooner for worsening snoring or unsafe driving.

Insomnia, unspecified
Essential (primary) hypertension

dialogue:
[doctor] good afternoon , rashad . how have you been since we last saw each other ?
[patient] oh , same old , doctor abernethy . some days are fine and some days i just ca n't get out of the chair .
[doctor] i'm sorry to hear that . tell me about a typical day .
[patient] i get up around six , make my coffee , and sit by the window . the crossword helps for about an hour . then the afternoon is long .
[doctor] how is your appetite and your sleep ?
[patient] i'm eating maybe half of what i used to . i wake up at three in the morning and i ca n't get back to sleep .
[doctor] okay . and your mood , how would you rate it on a scale from one to ten ?
[patient] maybe a four . on the good days it's a six .
[doctor] okay . i know your wife passed away last year . how are you holding up with that ?
[patient] it's been about fourteen months now . people keep saying it gets easier , but it does n't feel like that .
[doctor] that's a lot of grief to carry . do you still have thoughts of hurting yourself , or of not wanting to be here ?
[patient] no , no . i'd never do that . i think about her a lot , that's all . the anniversary was september second , and that was hard .
[doctor] i'm glad to hear it . how often do you see your family ?
[patient] denise calls every evening around seven . she drives over on sundays . she worries too much , honestly .
[doctor] she cares about you . you worked at a bank for a long time , right ?
[patient] yes , i was a loan officer at tri-county ems for thirty one years . i still have the habit of checking everyone's paperwork .
[doctor] that's a good habit . now , tell me about your memory . have you noticed more trouble finding words , or losing track of things ?
[patient] a little . i misplaced my keys twice this week , and i ca n't remember the name of the lady at the pharmacy . but my daughter says everybody does that .
[doctor] it's common . we'll do a short memory test today . let's start with the clock drawing .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] your scores are a bit lower than last time , but not dramatically . you got twenty three out of thirty on the screen today .
[patient] is that bad ?
[doctor] it's in the mild range . the memory changes and the mood symptoms can overlap , which is why we're watching both closely .
[patient] i see .
[doctor] okay . let's look at your medicines . you're still taking the sertraline one hundred milligrams every morning ?
[patient] yes . and the blood pressure pill , lisinopril , twenty milligrams .
[doctor] how many days a week do you miss a dose ?
[patient] maybe once a week . i forget the evening pill .
[doctor] okay . let's use a pill box with a reminder alarm . have you taken any sleeping pills , or anything over the counter ?
[patient] just a tylenol now and then for my back .
[doctor] good . any alcohol ?
[patient] a glass of wine with dinner , that's all . my doctor from years ago said it's fine .
[doctor] okay . let's check your vitals . blood pressure one thirty eight over eighty two . pulse seventy four , and your weight is one hundred seventy pounds , down about eight pounds since the spring .
[patient] that's the not eating .
[doctor] it probably is . let me examine you . any tremor in your hands ?
[patient] a little when i hold a cup . my brother had crohn's disease , and i never had any of that , but i get some stiffness in the shoulders .
[doctor] okay . your gait looks steady . strength is normal in both arms and legs . no tremor at rest .
[patient] good .
[doctor] let's talk about the plan . i'd like to increase the sertraline to one hundred fifty milligrams daily , and we'll recheck in four weeks .
[patient] okay . will that make me sleepy ?
[doctor] it can at first . take it with breakfast . i'd also like you to try the senior center on tuesdays , where they do art and music . and i'll send a referral for counseling .
[patient] i used to volunteer at the library on tuesdays . maybe i'll try the center instead .
[doctor] that sounds great . the counseling is a grief group on thursdays at st. agnes parish .
[patient] st. agnes parish ? my wife and i went there for years .
[doctor] then it's a good fit . i'll see you in four weeks . and call the clinic right away if you have any thoughts of hurting yourself .
[patient] i will . thank you , doctor abernethy .

Brother with Crohn's disease.

Sertraline 100 mg every morning, to increase to 150 mg daily. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. Missing the evening pill about once weekly.

4. Unintentional weight loss. Monitor weight at each visit.

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , siobhan . good to see you . how have you been feeling since the last visit ?
[patient] better than in the spring . i'm still tired by the afternoon , but the walks help a bit .
[doctor] okay . let's go over the labs from last week . your hemoglobin came back at eleven point two , which is up from nine point eight .
[patient] good . is that the iron working ?
[doctor] it is . your ferritin is still low , at fourteen , so we want to keep the iron going for a few more months .
[patient] okay . i take it every morning with orange juice , like you said .
[doctor] and not with your tea or your milk ?
[patient] right , i've been good about that . except on weekends .
[doctor] that's fine . now , your periods . are they still heavy ?
[patient] a little lighter since i started the pill . i still change a pad every two hours on the first day , but it's not as bad as before .
[doctor] okay . when did you first find out you had anemia ?
[patient] 2020 , when i gave blood at the drive and they said my iron was low . i was shocked .
[doctor] that's a common story . what were you doing back then ?
[patient] i was working the front desk at metro transit , and i was doing a lot of double shifts .
[doctor] okay . any new bruising or nosebleeds ?
[patient] no , nothing new . my gums bleed a little when i floss , but that's it .
[doctor] alright . let's check you over . your blood pressure is one eleven over sixty eight , and your pulse is seventy eight . i don't see any pallor today , your color looks better .
[patient] thanks .
[doctor] your spleen is not enlarged , and your lymph nodes are normal . your heart sounds regular .
[patient] great .
[doctor] your last iron infusion was on september ninth , correct ?
[patient] yes , that's right . i felt a little flushed for about an hour afterward , but the nurse was great .
[doctor] that's a known side effect . are you still planning to finish the course of iron tablets ?
[patient] yes . i'll take them for three more months , then come back for blood work .
[doctor] perfect . i'd like to start you on a low dose of folic acid as well , one milligram daily .
[patient] okay . anything else i should know ?
[doctor] keep the iron away from calcium supplements , and eat foods with vitamin c . you'll get constipated sometimes , so drink plenty of water and get some fiber .
[patient] i do get constipated . okay .
[doctor] i'll see you back in six weeks with repeat labs . if your bleeding gets heavier , or you feel faint , call us right away .
[patient] i will . thanks , doctor petrov .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up for iron deficiency anemia with heavy menstrual bleeding.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Siobhan Zhang is a 30-year-old female with iron deficiency anemia diagnosed in 2020 after a blood donation screening, who presents for follow-up. She reports ongoing fatigue in the afternoons, improved with daily walks. Menstrual bleeding is lighter on combined oral contraceptive, but she still requires a pad change every two hours on the first day of menses. She reports gum bleeding with flossing. She denies melena, hematochezia, new bruising, or epistaxis.

She takes oral iron every morning with orange juice, with occasional lapses on weekends. She has intermittent constipation.

Work history includes front desk responsibilities at Metro Transit, with frequent double shifts at the time of diagnosis.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

Iron deficiency anemia. No known bleeding disorder.

MEDICATIONS

Ferrous sulfate tablets daily. Combined oral contraceptive. Folic acid 1 mg daily, newly started.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Vitals: BP 111/68, pulse 78. No conjunctival pallor. Spleen not palpable. Lymph nodes not enlarged. Heart regular rate and rhythm.

RESULTS

Hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, up from 9.8 g/dL. Ferritin 14 ng/mL, still low.

Last IV iron infusion on September Ninth, tolerated with transient flushing.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Iron deficiency anemia with improving hemoglobin on oral iron. Continue ferrous sulfate for three additional months, then repeat CBC, ferritin, and iron studies. Folic acid 1 mg daily started. Counseled to take iron on an empty stomach with vitamin C and to separate it from calcium.
2. Heavy menstrual bleeding, improved on combined oral contraceptive. Return precautions reviewed for increased bleeding or presyncope.
3. Constipation related to oral iron; fluids and fiber advised.

Follow-up in six weeks with repeat labs.

[patient] no , just the usual . i take my blood pressure pill in the morning and that's it .

[patient] no , my breathing is fine . my throat feels a little scratchy , that's all .
[doctor] good . how soon after eating did the hives start ?

[doctor] i see . did you have any vomiting , diarrhea , or stomach cramps ?
[patient] a little stomach upset . i felt queasy for an hour or so , then it settled .
[doctor] okay . tell me about your allergies . do you have hay fever or asthma ?
[patient] i have hay fever in the spring , and i take a pill for it . and i've been wheezing a little at night since we got the cats .
[doctor] tell me about the cats .
[patient] we took in three rescue cats last spring . my wife could n't say no . they're in the house all day , and they sleep on my bed . my nose runs all the time now .
[doctor] okay . so the cats are probably making your nose and your breathing worse . what did you do for work ?
[patient] i was a mail carrier for thirty four years , so i'm used to being outside in all kinds of weather . i still restore pocket watches at my kitchen table , too .
[doctor] that's a long career . have you had hives before ?
[patient] once , when i was about forty , after taking an antibiotic . the doctor said it was penicillin . i had to stop it right away .
[doctor] okay . that's important to know , so we need to note the penicillin reaction too .
[patient] yeah . i'd like that on the record .
[doctor] let me check you now . your blood pressure is one forty two over eighty eight . your pulse is eighty four . your temperature is ninety eight point two .
[patient] that's a little high , is it ?
[doctor] it's higher than we'd like . the nurse will recheck it before you leave .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] let's look at your skin . i can see raised welts on the chest and across the back . they're pink , and they blanch when i press . your lips look a bit puffy , but your tongue is normal .
[patient] it's the itching that's driving me crazy .
[doctor] i know . your lungs sound clear , with no wheezing today . that's good .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so this looks like hives from the shrimp , which is a food reaction . it's called acute urticaria . shellfish allergy is very common in men your age .
[patient] so i'm allergic to shellfish now ?

[patient] okay . will that make me jittery ?

[patient] i do n't have one . should i get one ?

[patient] i will .
[doctor] i'd also like you to keep the cats out of the bedroom , and wash your hands after you play with them .
[patient] that's going to be hard . they're family now .
[doctor] i understand . the nurse will also need a callback number so she can follow up with you . what's the best number to reach you at ?
[patient] it's 762-323-9005 . that's the house phone . my cell does n't get signal in the basement , so use the house one .
[doctor] got it . the nurse will call you within two days with the blood test results and your appointment time .
[patient] okay . i'm going to the volunteer dinner at the fire hall next week , so i'd like to know what to avoid .
[doctor] you should avoid all shellfish there , and ask the cooks to confirm what's in the food .
[patient] will do . that's what i'm planning .
[doctor] come back to the clinic if the hives spread , or if your lips or tongue start to swell , or if you feel any tightness in your throat . call nine one one right away in that case .
[patient] okay . i'll remember that . thank you , doctor moreau .

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

Hypertension. Seasonal allergic rhinitis. Prior penicillin-associated urticaria.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Retired mail carrier after a thirty-four-year career. Restores pocket watches at his kitchen table. Lives with his wife and three rescue cats. Best callback number: 762-323-9005 (house line; cell phone has poor reception at home).

Antihypertensive medication every morning. Seasonal oral antihistamine. Cetirizine 10 mg twice daily to start.

Vitals: BP 142/88, pulse 84, temperature 98.2 F. Urticarial wheals on the chest and back that blanch with pressure. Mild lip edema, tongue normal. Lungs clear without wheezing. Nasal mucosa boggy with clear discharge.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Scaly scalp and forearm patches, and a waxy brown lesion on the upper back. Telehealth follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Marcus Montgomery is a 82-year-old male who presents by synchronous video visit for evaluation of rough, scaly patches on the scalp and bilateral forearms, present since the summer. His daughter, Giovanni, assists with the device. The scalp lesion is mildly pruritic and has bled once after scratching with a comb. The forearm lesions feel rough to touch. He also has a long-standing waxy brown lesion on the upper back that the family has asked him to have evaluated.

Lifetime sun exposure is extensive. He worked outdoors for nearly forty years, including roofing and crew supervision for a landscaping company, and spent several years loading trucks at a warehouse with the dock open to the sun. He currently gardens daily in his backyard and does not use a hat or sunscreen.

Video quality was limited by intermittent connectivity; the examination was performed by camera review with patient repositioning.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

Prior dermatology care at Blue Ridge Dermatology with last visit in 2021; not followed there since relocation. No known history of skin cancer. Cataract, awaiting surgical evaluation.

MEDICATIONS

None listed for dermatologic conditions.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Retired. Relies on his daughter for transportation and for picking up medications. Does not drive pending cataract surgery.

EXAM (VIDEO)

Scalp: multiple flat, scaly, erythematous patches over the vertex and crown with adherent scale. Bilateral dorsal forearms: rough, scaly papules. Upper back: waxy, stuck-on, brown papule.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Actinic keratoses of the scalp and bilateral forearms, consistent with chronic cumulative sun exposure. Topical fluorouracil cream applied once or twice daily to affected areas for two to three weeks. Counseled on expected erythema, crusting, and burning. Prescription sent to Tidewater Seafood for pickup the following afternoon.
2. Seborrheic keratosis of the upper back. Benign appearance. Cryotherapy offered; biopsy if the lesion changes in color or grows rapidly.
3. Photoprotection counseled: broad spectrum sunscreen SPF 30 or higher daily, wide brim hat, and long sleeves.
4. Pruritus of the scalp: lukewarm water, mild soap, and emollient after bathing.

Return to video visit in four weeks. Patient instructed to call the office for bleeding that does not stop or for open sores.

[doctor] hi , ignacio . i'm doctor villanueva . you're back with us in the emergency department again . what's going on today ?

[patient] yes , that's me .
[doctor] good . when did the pain start ?
[patient] about six hours ago . i was at the gym and it just came on . it's coming in waves , and it goes down into my groin .
[doctor] okay . does it burn when you urinate , or do you see blood in your urine ?
[patient] a little burning , and yes , my urine looked pink this morning .
[doctor] okay . any fever or chills ?

[doctor] alright . any nausea or vomiting ?
[patient] i threw up once in the parking lot . that's why i came straight here .
[doctor] that's good that you came in . how much water have you been drinking ?
[patient] not enough , honestly . i've been busy with the new job , and i forget .
[doctor] okay . now tell me about your sugar . when did you last check your blood glucose ?
[patient] this morning . it was two hundred and eighteen . i took my metformin and my glipizide like always .
[doctor] that's high . how often are you checking it ?
[patient] twice a day , usually . sometimes i skip the evening one .
[doctor] okay . and your blood pressure medicine ?
[patient] lisinopril , ten milligrams every morning .
[doctor] alright . let's get your vitals . your blood pressure is one forty four over ninety . your heart rate is ninety eight . your temperature is ninety eight point nine .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] let me examine you . does it hurt more on the right side or the left ?
[patient] right side , definitely . it's like a knife going in .
[doctor] okay . there's marked tenderness over the right flank , and the abdomen is soft with no rebound .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] i'd like to check your urine and some blood work . we'll get a ct scan of your abdomen and pelvis to look for the stone .
[patient] the last time they found a stone it was almost one centimeter . i thought the lithotripsy took care of it .
[doctor] it did for that one , but you've had another episode since . let's see what the scan shows .
[patient] okay . whatever you need .
[doctor] your glucose on the blood work is two hundred and sixty one , and your creatinine is one point one . so your kidneys are working well .
[patient] that's a relief .
[doctor] the ct shows a four millimeter stone in the lower part of the right ureter , with some mild swelling of the kidney . it's moving , which is good , but it's causing the pain .
[patient] so it just needs to pass ?
[doctor] most stones this size pass on their own with fluids and pain control . i'd like you to give it a few days .
[patient] okay . i'm supposed to be at a wedding in durango this weekend . is it okay to travel ?
[doctor] i'd rather you stay close to a bathroom for the next few days . if the pain becomes uncontrollable or you develop a fever , you need to come back right away .
[patient] my trip to mount rainier got canceled because of this , so at least i'm not flying anywhere .
[doctor] for pain you can take ibuprofen , four hundred milligrams every six hours with food , and use tamsulosin at night to help the stone move .

[patient] i do drink a lot of soda at work . i'll try to switch to seltzer .
[doctor] that's a good swap . we also want to check a hemoglobin a1c next week to see your average sugar over three months .
[patient] okay . i grew up in harlow ridge , and my mother still lives there . i might go out there for a few days once the stone passes .
[doctor] that's nice . let me know if the pain changes . and if you end up at another hospital , make sure they have your records .
[patient] will do . thanks , doctor villanueva .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Recurrent right flank pain consistent with ureteral calculus, with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Ignacio Szymanski is a 43-year-old male returning to the emergency department with recurrent right flank pain. Onset approximately six hours prior to arrival while exercising, with colicky waves radiating to the right groin. Associated dysuria and gross hematuria this morning. One episode of emesis in the parking lot. He denies fever. He reports suboptimal oral fluid intake.

He has a prior history of nephrolithiasis treated with lithotripsy. Fasting home blood glucose this morning was 218 mg/dL. He reports taking metformin and glipizide as prescribed, but skips the evening glucose check.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Hypertension. Nephrolithiasis with prior lithotripsy. Family history of Barrett's esophagus in a cousin.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Grew up in Harlow Ridge; mother still lives there. Planned trip to Mount Rainier canceled. Drinks sugar-sweetened soda daily at work.

IDENTIFICATION

Medical record number: mrn824714

MEDICATIONS

Metformin, increased to 1000 mg twice daily. Glipizide. Lisinopril 10 mg every morning. Ibuprofen 400 mg every six hours with food as needed. Tamsulosin nightly, new.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Vitals: BP 144/90, HR 98, T 98.9 F. Abdomen soft, nondistended, no rebound. Marked tenderness over the right flank and costovertebral angle.

RESULTS

Urinalysis positive for blood and glucose. Serum glucose 261 mg/dL. Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL. CT abdomen and pelvis without contrast: 4 mm calculus in the distal right ureter with mild right hydronephrosis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right ureteral calculus, 4 mm, with mild hydronephrosis. Hydration, ibuprofen and tamsulosin for analgesia and stone passage. Strain urine. Return precautions: uncontrolled pain, fever, or inability to keep fluids down.
2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia. Metformin increased to 1000 mg twice daily. Home glucose checks twice daily. HbA1c next week. Reduce sugar-sweetened beverages.
3. Hypertension, BP 144/90. Continue lisinopril; recheck at follow-up.

Follow-up with primary care in one week.

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , ingrid . how are you doing today ?
[patient] oh , i've been better , doctor hutchinson . my wrist is killing me .
[doctor] i'm sorry to hear that . i see you brought your daughter with you .
[patient] yes , this is raymond . she drove me over because i ca n't really use my right hand right now .
[doctor] hi , raymond , nice to meet you . so tell me what happened .
[patient] well , yesterday morning i was walking back to my car after getting groceries , and i slipped on the ice in the parking lot at allied waste services . it was one of those patches you ca n't see , you know , black ice . my feet just went right out from under me .
[doctor] oh no . and how did you land ?
[patient] i put my right hand out to catch myself , and i landed right on it . i heard kind of a crunch .
[doctor] okay . did you hit your head at all when you fell ?
[patient] no , no , i did n't hit my head . my bottom hurt a little but that's fine now . it's really the wrist .
[doctor] okay , good . did you pass out or feel dizzy before you slipped ?
[patient] no , it was just the ice . i felt fine before .
[doctor] alright . and what did you do after you fell ?
[patient] a young man helped me up and put my groceries in the car . i drove home with my left hand , which was probably not smart . and then i put ice on it and took some tylenol .
[doctor] did the tylenol help ?
[patient] a little bit . it's still throbbing though . i'd say it's about a seven out of ten .
[doctor] okay . any numbness or tingling in your fingers ?
[patient] a little tingling in my thumb and first finger last night , but it seems better this morning .
[doctor] okay . and the swelling , has that gotten worse ?
[patient] it's pretty puffy . my daughter said it looks like a fork .
[patient] yeah , mom , it kind of bends funny at the wrist .
[doctor] okay , we'll take a good look at that . now , before we go further , i see that you have a history of high blood pressure . how has that been going ?
[patient] it's been okay . i take my lisinopril every morning , ten milligrams . i check it at home sometimes and it's usually around one thirty over eighty .
[doctor] good . any headaches , chest pain , shortness of breath ?
[patient] no , none of that .
[doctor] okay . and are you still working at the library ?
[patient] oh no , i'm a retired librarian now . but i still volunteer to read to the kids on saturdays . that's what i'm worried about , i want to be able to turn the pages .
[doctor] we'll get you back to that . any history of osteoporosis or any bone density scan ?
[patient] i had one a long time ago , i do n't remember what it said .
[doctor] okay . let's go ahead and do a physical exam . your blood pressure today is one forty two over eighty four , which is a little up , but you're in pain , so i'm not too worried about it . heart rate is eighty eight .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] let me look at your right wrist . i can see there's significant swelling over the distal forearm and there is a dorsal angulation , what we call a dinner fork deformity . does it hurt when i press here ?
[patient] ouch , yes , that hurts a lot .
[doctor] okay , there's tenderness over the distal radius . how about here on the ulnar side ?
[patient] a little , not as much .
[doctor] can you wiggle your fingers for me ?
[patient] yes , it hurts but i can .
[doctor] good . can you feel me touching each finger ?
[patient] yes .
[doctor] okay , sensation is intact . your fingers are pink and the capillary refill is brisk . i can feel your radial pulse . your elbow and your shoulder move fine without pain ?
[patient] yes , those are fine .
[doctor] okay . we got an x-ray of the right wrist before i came in . let me pull that up . so the x-ray shows a fracture of the distal radius , right about an inch above the wrist joint , and the broken piece is tilted backwards . this is what we call a colles fracture . it does not go into the joint , and the ulna looks okay .
[patient] so it's broken .
[doctor] it is broken , yes . the good news is it's a closed fracture , the skin is n't broken , and your nerves and blood flow look good .
[patient] okay . what do we do about it ?
[doctor] so , because it's angulated , i'd like to do a closed reduction , which means we numb the area and gently put the bone back into a better position , and then we put you in a splint . we'll get another x-ray after that to make sure it's lined up .
[patient] will i need surgery ?
[doctor] possibly not . if the bone stays in good position , we can treat it in a cast for about six weeks . if it slips , we'd talk to the orthopedic surgeon about a plate . i'm going to refer you to orthopedics to see you within a week either way .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] for pain you can continue tylenol , up to one thousand milligrams three times a day . i'd avoid ibuprofen for now with your blood pressure . keep the arm elevated above your heart and ice it twenty minutes at a time .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] and because you broke your wrist from a simple fall , i'd like to order a dexa scan to check your bone density .
[patient] that makes sense .
[doctor] for the high blood pressure , let's continue the lisinopril ten milligrams daily , and i want you to keep checking it at home . if it stays above one forty once the pain settles , let me know .
[patient] i will .
[doctor] and please , be careful on the ice . wear shoes with good grips , and maybe have raymond do the grocery runs for a while .
[patient] she's already offered .
[doctor] perfect . any questions for me ?
[patient] no , i think that's it . thank you , doctor .
[doctor] you're welcome . the nurse will be in to get you ready for the reduction .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right wrist pain after a fall.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Ingrid Weatherby is a 58-year-old female with a history of hypertension who presents for evaluation of right wrist pain. She is accompanied today by her daughter, Raymond.

Yesterday morning, the patient was walking to her car when she slipped on black ice in a parking lot and fell onto her outstretched right hand. She heard a crunch at the time of injury. She denies head strike, loss of consciousness, or presyncope. She has been using ice and Tylenol with minimal relief and rates her pain as 7/10. She reports transient tingling in the thumb and index finger overnight, which has improved. Her daughter notes a deformity of the wrist.

Regarding her hypertension, she takes lisinopril 10 mg daily. Home blood pressure readings are around 130/80. She denies headaches, chest pain, or shortness of breath.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Retired librarian.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Vitals: BP 142/84, HR 88.
Right Wrist: Significant swelling of the distal forearm with dorsal angulation (dinner fork deformity). Tenderness to palpation over the distal radius. Mild tenderness over the ulnar side. Finger motion intact but painful. Sensation intact in all digits. Capillary refill brisk. Radial pulse palpable. Elbow and shoulder with full painless range of motion.

RESULTS

X-ray of the right wrist demonstrates an extra-articular fracture of the distal radius with dorsal angulation, consistent with a Colles fracture. The ulna is intact.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Closed Colles fracture of the right distal radius.
- Closed reduction under local anesthesia and placement of a sugar-tong splint today, followed by post-reduction x-ray.
- Referral to orthopedics within 1 week.
- Tylenol 1000 mg three times daily as needed for pain. Avoid NSAIDs.
- Elevation and ice.
- DEXA scan ordered to evaluate bone density given fracture after a low-energy fall.

2. Hypertension.
- Mildly elevated today in the setting of pain.
- Continue lisinopril 10 mg daily and home blood pressure monitoring.

The patient was counseled on fall prevention in icy conditions. She understands and agrees with the plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right wrist pain after a fall.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Gabriela Isaacson is a 62-year-old female with a history of hypertension who presents for evaluation of right wrist pain. She is accompanied today by her daughter, Phillip.

Yesterday morning, the patient was walking to her car when she slipped on black ice in a parking lot and fell onto her outstretched right hand. She heard a crunch at the time of injury. She denies head strike, loss of consciousness, or presyncope. She has been using ice and Tylenol with minimal relief and rates her pain as 7/10. She reports transient tingling in the thumb and index finger overnight, which has improved. Her daughter notes a deformity of the wrist.

Regarding her hypertension, she takes lisinopril 10 mg daily. Home blood pressure readings are around 130/80. She denies headaches, chest pain, or shortness of breath.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Retired librarian.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Vitals: BP 142/84, HR 88.
Right Wrist: Significant swelling of the distal forearm with dorsal angulation (dinner fork deformity). Tenderness to palpation over the distal radius. Mild tenderness over the ulnar side. Finger motion intact but painful. Sensation intact in all digits. Capillary refill brisk. Radial pulse palpable. Elbow and shoulder with full painless range of motion.

RESULTS

X-ray of the right wrist demonstrates an extra-articular fracture of the distal radius with dorsal angulation, consistent with a Colles fracture. The ulna is intact.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Closed Colles fracture of the right distal radius.
- Closed reduction under local anesthesia and placement of a sugar-tong splint today, followed by post-reduction x-ray.
- Referral to orthopedics within 1 week.
- Tylenol 1000 mg three times daily as needed for pain. Avoid NSAIDs.
- Elevation and ice.
- DEXA scan ordered to evaluate bone density given fracture after a low-energy fall.

2. Hypertension.
- Mildly elevated today in the setting of pain.
- Continue lisinopril 10 mg daily and home blood pressure monitoring.

The patient was counseled on fall prevention in icy conditions. She understands and agrees with the plan.

dialogue:
[doctor] good afternoon , mr . petrov . i'm doctor haddad .
[patient] hey , doc . call me hamid .
[doctor] alright , hamid . i see you came in on crutches . what happened ?
[patient] so , i'm kind of embarrassed . on june fifth i was up on a ladder cleaning the gutters on the back of the house , and the ladder just kind of slid out sideways . i fell off the ladder and landed on my left heel on the patio stones in the backyard .
[doctor] ouch . how high up were you ?
[patient] maybe ten , twelve feet . i was on the second to last rung , which i know you're not supposed to do .
[doctor] did you land on both feet or just the left ?
[patient] mostly the left . the right one kind of touched down after . then i fell over onto my side .
[doctor] did you hit your head or black out ?
[patient] no , my wife gustavo came running out and i was awake the whole time . i just could n't put any weight on the left foot .
[doctor] okay . any pain in your back or neck ?
[patient] my lower back was a little sore that night but it's fine now . it's really the heel .
[doctor] alright . and how has the pain been ?
[patient] it's bad . like an eight out of ten when i try to stand on it . the whole heel swelled up and it's purple on both sides now .
[doctor] what have you been taking for it ?
[patient] ibuprofen , like six hundred milligrams a couple times a day , and keeping it up on pillows .
[doctor] any numbness or tingling in your foot or toes ?
[patient] no , i can feel everything .
[doctor] okay , good . let me ask you about your other stuff . i see you have high cholesterol . are you still taking the atorvastatin ?
[patient] yeah , forty milligrams at night . i have n't missed any .
[doctor] any muscle aches from it ?
[patient] no , nothing like that .
[doctor] good . your last lipid panel was a few months ago and your ldl was one twenty two , which is better than before but still a bit above where we want it .
[patient] yeah , i've been trying to cut back on the fried stuff .
[doctor] alright , we'll keep working on that . what do you do for work ?
[patient] i teach chemistry at the high school here in bangor . so i'm on my feet all day .
[doctor] that's going to be a challenge for a while . let me take a look . go ahead and lie back . okay , i'm looking at the left foot . there's marked swelling around the heel , and there's ecchymosis on both the medial and lateral sides of the hindfoot . does it hurt when i squeeze here ?
[patient] yes ! yes , that hurts .
[doctor] sorry . so you have a positive heel squeeze test , tenderness over the calcaneus . how about over the ankle bones here ?
[patient] a little , but not like the heel .
[doctor] okay . can you move your toes ?
[patient] yes .
[doctor] good . your dorsalis pedis pulse is strong and your sensation is intact on the top and bottom of the foot . the skin is intact , no blisters yet . i'm going to press on your lower back now .
[patient] no , that does n't really hurt .
[doctor] okay , no midline tenderness of the spine . and the right foot looks normal .

[patient] okay .
[doctor] for the cholesterol , let's continue the atorvastatin forty milligrams and recheck a lipid panel in three months .
[patient] sounds good .
[doctor] and maybe hire someone for the gutters next time .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right ankle injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Yvonne Jablonski is a 84-year-old female with a history of asthma who presents today for evaluation of a right ankle injury.

Yesterday morning, the patient was running on the sidewalk when she tripped on a curb, inverting her right ankle, and fell. She felt a pop at the time of the injury. She was able to limp home but developed significant swelling. She also sustained minor abrasions to her palms. She has been treating her symptoms with ice, an ACE wrap, and Advil with mild improvement. She rates her pain as 3/10 at rest and 6-7/10 with weight bearing. She reports a remote right ankle sprain in high school. She runs 4 to 5 days per week. She works as a dental hygienist.

Her asthma is well controlled. She uses her albuterol inhaler approximately 1 to 2 times per week, mostly before exercise or in cold weather. She denies nocturnal symptoms, emergency room visits, or steroid courses in the past year.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right ankle pain and swelling.
Skin: Reports abrasions of the palms.
Respiratory: Denies nocturnal cough or wheezing.

PHYSICAL EXAM

MSK: Examination of the right ankle: Lateral ankle swelling with early ecchymosis along the lateral foot. Tenderness to palpation over the anterior talofibular ligament. No tenderness at the posterior edge or tip of the lateral malleolus, the medial malleolus, the base of the fifth metatarsal, or the navicular. Mild laxity on anterior drawer with a firm endpoint. Distal pulses intact. Sensation intact.
SKIN: Small superficial abrasions of the bilateral palms, clean.

RESULTS

X-rays of the right ankle were obtained and reviewed today. No evidence of fracture. Ankle mortise intact. Lateral soft tissue swelling.

ASSESSMENT

1. Right ankle sprain, likely anterior talofibular ligament.
2. Mild intermittent asthma, well controlled.

PLAN

1. Right ankle sprain: Rest, ice, compression, and elevation. Air stirrup ankle brace when ambulating. Advil 600 mg every 8 hours with food as needed. Referral to physical therapy for range of motion, strengthening, and balance training. Gradual return to running in 3 to 4 weeks as tolerated.
2. Asthma: Continue albuterol 2 puffs before exercise or as needed. Refill sent.

INSTRUCTIONS

The patient will follow up in 3 weeks.

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , valeria , i'm doctor kowalski , one of the orthopedic doctors here . how are you doing ?
[patient] hi . honestly not great , my knee is pretty messed up .
[doctor] i'm sorry . i read the note from urgent care , but i'd like to hear it from you . what happened ?
[patient] so i was skiing up at indian river lagoon on saturday . it was the last run of the day , i was a little tired , and i caught an edge on an icy patch coming down a blue run . my skis went in different directions and i fell , and my right ski did n't release from the binding . so my leg kind of twisted underneath me while i was going down .
[doctor] okay . so your knee twisted with your foot planted in the ski .
[patient] yeah , exactly . and i felt a pop in my knee , like a real pop , and it hurt a lot right away .
[doctor] were you able to ski down ?
[patient] no , ski patrol brought me down in the toboggan . it was humiliating .
[doctor] it happens to a lot of people . did the knee swell up ?
[patient] within like an hour it was huge . ski patrol gave me ice and a knee immobilizer and i went to the urgent care in town .
[doctor] okay . and they got x-rays there , i see . since then , how's it been ?
[patient] it's still swollen , i ca n't straighten it all the way , and it feels like it's going to give out when i try to walk without the crutches .
[doctor] okay , that feeling of the knee giving way is important . any locking or catching ?
[patient] not really locking . it just feels unstable .
[doctor] okay . any numbness in your foot ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] what have you been taking for pain ?
[patient] naproxen , the over the counter one , two in the morning and two at night .
[doctor] alright . any other medical problems ?
[patient] no , i'm pretty healthy . i do n't take anything regularly except birth control pills .
[doctor] okay . have you ever hurt this knee before ?
[patient] never .
[doctor] and what do you do for work ?
[patient] i'm a software engineer , so i sit at a desk . i'm from erie , so we drove out for a long weekend with my book club . it's an annual thing .
[doctor] that sounds fun , minus the knee . okay , let me examine you . go ahead and lie back . i'm looking at your right knee , there's a moderate effusion , there's a lot of fluid in the knee . you're lacking about ten degrees of full extension and you can bend it to about ninety degrees . does it hurt when i push here along the joint line on the inside ?
[patient] a little .
[doctor] and the outside ?
[patient] yeah , that's more sore .
[doctor] okay , lateral joint line tenderness . now i'm going to do a test where i pull your shin forward , just relax for me . okay , that's a lachman test , and compared to your left knee , there's increased translation on the right and i do n't feel a firm endpoint . the left side is normal .
[patient] what does that mean ?
[doctor] i'll explain in a second . now let me check your collateral ligaments , i'm going to stress the knee from the side . no real opening on the inside or outside . your kneecap is stable . and your pulses are good , sensation is normal in your foot .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so the x-rays from urgent care show no fracture . there's a little effusion , and there's no avulsion fragment . so x-ray-wise the bones look good .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so based on how you got hurt , the pop , the fast swelling , and the lachman test , i'm very suspicious that you tore your anterior cruciate ligament , your acl . i'd like to get an mri of the right knee to confirm that and to look at your meniscus , because of that tenderness on the outside .
[patient] is that going to need surgery ?
[doctor] a lot of people who are active and want to get back to cutting and pivoting sports like skiing do choose acl reconstruction . but we do n't have to decide that today . first , we'll get the mri . meanwhile , i want you to start prehab with physical therapy , to get the swelling down and get your knee straight again . that makes recovery from surgery a lot better if you go that route .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] you can keep using the crutches and weight bear as tolerated , and you can take off the immobilizer when you're sitting and doing your exercises . i'll put you in a hinged knee brace for walking . keep taking the naproxen with food , five hundred milligrams twice a day , and ice it a few times a day .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] i'll see you back after the mri , and we'll go over the results and talk about the options .
[patient] thank you . and so no more skiing this season , huh ?
[doctor] i'm afraid not this season .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right knee injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Valeria Moreau is a 40-year-old female who presents for orthopedic evaluation of a right knee injury sustained while downhill skiing at a ski resort on Saturday. She caught an edge on an icy patch and fell from her skis, and her right ski did not release from the binding, resulting in a twisting injury to the right knee. She felt a pop with immediate pain. She was unable to ski down and was transported by ski patrol. She developed significant swelling within an hour. She was seen at an urgent care where x-rays were obtained and she was placed in a knee immobilizer.

She currently reports persistent swelling, inability to fully straighten the knee, and a sensation of instability. She denies locking. She denies numbness. She is taking over-the-counter naproxen twice daily. She has no prior injuries to this knee.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

None.

MEDICATIONS

Oral contraceptive pills.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Works as a software engineer.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Right Knee: Moderate effusion. Range of motion lacking 10 degrees of extension, flexion to 90 degrees. Mild medial joint line tenderness. Lateral joint line tenderness. Positive Lachman test with increased anterior translation and soft endpoint compared to the left. Stable to varus and valgus stress. Patella stable. Distal pulses intact. Sensation intact.
Left Knee: Normal.

RESULTS

X-rays of the right knee from urgent care were reviewed. No fracture. Small joint effusion. No avulsion fragment.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right knee anterior cruciate ligament sprain, suspected complete tear.
- MRI of the right knee to confirm ACL tear and evaluate the lateral meniscus.
- Prehabilitation with physical therapy for effusion control and restoration of extension.
- Hinged knee brace for ambulation, weight bearing as tolerated with crutches.
- Naproxen 500 mg twice daily with food. Ice.
- Discussed ACL reconstruction as an option; will decide after MRI.
- Follow up after MRI.

dialogue:
[doctor] good morning , desmond . i'm doctor santiago jablonski .
[patient] morning , doctor .
[doctor] so i understand you came off a horse yesterday . tell me about it .
[patient] yeah . so my buddy felix has a farm out past the county line , st. brigid parish , and a few of us go out on sundays and ride . i was horseback riding across the hay field , just at a trot , and a deer jumped out of the tree line and the horse spooked . she reared up and kind of twisted , and i got thrown off the horse .
[doctor] okay . and how did you land ?
[patient] right on my left shoulder . i hit the ground pretty hard . i heard a crack , and i knew right away something was broken .
[doctor] were you wearing a helmet ?
[patient] i was , yeah . i did n't hit my head , though . the helmet was fine , no dents or anything .
[doctor] okay , good . did you lose consciousness at all ?
[patient] no , i was awake the whole time . i got up and walked back to the barn holding my arm .
[doctor] okay . where's the pain right now ?
[patient] right here , on the collarbone . there's a bump there that was n't there before .
[doctor] okay . any pain in your neck , your ribs , or trouble breathing ?
[patient] no , my ribs are okay . breathing is fine .
[doctor] any numbness or tingling down your arm or into your hand ?
[patient] no , my hand feels normal . it just hurts to lift my arm at all .
[doctor] alright , and what have you taken for the pain ?
[patient] felix's wife gave me a sling and some ibuprofen . i took eight hundred last night .
[doctor] okay . and does that bother your stomach ? i see that you have reflux .
[patient] it made my heartburn a little worse , yeah . i take omeprazole every morning , twenty milligrams . most days the reflux is under control .
[doctor] any trouble swallowing , or any black stools , vomiting blood , anything like that ?
[patient] no , nothing like that .
[doctor] okay , good . what do you do for work ? is it physical ?
[patient] i'm an insurance adjuster , so a lot of driving and climbing around damaged houses . i'm also a volunteer firefighter .
[doctor] okay , so you're going to need that arm . which hand do you write with ?
[patient] right .
[doctor] okay , good . let me take a look . so i'm going to take your sling off carefully . looking at the left clavicle , there is an obvious deformity over the middle of the collarbone , with some swelling and bruising . the skin is intact , it's not tented . does it hurt when i press here ?
[patient] yeah , that's it .
[doctor] okay , point tenderness over the midshaft of the clavicle . i'm going to check the shoulder joint here . no tenderness at the ac joint . your shoulder is lower on the left side and it drops forward a little . can you squeeze my fingers ? spread your fingers ? good . your radial pulse is strong and sensation is normal in your arm and hand . i'm going to listen to your lungs . breath sounds are equal on both sides .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so we got an x-ray of your left clavicle and a chest x-ray . hey dragon , show me the clavicle x-ray . okay . so the x-ray shows a fracture of the middle third of the left clavicle . the two ends are displaced , about one bone width , and there's about a centimeter of shortening . the chest x-ray shows no pneumothorax and no rib fractures .
[patient] so what's the plan ?
[doctor] so this is a displaced midshaft clavicle fracture . a lot of these heal fine in a sling . but when they're displaced and shortened , and especially in somebody who's active and does physical work , there's a higher chance that it does n't heal or heals short , so some people choose surgery with a plate and screws . i'd like you to see the orthopedic surgeon this week to talk about the options .
[patient] okay . i'd like to hear about the surgery .
[doctor] for now , keep the sling on for comfort . you can take it off to shower and to move your elbow and wrist so they do n't get stiff . no lifting with that arm , and no riding until you're cleared .
[patient] understood .
[doctor] for pain , let's switch from ibuprofen to acetaminophen , one thousand milligrams three times a day , because of your reflux , and i'll give you a few tablets of hydrocodone for night if you need it . ice it twenty minutes at a time .
[patient] sounds good .
[doctor] for the reflux , continue the omeprazole twenty milligrams in the morning . if the heartburn is worse , you can take it twice a day for a couple of weeks .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] and no volunteer calls for a while .
[patient] yeah , i figured .
