CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left shoulder pain after being thrown from a horse.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Desmond Lockhart is a 76-year-old right-hand-dominant male with a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease who presents for evaluation of left clavicle pain. Yesterday, he was horseback riding at a trot across a hay field on a farm when the horse spooked, reared, and he was thrown from the horse, landing directly on his left shoulder. He heard a crack. He was wearing a helmet and denies head strike or loss of consciousness. He reports a new bump over the collarbone and pain with any shoulder motion. He denies neck pain, rib pain, shortness of breath, numbness, or tingling. He took ibuprofen 800 mg, which worsened his heartburn.

His reflux is managed with omeprazole 20 mg daily and is generally well controlled. He denies dysphagia, melena, or hematemesis.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Insurance adjuster and volunteer firefighter.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Left Shoulder: Visible deformity over the midshaft of the clavicle with swelling and ecchymosis. Skin intact, not tented. Point tenderness over the midshaft clavicle. No tenderness over the acromioclavicular joint. Shoulder ptosis on the left.
Neurovascular: Grip strength and finger abduction intact. Radial pulse 2+. Sensation intact throughout the left upper extremity.
Respiratory: Breath sounds equal bilaterally.

RESULTS

X-ray of the left clavicle: Displaced fracture of the middle third of the left clavicle with 100% displacement and approximately 1 cm of shortening.

Chest x-ray: No pneumothorax. No rib fractures.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Closed displaced fracture of the shaft of the left clavicle.
- Sling for comfort with elbow, wrist, and hand range of motion.
- No lifting with the left arm and no horseback riding until cleared.
- Referral to orthopedic surgery this week to discuss nonoperative management versus open reduction and internal fixation.
- Acetaminophen 1000 mg three times daily, hydrocodone-acetaminophen as needed at night, and ice packs.

2. Gastroesophageal reflux disease.
- Avoid NSAIDs.
- Continue omeprazole 20 mg daily; may increase to twice daily for 2 weeks if symptoms worsen.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Valeria Alvarado is a 30-year-old female with a history of hypothyroidism who presents to the emergency department on 09/02/2023 approximately 1.5 hours after a left elbow injury. She was jumping on a trampoline in her backyard when she was propelled sideways and fell off the trampoline, landing on her outstretched left hand on the grass. The trampoline safety net had been torn. She denies head injury or loss of consciousness. She reports 10/10 pain and inability to move the elbow. She endorses mild tingling of the ring and small fingers.

ALLERGIES

No known drug allergies.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Hairdresser who owns a salon.

Left Elbow: Held in approximately 90 degrees of flexion with prominent posterior olecranon and marked swelling. Skin intact without open wounds.

- Stable. Continue levothyroxine 75 mcg daily.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left hip pain after a fall in the shower.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Carmen Kowalski is a 19-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus who presents to the emergency department after a fall. She is visiting from out of town and is staying at a hotel. This morning, while showering in the hotel bathroom, she slipped in the bathtub and fell in the shower, landing directly on her left hip against the edge of the tub. She denies head strike, loss of consciousness, or prodromal dizziness. She was unable to get up after the fall. She reports severe left hip and groin pain, 9/10 with movement, and mild right wrist soreness.

At baseline, she ambulates independently without an assistive device. No prior fractures.

Her diabetes is managed with metformin 500 mg twice daily. Most recent hemoglobin A1c was 6.8%. She denies peripheral neuropathy or kidney disease. She takes aspirin 81 mg daily and no anticoagulants.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Retired mail carrier. Lives independently.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Left Lower Extremity: Shortened and externally rotated. Pain with log roll of the left hip. Early ecchymosis over the lateral hip. Toe motion and ankle plantarflexion and dorsiflexion intact. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses palpable. Sensation intact.
Right Wrist: Mild tenderness. Full range of motion. No swelling.

RESULTS

X-ray of the left hip and pelvis: Displaced intertrochanteric fracture of the left femur.

X-ray of the right wrist: No fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Closed displaced intertrochanteric fracture of the left femur.
- Admit to orthopedics. Plan for intramedullary nail fixation within 24 hours.
- Preoperative labs, ECG, and chest x-ray.
- Fascia iliaca nerve block for pain control; analgesics as needed.
- Hold aspirin.
- Postoperative weight bearing as tolerated and physical therapy.
- Bone density and vitamin D evaluation.

2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Well controlled with A1c 6.8%.
- Hold metformin while inpatient. Fingerstick glucose before meals and at bedtime with sliding scale insulin.

3. Right wrist contusion.
- Symptomatic care.

[patient] oh hello yes thank you for coming
[doctor] of course and who do we have here
[patient] this is my granddaughter chloe i'm in town from olympia for her wedding on november fifth
[doctor] oh congratulations
[patient] thank you well we'll see if grandma makes it to the wedding now
[doctor] we're going to do our best so can you tell me what happened
[patient] so we're staying at a hotel downtown and this morning i was taking a shower and the tub in the hotel bathroom is one of those slippery ones and there was no mat and i reached for the shampoo and my feet slipped and i fell in the shower and landed right on my left hip on the edge of the tub
[doctor] okay did you hit your head
[patient] no i caught myself with my arm on the shower curtain bar but my hip took the whole fall
[doctor] okay and did you get dizzy or lightheaded or black out before you fell
[patient] no nothing like that it was just slippery i felt fine
[doctor] okay and were you able to get up after
[patient] no i could n't get up at all chloe heard me yelling and she called the front desk and they called the ambulance
[doctor] okay where's the pain now
[patient] it's in my left hip and kind of down into my groin and it hurts terribly when anybody moves my leg
[doctor] okay on a scale of zero to ten
[patient] about a nine when they move me
[doctor] okay any pain anywhere else your wrist your back your neck
[patient] my right wrist is a little sore but it's not bad
[doctor] okay and before this were you walking on your own
[patient] yes i walk every day i do n't use a cane or anything i still do my garden
[doctor] good now tell me about your medical problems i see you have diabetes
[patient] yes type two i take metformin five hundred milligrams twice a day
[doctor] and how's your sugar been
[patient] pretty good my last a1c was six point eight my doctor at home was happy with it
[doctor] okay any numbness in your feet from the diabetes or any kidney problems
[patient] no my feet are fine
[doctor] okay and any blood thinners
[patient] no just a baby aspirin
[doctor] okay any problems with your heart or lungs
[patient] no
[doctor] any previous fractures
[patient] no i've never broken anything
[doctor] okay and what did you do for work before you retired
[patient] i was a mail carrier for thirty one years so i've done a lot of walking
[doctor] that's great alright let me take a look at you so i'm looking at your left leg it's shortened compared to the right and it's rotated outward does it hurt when i gently roll the leg
[patient] oh yes that hurts
[doctor] okay pain with log roll of the left hip there's some bruising starting on the outside of your hip can you wiggle your toes for me
[patient] yes
[doctor] good push down with your foot like a gas pedal and pull up good your pulses in the foot are good and you can feel me touching your foot
[patient] yes
[doctor] okay and let me look at your right wrist there's mild tenderness but full range of motion and no swelling
[doctor] okay so they did x-rays of your hip and pelvis down in the er and the x-ray shows a fracture of the left hip specifically it's what we call an intertrochanteric fracture which is a break just below the ball of the hip joint and it is displaced so the pieces are out of place the x-ray of your wrist did n't show a fracture
[patient] oh dear so what happens now
[doctor] so for this kind of hip fracture the best treatment is surgery we would put a rod with a screw up into the ball of the hip to hold it together it's called an intramedullary nail and the good news is that it lets you get up and walk on it pretty much right away usually the day after surgery
[patient] and when would you do that
[doctor] we'd like to do it within the next twenty four hours ideally tomorrow morning
[patient] okay
[doctor] before surgery we're going to get some blood work an ekg and a chest x-ray and we'll hold your metformin and the aspirin while you're in the hospital we'll check your blood sugar before meals and at bedtime and cover you with insulin as needed
[patient] okay
[doctor] for pain we'll do a nerve block in your hip area which helps a lot and you'll have pain medicine as you need it
[patient] thank you
[doctor] after surgery you'll work with physical therapy and we'll also check your bone density and vitamin d since you broke your hip from a fall in the shower
[patient] that makes sense
[doctor] and chloe we'll do everything we can to get grandma to the wedding even if she's in a wheelchair
[patient] that's all i want
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left hip pain after a fall in the shower.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Harriet Petrov is a 61-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus who presents to the emergency department after a fall. She is visiting from out of town and is staying at a hotel. This morning, while showering in the hotel bathroom, she slipped in the bathtub and fell in the shower, landing directly on her left hip against the edge of the tub. She denies head strike, loss of consciousness, or prodromal dizziness. She was unable to get up after the fall. She reports severe left hip and groin pain, 9/10 with movement, and mild right wrist soreness.

At baseline, she ambulates independently without an assistive device. No prior fractures.

Her diabetes is managed with metformin 500 mg twice daily. Most recent hemoglobin A1c was 6.8%. She denies peripheral neuropathy or kidney disease. She takes aspirin 81 mg daily and no anticoagulants.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Retired mail carrier. Lives independently.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Left Lower Extremity: Shortened and externally rotated. Pain with log roll of the left hip. Early ecchymosis over the lateral hip. Toe motion and ankle plantarflexion and dorsiflexion intact. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses palpable. Sensation intact.
Right Wrist: Mild tenderness. Full range of motion. No swelling.

RESULTS

X-ray of the left hip and pelvis: Displaced intertrochanteric fracture of the left femur.

X-ray of the right wrist: No fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Closed displaced intertrochanteric fracture of the left femur.
- Admit to orthopedics. Plan for intramedullary nail fixation within 24 hours.
- Preoperative labs, ECG, and chest x-ray.
- Fascia iliaca nerve block for pain control; analgesics as needed.
- Hold aspirin.
- Postoperative weight bearing as tolerated and physical therapy.
- Bone density and vitamin D evaluation.

2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Well controlled with A1c 6.8%.
- Hold metformin while inpatient. Fingerstick glucose before meals and at bedtime with sliding scale insulin.

3. Right wrist contusion.
- Symptomatic care.

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , gordon . i'm doctor nwosu . how are you feeling ?
[patient] sore . my back is really sore .
[doctor] i bet . so i've read through what the paramedics wrote , but walk me through what happened today .
[patient] so i was at work , i work for eastgate veterinary clinic , and we're building a new house on a subdivision out on the east side . i was up on the roof putting down the plywood sheathing , and it had rained a little in the morning , and my boot slipped on the wet plywood , and i slid down and went right off the edge of the roof .
[doctor] how far did you fall ?
[patient] it's a two story , so maybe eighteen , twenty feet . i landed on my butt and my back on a pile of dirt , which was lucky , i guess .
[doctor] that is lucky . were you wearing a harness ?
[patient] no . we're supposed to . the harness anchor was n't set up on that side yet . my foreman simon is not happy about it .
[doctor] okay . did you hit your head ?
[patient] no , i had my hard hat on and i did n't hit my head .
[doctor] any loss of consciousness ?
[patient] no , i remember all of it . i just could n't catch my breath for a minute .
[doctor] okay . and where's the pain ?
[patient] mostly in my mid to low back , right in the middle . it's sharp when i try to sit up or twist .
[doctor] does it go down your legs at all ?
[patient] no , it's just in the back .
[doctor] any numbness or tingling in your legs , or weakness ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] any trouble with your bladder or bowels , like not being able to pee or leaking ?
[patient] no , i peed in the er , it was fine .
[doctor] okay , good . any pain in your neck , chest , belly , hips ?
[patient] my left wrist was a little sore but it's better . nothing else .
[doctor] okay . any medical problems ?
[patient] no , i'm pretty healthy . i do n't take any medicines . i smoke about half a pack a day .
[doctor] okay , we'll talk about that . how long have you been doing construction ?
[patient] i've been a carpenter for about fifteen years . and i coach my daughter's wrestling team on the weekends .
[doctor] okay . let me examine you . we're going to keep you flat and do a log roll to look at your back . on three . okay . so there's tenderness right in the middle of your back at about the junction of the mid and low back , at the thoracolumbar junction . no step-off that i can feel . no bruising on the skin . does it hurt anywhere above or below that ?
[patient] no , it's right there .
[doctor] okay . now push down with both feet , pull up , squeeze your legs together . good , strength is five out of five in both legs . can you feel me touching your legs here , and here ?
[patient] yes , all normal .
[doctor] okay , sensation is intact . reflexes at the knees and ankles are normal . your rectal tone was checked by the er doctor and was normal . and the left wrist has some mild tenderness , but you have full motion and no swelling .
[doctor] so we did a ct scan of your whole spine . hey dragon , show me the ct of the lumbar spine . so the ct shows a compression fracture of the first lumbar vertebra , l1 . it's what's called a wedge compression fracture , the front of the bone is squished down about twenty percent , and the back wall of the vertebra is intact . there are no fragments going back toward the spinal canal . the rest of the spine looks normal . and the x-ray of your wrist is normal .
[patient] so i broke my back ?
[doctor] you did break a bone in your back , but it's a stable type of fracture , and your nerves are working normally , which is the most important thing . most of these heal without surgery .
[patient] okay . that's a relief .
[doctor] so we'll fit you for a back brace called a tlso , and you'll wear it whenever you're up out of bed . we'll get standing x-rays in the brace to make sure the fracture does n't collapse more . i'd like you to see the spine clinic in two weeks .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] for pain , you can take acetaminophen one thousand milligrams three times a day and ibuprofen six hundred milligrams with food . and i'll give you a short course of oxycodone five milligrams for the worst pain .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] no work at all for now . no lifting , no climbing , definitely no roofs . i'll fill out the workers' comp paperwork today .
[patient] thank you .
[doctor] and the smoking slows bone healing , so this would be a really good time to quit . i can give you nicotine patches .
[patient] yeah , let's try that .
[doctor] okay . if you get any numbness , weakness , or trouble with your bladder or bowels , come back right away .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Back pain after a fall from a roof at work.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Gordon Vukovic is a 46-year-old male with no significant past medical history who presents on 06/04/2019 after a work-related fall. He is employed by Eastgate Veterinary Clinic and was working on a residential construction site, installing plywood roof sheathing on a two-story house under construction, when his boot slipped on wet plywood and he slid off the edge of the roof. He fell approximately 18 to 20 feet, landing on his buttocks and back on soft dirt. He was not wearing a fall-arrest harness. He was wearing a hard hat and denies head strike or loss of consciousness. He reports transient difficulty catching his breath.

He reports sharp thoracolumbar back pain worse with sitting up or twisting. He denies radiation of pain, lower extremity numbness, tingling, or weakness, and bowel or bladder dysfunction. He reports mild left wrist soreness that has improved.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Carpenter. Smokes approximately one-half pack per day.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Back: Tenderness at the thoracolumbar junction. No palpable step-off. No ecchymosis.
Neuro: Strength 5/5 in bilateral lower extremities. Sensation intact to light touch. Patellar and Achilles reflexes 2+ and symmetric. Rectal tone normal per ED.
Left Wrist: Mild tenderness. Full range of motion. No swelling.

RESULTS

CT of the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine: Wedge compression fracture of the L1 vertebral body with approximately 20% loss of anterior height. Posterior vertebral wall intact. No retropulsion. Remainder of the spine unremarkable.

X-ray of the left wrist: Normal.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Closed wedge compression fracture of the L1 vertebra, neurologically intact.
- TLSO brace when upright.
- Upright lumbar x-rays in the brace.
- Follow-up in spine clinic in 2 weeks.
- Acetaminophen 1000 mg three times daily, ibuprofen 600 mg with food, oxycodone 5 mg as needed for severe pain.
- Off work. No lifting or climbing.
- Workers' compensation paperwork completed.
- Return precautions for new neurologic deficits or bowel or bladder dysfunction.

2. Tobacco use.
- Counseled on smoking cessation and its effect on bone healing. Nicotine patch prescribed.

dialogue:
[doctor] hello , ms . dubois . i'm doctor farah ortega . nice to meet you .
[patient] nice to meet you too . you can call me yvonne .
[doctor] okay , yvonne . so i understand you were hurt at work . this is a workers' comp visit ?
[patient] yes . my manager , kwame , filled out the incident report and sent me over here .
[doctor] okay . tell me what happened .
[patient] so i work at the evergreen assisted living supermarket on the main road . last night on my shift , i was walking down the dairy aisle with a cart of milk to restock the cooler , and somebody had dropped a jug of juice and nobody had mopped it up yet . there was no wet floor sign or anything . i stepped right in it , slipped on the wet floor , and my feet went out from under me .
[doctor] okay . and how did you land ?
[patient] i came down hard on my right knee first and then kind of twisted and landed on my back and my bottom . i did n't hit anything on the way down , just the floor .
[doctor] did you hit your head ?
[patient] no , my head was fine .
[doctor] okay . and what bothers you the most right now ?
[patient] my lower back , definitely . it was stiff last night , and this morning i could barely get out of bed . it's like a tight , achy pain across the low back , and it gets sharp when i bend over or lift .
[doctor] does the pain go down into your legs ?
[patient] no , it stays in my back .
[doctor] any numbness or tingling in your legs , any weakness ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] any trouble with your bladder or bowels ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] and the knee ?
[patient] it's bruised and sore on the front , right on the kneecap . it hurts to kneel , but i can walk on it okay .
[doctor] any swelling , locking , or giving way in the knee ?
[patient] a little swelling , but no locking or giving way .
[doctor] okay . what have you done for it ?
[patient] i took two ibuprofen last night and used a heating pad on my back this morning .
[doctor] okay . have you ever had back problems before ?
[patient] i strained it once about five years ago moving furniture , but it got better in a couple weeks .
[doctor] okay . any other medical problems ?
[patient] no , i do n't take any regular medicines .
[doctor] alright . and what's your job like there ? lots of lifting ?
[patient] yes , i'm the assistant manager of the dairy department , so i'm unloading cases , stocking the shelves , lifting crates all night . and at home i'm raising my two grandkids , so i'm picking up a four year old .
[doctor] that's a lot of lifting . okay , let me examine you . can you stand up for me ? okay , bend forward as far as you can .
[patient] ouch . that's about it .
[doctor] okay , flexion is limited to about forty five degrees by pain . lean back for me .
[patient] that's not as bad .
[doctor] okay . i'm going to press along your back . there's tenderness and spasm in the muscles on both sides of the lower back , but no tenderness right on the spine itself . now lie down for me . i'm going to lift your leg straight up .
[patient] it pulls in my back but not in the leg .
[doctor] okay , negative straight leg raise on both sides . strength in your legs is five out of five , sensation is normal , and reflexes are normal and equal . now let me look at the right knee . there's a bruise on the front of the kneecap with mild swelling over it . there's tenderness on the kneecap , but no tenderness at the joint lines . you can fully bend and straighten it . the ligaments are stable . and you can do a straight leg raise without a lag .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so we did an x-ray of your right knee because you landed on it directly . the x-ray shows no fracture of the kneecap or the rest of the knee , just some soft tissue swelling in front . i did n't get an x-ray of your back , because with no red flags , it's not needed right now .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so for my assessment , you have a lumbar sprain , which is a stretch injury of the muscles and ligaments of the low back , and a contusion , or a bruise , of the right knee . both of these should get better over the next few weeks .
[patient] that's good .
[doctor] for the back , i'd like you to keep moving , bed rest makes it worse . use heat or ice , whatever feels better . you can take naproxen five hundred milligrams twice a day with food , and i'll give you cyclobenzaprine five milligrams at night for the muscle spasms . it can make you sleepy , so do n't drive after taking it .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] i'm also going to refer you to physical therapy for your back . for the knee , ice it , and avoid kneeling for now .
[patient] can i work ?
[doctor] you can go back to work with restrictions . no lifting over fifteen pounds and no kneeling for two weeks . i'll write that up for your workers' comp form . i'll see you back in two weeks .
[patient] okay , thank you .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Low back pain and right knee pain after a work-related fall.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Yvonne Dubois is a 50-year-old female who presents for a workers' compensation evaluation following a work-related injury on January Second. While working her shift at a supermarket, she was walking down an aisle pushing a cart of product to restock a cooler when she slipped on a wet floor from a spilled beverage and fell. She landed initially on her right knee and then on her back and buttocks. She did not strike any objects during the fall. She denies head injury.

She reports low back stiffness and a tight, achy pain across the lumbar region, worse with bending and lifting. She denies radiating pain, lower extremity numbness, tingling, or weakness, and bowel or bladder dysfunction. She also reports anterior right knee pain and mild swelling, worse with kneeling, without locking or instability. She took ibuprofen and used a heating pad with partial relief. She reports a prior lumbar strain approximately 5 years ago that resolved.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Assistant manager of the dairy department. Her job requires frequent lifting.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Lumbar Spine: Flexion limited to 45 degrees by pain. Extension better tolerated. Bilateral paraspinal tenderness and muscle spasm. No midline tenderness. Negative straight leg raise bilaterally.
Neuro: Strength 5/5 in bilateral lower extremities. Sensation intact. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric.
Right Knee: Ecchymosis over the anterior patella with mild prepatellar swelling. Tenderness over the patella. No joint line tenderness. Full range of motion. Ligaments stable. Able to perform straight leg raise without extensor lag.

RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee: No fracture. Anterior soft tissue swelling.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Lumbar sprain.
- Remain active; avoid bed rest. Heat or ice as needed.
- Naproxen 500 mg twice daily with food.
- Cyclobenzaprine 5 mg at bedtime as needed for muscle spasm. Counseled on sedation.
- Referral to physical therapy.

2. Contusion of the right knee.
- Ice. Avoid kneeling.

Work status: Return to modified duty with no lifting over 15 pounds and no kneeling for 2 weeks. Workers' compensation forms completed. Follow up in 2 weeks.

Works in payroll at a desk job.

Oxygen saturation 98% on room air.

[doctor] okay .
[patient] and it was still a little dark under the trees , and i caught my toe on a tree root that was sticking up out of the path , and i tripped and went flying forward .
[doctor] oh , no .
[patient] and i put my right hand out to catch myself and landed on it , on the dirt path , and i felt it bend back and there was this awful pain .
[doctor] okay . so you landed on your outstretched right hand . did you hit anything else on the way down , a bench or a rock or anything ?
[patient] no , just the ground . i scraped my knees a little , but it's mostly my wrist .
[doctor] okay . did you hit your head ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] okay . and how does the wrist feel now ?
[patient] it's swollen and it looks kind of bent , like a fork . it really hurts if i try to move it . latoya drove me straight here .
[doctor] okay . on a scale of one to ten ?
[patient] about a seven . more if i move it .
[doctor] okay . any numbness or tingling in your fingers ?
[patient] my fingers feel a little bit tingly , but i can feel them .
[doctor] which fingers ?
[patient] kind of the thumb and the first two fingers .
[doctor] okay . we'll keep an eye on that . are you right handed ?
[patient] yes , unfortunately .
[doctor] okay . now , i see from your chart we've been treating your cholesterol . you're on atorvastatin ?
[patient] yes , twenty milligrams at night .
[doctor] okay . any muscle aches with it ?
[patient] no , i've been fine on it .
[doctor] good . your last lipid panel in the spring , your ldl was one twenty two , which was down from one sixty , so that's a good improvement .
[patient] oh , good .
[doctor] okay . have you ever had a bone density scan ?
[patient] i had one a few years ago and they said it was okay .
[doctor] okay . let me take a look at your wrist . i'm going to be gentle . so , looking at your right wrist , there is swelling and a dorsal angulation , what we call a dinner fork deformity . you're tender over the distal radius here . the skin is intact , no open wounds . i'm going to check your fingers . can you make an okay sign ? good . and spread your fingers ? good . your capillary refill is brisk and your radial pulse is present . you have slightly decreased light touch over the tip of the index finger , but otherwise sensation is intact . there's no tenderness in the snuffbox here , and your elbow is fine .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] you've got some superficial abrasions on both knees , they're clean .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so we did x-rays of your wrist . hey dragon , show me the right wrist x-rays . so looking at these , you have a fracture at the end of the radius , about two centimeters above the joint , and the broken piece is tilted backward . this is what we call a colles' fracture . it does n't look like it goes into the joint , and the ulna is okay .
[patient] okay . so it's broken .
[doctor] yes . so for my assessment and plan , for the right wrist , you have a closed colles' fracture with dorsal angulation . because it's tilted back , we're going to do a closed reduction today , which means we numb the area with a hematoma block and pull it back into position , and then put you in a splint .
[patient] okay .

[doctor] okay . and after you hit , did you have any numbness , tingling , or weakness in your arms or legs ? even for a second ?

[patient] no .

[patient] no .

[patient] i have no idea . probably high school .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Neck pain and scalp laceration after a diving injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Anders Northcott is a 31-year-old male brought in by EMS with spinal motion restriction on February Fourth after a diving injury at a public swimming pool. He was swimming and dove head first off the side into the shallow end, approximately 4 feet deep, striking the top of his head on the bottom of the pool. He reports a brief moment of seeing white but no loss of consciousness. He was assisted from the water and immobilized by the lifeguard. He reports immediate posterior neck pain, 5/10, radiating to the trapezius, and a mild headache at the laceration site. He denies numbness, tingling, weakness or electric shock sensations at any time. He denies nausea, vomiting, visual change or dyspnea. One alcoholic beverage 2 hours prior. No past medical history. No medications. Tetanus status unknown.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Line cook.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Neurological: Alert and oriented. Pupils equal and reactive. Strength 5/5 in all extremities. Sensation intact. Reflexes normal.
Head: 3 cm linear laceration of the vertex of the scalp, superficial, no foreign body, no exposed bone.
Neck: Lower cervical midline tenderness and bilateral paraspinal tenderness.

RESULTS

CT cervical spine: No fracture or malalignment.
CT head: No intracranial hemorrhage or skull fracture.

PROCEDURE

Scalp laceration irrigated and repaired with 4 staples. Tdap administered.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Cervical sprain, after diving into a swimming pool and striking the bottom.
- Medical Reasoning: Midline tenderness with normal CT and normal neurologic exam. Cervical collar cleared clinically.
- Medical Treatment: Soft collar for comfort as needed. Ibuprofen 600 mg every 8 hours with food. Cyclobenzaprine 5 mg at bedtime.
- Follow up with primary care in 1 week; MRI if persistent pain.

2. Laceration of the scalp without foreign body.
- Medical Treatment: Staple removal in 7 to 10 days. Wound care reviewed. Tetanus updated.

Return precautions reviewed for any numbness, weakness, gait change or bladder dysfunction.

[doctor] hello , carmen , good to see you again .
[patient] hi , doctor zielinski . i wish it was under better circumstances .
[doctor] so , last time you were here it was for your tennis elbow , on the right . what's going on now ?
[patient] so it had been getting a little better with the strap and the stretches you gave me . i'd say it was down to like a two out of ten most days . and then on saturday i had a league match , i'm the captain of our women's doubles team , so i was n't going to sit out .
[doctor] of course .
[patient] and we were playing tennis on the hard courts at pelican bay , and it was a really long match , three sets , and i was hitting backhand after backhand , because the other team kept going to my backhand side . and in the third set i hit a backhand and i felt this sharp pull on the outside of my elbow , like something tore .
[doctor] okay . so it happened on one specific backhand , after a lot of repetitive backhands .
[patient] yes . it had been aching more and more through the match , and then that one shot it just grabbed .
[doctor] okay . were you able to finish ?
[patient] barely . my partner nathaniel took most of the overheads . i could n't really grip the racquet after that .
[doctor] okay . and since saturday ?
[patient] it's a lot worse than before . it's maybe a six out of ten . it's swollen on the outside of my elbow , and it hurts to pick up a coffee cup or turn a doorknob . shaking hands is terrible .
[doctor] okay . any numbness or tingling in your hand ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] any pain in your neck or shooting down the arm ?
[patient] no , it's all right here at the elbow and a little bit into the forearm .
[doctor] okay . any bruising ?
[patient] a little bit of a faint bruise on the outside , yeah .
[doctor] okay . what have you been doing for it ?
[patient] ice , and i've been taking naproxen , two pills twice a day .
[doctor] okay . and you were doing the physical therapy exercises ?
[patient] yes , the wrist ones with the band , three times a week .
[doctor] good . and you're still working at the pharmacy ?
[patient] yes , i'm a pharmacist , so a lot of counting pills and typing . that bothers it a little , but not like tennis .
[doctor] okay . any other new medical problems ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] okay . let me take a look . so on your right elbow , there's mild swelling over the lateral epicondyle with a faint bruise just below it . you're very tender right over the lateral epicondyle and just distal to it , over the common extensor origin . does this hurt when i press here ?
[patient] ow , yes .
[doctor] okay . now resist me as i push your wrist down . does that hurt ?
[patient] yes , a lot .
[doctor] okay . and the middle finger , push up against me ?
[patient] that hurts too .
[doctor] okay . your grip strength is reduced on the right compared to the left . your elbow range of motion is full . there's no tenderness on the inside of the elbow , and the ligaments feel stable . sensation is normal in your hand .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so i went ahead and did a quick ultrasound here in the office . hey dragon , show me the elbow ultrasound . so you can see here the common extensor tendon is thickened , which is your chronic tennis elbow , but there is also a new small partial thickness tear at the origin , with some fluid around it . the tendon is not completely torn .
[patient] okay . so i tore it .
[doctor] a little bit , yes . so , my assessment is , you have an acute strain with a small partial tear of the extensor tendon at the elbow , on top of your known lateral epicondylitis , from repetitive backhands during the match .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] for the plan , i want you to rest it from tennis for at least six weeks . i'm going to put you in a wrist splint that holds your wrist slightly extended , which takes the stress off the tendon , and you can keep using the counterforce strap during the day . continue icing . you can keep taking the naproxen , five hundred milligrams twice a day with food , for two more weeks .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] i'm not going to do a steroid injection right now , because it can weaken the tendon when it's partially torn . i'll send you back to physical therapy , and we'll restart the eccentric strengthening once the acute pain settles , in about two weeks .
[patient] okay , that makes sense .
[doctor] and when you go back , we'll talk with the therapist about your backhand technique and maybe your racquet grip size .
[patient] my coach has been saying the same thing .
[doctor] i'll see you back in four weeks . if it's not improving , we can get an mri .
[patient] okay . thank you .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Worsening right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Carmen Zimmerman is a 65-year-old right-hand-dominant female with known right lateral epicondylitis who presents on 08/03/2019 with acute worsening of right elbow pain. Her lateral elbow pain had improved to 2/10 with a counterforce strap and a home exercise program. On Saturday, she was playing tennis in a three-set league match on a tennis court and was hitting repeated backhands. In the third set, she felt a sharp pulling sensation at the lateral elbow on a backhand stroke. Pain is now 6/10 with lateral elbow swelling, a faint bruise, pain with gripping, and weakness. She denies numbness, tingling, neck pain or radiating pain. She has been using ice and naproxen.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Pharmacist.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Right elbow: Mild swelling over the lateral epicondyle with faint ecchymosis distally. Marked tenderness over the lateral epicondyle and common extensor origin. Pain with resisted wrist extension and resisted middle finger extension. Grip strength decreased on the right. Full range of motion. No medial tenderness. Ligaments stable. Sensation intact.

RESULTS

Point-of-care ultrasound of the right elbow demonstrates thickening of the common extensor tendon with a small partial-thickness tear at its origin and adjacent fluid. No full-thickness tear.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Strain of the extensor tendon at the right elbow and forearm with a small partial-thickness tear, due to repetitive backhand strokes while playing tennis.
- Medical Reasoning: Acute injury superimposed on chronic tendinopathy, confirmed by ultrasound.
- Medical Treatment: Wrist splint in slight extension. Continue counterforce strap and ice. Naproxen 500 mg twice daily with food for 2 weeks. No corticosteroid injection given partial tear.
- No tennis for at least 6 weeks.

2. Lateral epicondylitis, right elbow.
- Medical Treatment: Resume physical therapy with eccentric strengthening in 2 weeks. Review stroke mechanics and grip size.

Follow-up in 4 weeks; MRI if not improving.

dialogue:
[doctor] hey , nathaniel . what happened to the shoulder ?
[patient] hey , doc . hockey happened .
[doctor] i figured . go ahead and tell me about it .
[patient] so i play in a men's league on tuesday nights , our team is sponsored by anchor marine supply . and last night we were playing ice hockey at the rink , and i was chasing the puck into the corner , and i caught an edge with my skate , and i could n't stop . i went right into the boards , shoulder first , full speed .
[doctor] okay . so nobody checked you , you just lost your edge and hit the boards ?
[patient] nobody touched me . it's a no checking league anyway . it was all me and the boards .
[doctor] okay . which shoulder ?
[patient] the right one . i hit right on the top of it , like the point of the shoulder .
[doctor] okay . did you hit your head ?
[patient] no , my helmet did n't touch anything .
[doctor] okay . and what did you feel ?
[patient] it was instant pain on the top of my shoulder . i went down on the ice and i could n't really lift my arm . i skated off holding it . and when i took my pads off , there was this bump sticking up on top of my shoulder .
[doctor] okay . any numbness or tingling down your arm ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] any weakness in your hand ?
[patient] no , my hand is fine . it's just really hard to lift my arm over my head , and reaching across my body hurts a lot .
[doctor] okay . on a scale of one to ten ?
[patient] a seven when i move it , maybe a three when i keep it still .
[doctor] okay . have you hurt this shoulder before ?
[patient] never . i've had a lot of stitches and a broken nose from hockey , but never the shoulder .
[doctor] okay . what have you taken for it ?
[patient] i took some ibuprofen last night , and then my heartburn kicked up .
[doctor] okay , so let's talk about that . you've got reflux and you're on omeprazole ?
[patient] yeah , twenty milligrams every morning . usually it's under control , unless i eat late or take a bunch of ibuprofen .
[doctor] okay . any trouble swallowing , vomiting , black stools ?
[patient] no , nothing like that .
[doctor] okay , good . so what do you do for work ?
[patient] i'm a firefighter , so i need this shoulder .
[doctor] okay . let me take a look . so , on your right shoulder , there is a visible step off at the acromioclavicular joint , that's where the collarbone meets the top of the shoulder blade . there's mild swelling there and a little bit of bruising . i'm going to press on it .
[patient] ow , yep .
[doctor] okay . you're very tender right over the ac joint , and the end of the collarbone moves a little when i press it down . now i'm going to bring your arm across your body .
[patient] that's the worst .
[doctor] okay . so you have a positive cross body adduction test . your rotator cuff strength is good , although it's limited by pain when you lift your arm . you're not tender along the middle of the collarbone . your pulses and sensation in the arm are normal .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so we got x-rays of the shoulder . hey dragon , show me the right shoulder x-rays . so looking at these , the end of the collarbone is sitting a little bit higher than the acromion , but less than the full width of the collarbone . there's no fracture of the collarbone or the shoulder blade , and the shoulder joint itself is in place .
[patient] so it's separated ?
[doctor] it is . so my assessment is you have a right ac joint separation , what we'd call a subluxation of the acromioclavicular joint , or a grade two separation , from crashing into the boards while skating . the good news is these almost always heal without surgery .
[patient] okay . good .
[doctor] i want you to wear a sling for comfort for about one to two weeks , and start gentle range of motion as the pain allows . ice twenty minutes a few times a day . for the pain , because of your reflux , i want you to use tylenol as your main medicine , up to three thousand milligrams a day , and if you do need ibuprofen , take it with food , and only for a few days .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] and for your reflux , continue the omeprazole twenty milligrams every morning . if the heartburn does n't settle within a week after you stop the ibuprofen , let me know .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] i'll refer you to physical therapy in about a week . for work , you're on light duty , no lifting with the right arm and no ladders or hose work for at least four weeks . and no hockey for about six weeks , until you have full strength and no pain .
[patient] okay . the guys are going to give me a hard time .
[doctor] i'm sure they will . i'll see you back in three weeks .

Right shoulder injury.

Firefighter.

Right shoulder: Visible step-off at the acromioclavicular joint with mild swelling and ecchymosis. - Work: Light duty, no lifting with the right arm, no ladder or hose work for 4 weeks. No hockey for 6 weeks.

2. Gastroesophageal reflux disease.
- Medical Reasoning: Symptoms aggravated by NSAID use, otherwise controlled.
- Medical Treatment: Continue omeprazole 20 mg every morning.

Follow-up in 3 weeks.

Neck pain after motor vehicle collision.

Nkechi Grabowski is a 43-year-old female with a history of hypertension who presents for evaluation of neck pain following a motor vehicle collision on 01/21/2025.

The patient was the restrained driver of a car that was stopped in traffic on the interstate highway near Toledo when she was rear-ended by another car traveling at speed. She was driving home from work at the time. She works as a dental hygienist. Airbags did not deploy. She denies head strike or loss of consciousness. She noted neck stiffness the evening of the accident, which worsened the following morning. Pain is located in the posterior neck and radiates to the upper shoulders, right worse than left. She rates the pain 6/10 at rest and 8/10 with rotation. She reports a mild occipital headache which improves with Tylenol. She denies numbness, tingling, or weakness in the upper extremities. She denies nausea, vomiting, dizziness, or visual changes. She has been taking Tylenol extra strength and using a heating pad.

Regarding her hypertension, she takes lisinopril 20 mg daily. Home blood pressures have been in the 130s/80s, possibly slightly higher since the accident due to stress and pain. She denies chest pain or shortness of breath.

Neck: Tenderness to palpation of the posterior cervical paraspinal muscles. Spasm of the right trapezius. No midline bony tenderness. Decreased range of motion with right rotation and extension.
Neurological: Strength 5/5 in bilateral upper extremities. Reflexes normal. Sensation intact.

RESULTS

X-ray of the cervical spine: No fracture. Normal alignment. Mild straightening of the cervical lordosis consistent with muscle spasm.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Cervical sprain (whiplash injury) after rear-end collision.
- Prescribed cyclobenzaprine 5 mg at bedtime.
- Ibuprofen 600 mg three times daily with food for one week, in addition to Tylenol.
- Continue heat.
- Referral to physical therapy twice weekly for 4 weeks.
- No cervical collar recommended.
- Avoid driving until able to rotate the neck sufficiently.
- Return precautions reviewed for numbness, tingling, weakness, or worsening headache.

2. Hypertension.
- Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily.
- Monitor home blood pressure while on NSAIDs; call if greater than 150 systolic.

Follow up in 3 weeks.

[patient] hey , nice to meet you .
[doctor] hey , dragon , i'm seeing harold mendoza , he's a 63-year-old male here for a right shoulder injury . so what happened ?
[patient] so i wrecked my motorcycle on saturday . me and my buddy reginald were riding up to pine ridge trail , just a weekend ride , and we were on the state route that goes up through the hills . it's a two-lane road with a lot of curves .
[doctor] okay .
[patient] and i came around a curve and there was a bunch of gravel spread across my lane . i hit it , and the back tire just slid out from under me . i laid the bike down and slid , and i landed right on my right shoulder .
[doctor] okay . so no other vehicles were involved ? you did n't hit a car or anything ?
[patient] no , nobody else . it was just me and the gravel .
[doctor] were you wearing a helmet ?
[patient] yeah , full face helmet , and my jacket .
[doctor] good . did you hit your head ?
[patient] the helmet hit the road a little , but i did n't black out or anything . i remember the whole thing .
[doctor] any headache , nausea , blurry vision since then ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] okay . and where is the pain exactly ?
[patient] it's like right here , on the collarbone . there's a big bump there now .
[doctor] okay . and how bad is the pain ?
[patient] like a seven . it's really bad when i try to lift my arm .
[doctor] any numbness or tingling in your arm or your fingers ?
[patient] no , my hand feels fine .
[doctor] okay . any other injuries ? any pain in your chest , your ribs , your hips ?
[patient] just some road rash on my right forearm , like scrapes , but the jacket took most of it . my buddy cleaned it up .
[doctor] okay . did you go to the emergency room ?
[patient] no , i probably should have . i just put my arm in a sling i had at home and took some advil .
[doctor] okay . do you have any medical problems ?
[patient] no , not really .
[doctor] do you smoke ?
[patient] yeah , about a pack a day .
[doctor] how long have you been smoking ?
[patient] since i was like 16 .
[doctor] okay . so i do wanna talk to you about that , because smoking actually slows down bone healing quite a bit .
[patient] really ? i did n't know that .
[doctor] yeah . have you ever tried to quit ?
[patient] i tried once with the gum . i made it about a month . i get cravings first thing in the morning , i usually light one up within like 10 minutes of waking up .
[doctor] okay . would you be interested in trying again ?
[patient] yeah , i mean , if it's gonna help this heal , i'll try .
[doctor] okay . let's take a look at you . so , on exam , there's an obvious deformity over the middle of the right clavicle , with swelling and bruising . the skin is intact , it's not tented . i'm gonna press here gently .

[patient] okay .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right shoulder pain after motorcycle accident.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Malik Jablonski is a 67-year-old male who presents with right clavicle pain after a motorcycle accident on Saturday.

The patient was the driver of a motorcycle on a two-lane state road during a weekend ride when he lost control on gravel in a curve. The rear tire slid out and he laid the bike down, landing on his right shoulder. No other vehicles were involved. He was wearing a full-face helmet and riding jacket. His helmet struck the road, but he denies loss of consciousness, headache, nausea, or blurry vision. He reports pain over the right collarbone with a visible bump, rated 7/10, worse with arm elevation. He denies numbness or tingling. He also sustained abrasions to the right forearm. He did not seek emergency care. He has been using a sling and Advil.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Smokes 1 pack per day since age 16. Smokes within 10 minutes of waking. Previously tried nicotine gum with 1 month of abstinence. He is interested in quitting. He works as an electrician.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Right shoulder: Obvious deformity over the midshaft of the right clavicle with swelling and ecchymosis. Skin intact, not tented. Tender to palpation over the midshaft clavicle.
Neurovascular: Radial pulse intact. Sensation intact in the hand. Full finger motion and grip.
Skin: Healing abrasions on the right forearm, clean, without signs of infection.

RESULTS

X-ray of the right clavicle: Displaced midshaft clavicle fracture with approximately 1 cm of shortening. No comminution.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Displaced fracture of the shaft of the right clavicle, closed.
- Nonoperative management with sling for comfort for 2 to 3 weeks.
- Gentle elbow, wrist, and hand range of motion.
- Light duty at work for at least 6 weeks.

[doctor] did you pass out at all ?

[doctor] okay , good . and how's the pain ?
[patient] it's pretty bad . like a seven out of 10 . it's throbbing , and it's swollen .
[doctor] any numbness or tingling in your fingers ?
[patient] my fingers felt a little tingly last night , but it's better this morning .
[doctor] okay . is it in your thumb and index finger ?
[patient] yeah , kind of the thumb side .
[doctor] okay . we'll keep an eye on that . any other injuries ?
[patient] i scraped up my left knee , but it's just a scrape .
[doctor] okay . what have you taken for pain ?

[doctor] good . any other medical problems ?
[patient] just asthma .
[doctor] okay . how's your asthma been doing lately ?

[doctor] okay . any nighttime coughing or waking up short of breath ?
[patient] no , not really .

[doctor] i know . and for your asthma , i want you to use the fluticasone every day , twice a day , and keep the albuterol for rescue .
[patient] okay , i'll try .
[doctor] all right , we'll get you into a cast and see you back in one week with an x-ray .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right wrist injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Aisha Mbeki is a 58-year-old female with a history of asthma who presents for evaluation of a right wrist injury sustained on 02/05/2023.

The patient was riding her bicycle to work in the bike lane of a residential street when a car turning right struck her rear wheel. She fell onto an outstretched right hand on the pavement. She was wearing a helmet and denies significant head strike or loss of consciousness. She was evaluated at urgent care, where x-rays were obtained and a splint was applied. She reports throbbing pain rated 7/10 and swelling. She had transient tingling in the radial-sided fingers overnight, which has improved. She also sustained a left knee abrasion. She has been taking Tylenol, icing, and elevating.

Regarding her asthma, she uses albuterol about once weekly, mainly in cold weather while cycling. She is prescribed fluticasone twice daily but uses it approximately 5 days per week. She denies nocturnal symptoms. She tolerates ibuprofen without bronchospasm.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Right wrist: Swelling with dorsal angulation (dinner fork deformity). Tender over the distal radius. Thumb opposition intact. Sensation intact. Capillary refill normal.
Left knee: Superficial abrasion, clean.
Lungs: Clear to auscultation. No wheezing.

RESULTS

X-ray of the right wrist: Extra-articular distal radius fracture with dorsal angulation, consistent with a Colles' fracture, mildly angulated, acceptable alignment.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Colles' fracture of the right radius, closed.
- Short arm cast applied today.
- Weekly x-rays for 2 to 3 weeks to monitor alignment; surgical fixation if displacement occurs.
- Elevation and finger range of motion.
- Advil 600 mg three times daily with food, alternating with Tylenol.
- Return precautions for worsening numbness, tingling, swelling, or cold fingers.
- No cycling until fracture healed.

2. Asthma, uncomplicated.
- Counseled on daily adherence to fluticasone twice daily.
- Continue albuterol as needed.

Follow up in 1 week with x-ray.

dialogue:
[doctor] mr. szymanski , good afternoon . how are you doing ?
[patient] oh , i've had better weeks , doctor .
[doctor] i heard . your grandson marcus called the office and said you got hit by a car ?
[patient] well , sort of . it was tuesday . i'd parked at the grocery store , and i was walking across the parking lot to go in . and this lady was backing out of her spot , and she did n't see me , and she backed right into me .
[doctor] goodness . how fast was she going ?
[patient] not fast , thank god . but the bumper caught me right on the left hip and knocked me down . i landed on that same side , on the asphalt .
[doctor] so you were on foot , walking , and the car backed into you in the lot .
[patient] that's right . i was just walking in to get my groceries like i do every week .
[doctor] okay . did you hit your head when you fell ?
[patient] no , i caught myself with my hands , and my hip took the rest .
[doctor] okay . were you able to get up afterwards ?
[patient] yeah , the lady and a young fella helped me up . i was able to walk , but i was limping . they wanted to call an ambulance , but i said no .
[doctor] okay . and how has the hip been since then ?
[patient] it's sore . it's bruised up , big purple bruise , and it's tender when i lie on that side at night . walking hurts some , maybe a four or five out of 10 . i've been using my cane , which i usually do n't need .
[doctor] any pain in the groin ?
[patient] no , it's more on the outside .
[doctor] okay . any pain in your back , your neck , your wrists ?
[patient] my hands were a little scraped up but they're fine now .
[doctor] okay . now , the big thing i'm thinking about is you're on a blood thinner for your atrial fibrillation , right ? the eliquis ?
[patient] yes , 5 milligrams twice a day .
[doctor] okay . and have you noticed the bruise getting bigger ? any swelling that keeps spreading ?
[patient] it got bigger the first day , but it seems about the same now .
[doctor] okay . any blood in your urine , black stools , nosebleeds ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] any lightheadedness , dizziness ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] okay . and how's your heart been ? any palpitations , racing , fluttering ?
[patient] no , i feel fine with that . i take the metoprolol every day too .
[doctor] okay , good . metoprolol 25 milligrams twice a day ?
[patient] yes .
[doctor] okay . let's take a look . go ahead and stand up for me . so there's a large bruise over the outside of the left hip , about the size of my hand , and it's tender right over the bone here . there's no hard knot underneath , nothing that feels like a big collection of blood . i'm gonna move your leg around . does this hurt ? bending it up ?
[patient] a little bit .
[doctor] and rolling it in and out ?
[patient] no , that's okay .
[doctor] okay . no pain with log roll , which is reassuring . can you lift your leg straight up off the table ?
[patient] yeah .
[doctor] good . your leg is not shortened or turned out . your heart is irregular , which is what we expect with your afib , and the rate is good at about 72 .
[doctor] so we did an x-ray of your hip and your pelvis here today . there's no fracture , the hip joint looks good . you have some arthritis , which is normal at your age . and your blood count is stable , your hemoglobin is 13.1 , which is the same as it was in the spring .
[patient] oh , good .
[doctor] so what you have is a contusion , a deep bruise , of the left hip from being struck by the car . because you're on eliquis , these bruises can look really dramatic , but your blood count is stable and the bruise is n't expanding .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so i want you to continue the eliquis 5 milligrams twice a day . the risk of stroke if we stop it is higher than the risk from this bruise . you can ice the hip 20 minutes at a time , and take tylenol for pain , up to 3000 milligrams a day . please do n't take advil or aleve while you're on the eliquis .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] keep using your cane for the next couple of weeks until you're steady . and if the bruise starts getting bigger , or the hip gets very swollen or hard , or you feel lightheaded , i want you to call right away or go to the emergency room .
[patient] i will .
[doctor] and for the afib , continue the metoprolol 25 milligrams twice a day . your heart rate is well controlled .
[patient] okay . thank you , doctor .
[doctor] let's see you back in two weeks .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left hip pain after being struck by a car.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Harold Szymanski is a 31-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation on apixaban who presents with left hip pain after a pedestrian accident on 06/04/2020.

The patient was walking across a grocery store parking lot when a car backing out of a parking space struck him on the left hip at low speed. He was knocked down onto the asphalt, landing on his left side. He denies head strike. He was able to ambulate afterwards with a limp. Emergency services were not called. He reports lateral left hip pain rated 4-5/10, worse when lying on the left side and with walking, with a large bruise. He has needed his cane since the incident. He denies groin pain. He had minor abrasions to the hands which have healed. He denies hematuria, melena, epistaxis, lightheadedness, or dizziness.

Regarding his atrial fibrillation, he takes Eliquis 5 mg twice daily and metoprolol 25 mg twice daily. He denies palpitations.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Cardiovascular: Irregularly irregular rhythm, rate 72.
Left hip: Large ecchymosis over the lateral hip, approximately hand-sized. Tender over the greater trochanter. No palpable hematoma. Mild pain with hip flexion. No pain with log roll. Able to perform straight leg raise. No limb shortening or external rotation.

RESULTS

X-ray of the left hip and pelvis: No fracture. Mild degenerative changes of the hip joint.

Hemoglobin 13.1, stable compared to prior.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Contusion of the left hip.
- Pedestrian struck by a car in a parking lot while walking.
- No fracture on imaging. Hemoglobin stable and no expanding hematoma.
- Ice 20 minutes at a time. Tylenol up to 3000 mg daily. Avoid NSAIDs.
- Continue cane for ambulation.
- Return precautions for expanding bruising, swelling, firmness, or lightheadedness.

2. Atrial fibrillation.
- Rate controlled.
- Continue Eliquis 5 mg twice daily; benefit of stroke prevention outweighs bleeding risk.
- Continue metoprolol 25 mg twice daily.

Follow up in 2 weeks.

[doctor] hi there , jacqueline ? i'm doctor sorensen .
[patient] hi .
[doctor] so what brings you in today ?
[patient] so , um , i fell off one of those electric scooters , the rental ones , and i hurt my elbow .
[doctor] oh no . when did this happen ?
[patient] february second , so like three days ago . i was riding it back from class , i'm a junior at the university , and i was on the sidewalk on the way to my apartment .
[doctor] okay . and what happened ?
[patient] so the front wheel , it's like a really small wheel , it caught in a crack in the sidewalk where the concrete was all broken up , and the scooter just stopped and i flew forward . i put my right arm out and landed on my hand , and like , my elbow kind of jammed .
[doctor] okay . did anything else hit you , like a car , or a pole , or another person ?
[patient] no , nothing , it was just the crack . i just fell .
[doctor] were you going fast ?
[patient] i mean , i think those things go like 15 miles an hour , and i was probably going full speed .
[doctor] were you wearing a helmet ?
[patient] no . i know , i know .
[doctor] did you hit your head ?
[patient] no , i did n't , luckily . i landed mostly on my arm and my knees .
[doctor] okay . and what kind of pain are you having ?
[patient] it's on the outside of my elbow . it hurts to straighten it all the way , and turning my hand over , like to turn a doorknob or open a jar , that really hurts .
[doctor] how bad is it ?
[patient] like a six . if i try to straighten it , like an eight .
[doctor] okay . any numbness or tingling in your hand ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] any pain in your wrist ?
[patient] a little bit at first , but now it's mostly the elbow .
[doctor] okay . what have you done for it ?
[patient] my roommate maria made me ice it , and i've been taking ibuprofen . i've been kind of keeping it bent , because that's comfortable .
[doctor] okay . do you have any medical problems ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] take any medicines regularly ?
[patient] just birth control .
[doctor] any allergies ?
[patient] penicillin , i get a rash .
[doctor] okay . let me take a look . so i'm looking at your right elbow , there's some swelling on the outside . i'm gonna press here , right over the radial head .
[patient] ow . yes , that's it .
[doctor] okay . that's point tender . and on the inside of the elbow ? here ?
[patient] no , that's fine .
[doctor] and the wrist ? here on the forearm ?
[patient] that's okay .
[doctor] okay . go ahead and straighten your arm as much as you can .
[patient] that's as far as it goes .
[doctor] so you're missing about 20 degrees of extension . now turn your palm up , and palm down .
[patient] ow , that hurts .
[doctor] okay , pain with supination and pronation . but you're able to rotate it , that's important . squeeze my fingers . good . sensation is normal . you also have some scrapes on both knees , those look like they're healing fine .
[doctor] so we took an x-ray of your elbow . there's a small crack in the radial head , that's the top of one of the forearm bones where it meets the elbow . the piece is not shifted , it's a nondisplaced fracture of the head of the right radius . there's also a fat pad sign , which means there's a little bit of blood in the joint .
[patient] okay , so it's broken ?
[doctor] it is , but this is one of the good ones to have . these heal really well without surgery . we're gonna put you in a sling for comfort , but i actually want you to start moving it within a few days , because the biggest problem with these is stiffness .
[patient] okay .

[patient] okay .

[patient] yeah , i think i'm done with those .
[doctor] we'll see you back in two weeks with another x-ray , and we'll probably start physical therapy if it's stiff .
[patient] sounds good , thank you .

University student.

dialogue:
[doctor] hello , mrs. bergstrom . i'm doctor bartholomew ferreira , i'm one of the orthopedic doctors .
[patient] hello , doctor . excuse me if i do n't shake your hand .
[doctor] no , of course not . i can see that arm is in a sling . so tell me how this happened .
[patient] well , i was on the bus , going to my book club at the library like i do on thursdays . and it was crowded , so i was standing , holding onto the pole .
[doctor] okay .
[patient] and somebody pulled out in front of the bus , i think , and the driver slammed on the brakes . really hard . and i just went flying . i lost my grip and i fell forward and landed on my right shoulder on the floor of the bus .
[doctor] oh my . so the bus did n't actually hit anything ? it was just the sudden stop ?
[patient] no , he did n't hit anybody . he stopped in time . it was just the braking . we were going down the main avenue in provo , right in the middle of traffic .
[doctor] okay . did you hit your head ?
[patient] no , i do n't think so . my shoulder took all of it .
[doctor] did you black out ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] okay . and then what happened ?
[patient] well , the driver called an ambulance and they took me to the emergency room . they did x-rays and said i broke the top of my arm bone , and they gave me this sling and told me to see you .
[doctor] okay . how's the pain now ?
[patient] oh , it's bad , especially at night . i ca n't lie down , i've been sleeping in my recliner . maybe a seven .
[doctor] okay . any numbness or tingling down your arm or in your fingers ?
[patient] no , my fingers feel okay .
[doctor] okay . and what are you taking for the pain ?
[patient] they gave me some tramadol , but it makes me dizzy , so i've just been taking tylenol .
[doctor] okay . now i see in your chart you have osteoporosis .
[patient] yes . they found that on my bone density scan about three years ago .
[doctor] okay . and what are you taking for it ?
[patient] i take the alendronate once a week , on sundays , and calcium and vitamin d every day .
[doctor] good . and have you had any other fractures ?
[patient] i broke my wrist about five years ago when i slipped on some ice .
[doctor] okay . so this kind of fracture , from a fall like that , is what we call a fragility fracture . it tells us your bones are still pretty fragile .
[patient] i was afraid of that .
[doctor] okay . let me take a look . i'll be gentle . so there's a lot of bruising here , going down the upper arm , and it's swollen around the shoulder . i'm gonna press very gently here at the top of the arm .

[patient] okay .

[doctor] do you have help at home ?
[patient] my son owen has been coming by every day .
[doctor] good . and when you ride the bus again , try to get a seat , and if you ca n't , ask someone .
[patient] oh , believe me , i will .

[doctor] hello , mrs. weatherby . i'm doctor yasmin donnelly , i'm one of the orthopedic doctors .
[patient] hello , doctor . excuse me if i do n't shake your hand .
[doctor] no , of course not . i can see that arm is in a sling . so tell me how this happened .
[patient] well , i was on the bus , going to my book club at the library like i do on thursdays . and it was crowded , so i was standing , holding onto the pole .
[doctor] okay .
[patient] and somebody pulled out in front of the bus , i think , and the driver slammed on the brakes . really hard . and i just went flying . i lost my grip and i fell forward and landed on my right shoulder on the floor of the bus .
[doctor] oh my . so the bus did n't actually hit anything ? it was just the sudden stop ?
[patient] no , he did n't hit anybody . he stopped in time . it was just the braking . we were going down the main avenue in cheyenne , right in the middle of traffic .
[doctor] okay . did you hit your head ?
[patient] no , i do n't think so . my shoulder took all of it .
[doctor] did you black out ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] okay . and then what happened ?
[patient] well , the driver called an ambulance and they took me to the emergency room . they did x-rays and said i broke the top of my arm bone , and they gave me this sling and told me to see you .
[doctor] okay . how's the pain now ?
[patient] oh , it's bad , especially at night . i ca n't lie down , i've been sleeping in my recliner . maybe a seven .
[doctor] okay . any numbness or tingling down your arm or in your fingers ?
[patient] no , my fingers feel okay .
[doctor] okay . and what are you taking for the pain ?
[patient] they gave me some tramadol , but it makes me dizzy , so i've just been taking tylenol .
[doctor] okay . now i see in your chart you have osteoporosis .
[patient] yes . they found that on my bone density scan about three years ago .
[doctor] okay . and what are you taking for it ?
[patient] i take the alendronate once a week , on sundays , and calcium and vitamin d every day .
[doctor] good . and have you had any other fractures ?
[patient] i broke my wrist about five years ago when i slipped on some ice .
[doctor] okay . so this kind of fracture , from a fall like that , is what we call a fragility fracture . it tells us your bones are still pretty fragile .
[patient] i was afraid of that .
[doctor] okay . let me take a look . i'll be gentle . so there's a lot of bruising here , going down the upper arm , and it's swollen around the shoulder . i'm gonna press very gently here at the top of the arm .
[patient] ooh , yes .
[doctor] okay . i'm not gonna try to move the shoulder because it'll hurt . can you bend your elbow ? and make a fist ? and spread your fingers ?
[patient] yes .
[doctor] good . and can you feel me touching here on the outside of your shoulder ?
[patient] yes .
[doctor] okay . that's good , that tells me the nerve there is working . and your pulse at the wrist is strong .
[doctor] so i looked at your x-rays from the emergency room . you have a fracture of the upper end of the right humerus , right at the part we call the surgical neck . the ball part is shifted a little bit compared to the shaft , so it is displaced , but it's in two main pieces and the ball is still sitting in the socket .
[patient] do i need an operation ?

[patient] okay . that's a relief .
[doctor] i'll give you a handout with the pendulum exercises . for pain , keep taking tylenol , 1000 milligrams three times a day , and ice . i'd like to get another x-ray in one week to make sure it has n't moved .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] for your osteoporosis , continue the alendronate once a week , and your calcium and vitamin d . i'm gonna send a note to your primary care doctor , because with a second fracture , they may want to talk about a stronger medicine .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] and are you still working at all ?
[patient] oh , no . i'm retired . i taught third grade for thirty five years .
[doctor] do you have help at home ?
[patient] my son wendy has been coming by every day .
[doctor] good . and when you ride the bus again , try to get a seat , and if you ca n't , ask someone .
[patient] oh , believe me , i will .

Right shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Chloe Weatherby is a 84-year-old female with osteoporosis who presents for evaluation of a right proximal humerus fracture sustained on 04/01/2021.

The patient was a standing passenger on a city bus in traffic, on her way to a book club, when the driver braked suddenly to avoid a vehicle. There was no collision. She lost her grip on the pole, fell forward, and landed on her right shoulder on the floor of the bus. She denies head injury or loss of consciousness. She was transported by ambulance to the emergency department, where x-rays demonstrated a proximal humerus fracture, and she was placed in a sling. She reports pain rated 7/10, worse at night; she has been sleeping in a recliner. She denies numbness or tingling. Tramadol caused dizziness, so she has been taking Tylenol.

Osteoporosis was diagnosed on DEXA scan 3 years ago. She takes alendronate weekly plus calcium and vitamin D. Prior distal radius fracture 5 years ago after a fall on ice.

SOCIAL HISTORY

She is a retired elementary school teacher. Her son assists her daily.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Right shoulder: Ecchymosis extending down the upper arm. Swelling about the shoulder. Tender to palpation over the proximal humerus. Range of motion of the shoulder deferred due to pain.
Neurovascular: Elbow flexion, grip, and finger abduction intact. Sensation intact over the lateral shoulder (axillary nerve distribution). Radial pulse 2+.

RESULTS

X-rays of the right shoulder: Two-part displaced fracture of the surgical neck of the right humerus. Humeral head located within the glenoid. Alignment acceptable for nonoperative management.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Displaced fracture of the surgical neck of the right humerus, closed.
- Injury occurred as a standing bus passenger thrown forward during sudden braking.
- Nonoperative management. Continue sling.
- Begin pendulum exercises at 2 weeks, then physical therapy.
- Tylenol 1000 mg three times daily. Ice.
- Repeat x-ray in 1 week.

2. Age-related osteoporosis.
- Fragility fracture.
- Continue alendronate weekly, calcium, and vitamin D.
- Communicated with primary care regarding consideration of anabolic therapy given second fracture.

dialogue:
[doctor] reginald , how you doing ?
[patient] been better , doc . been better .
[doctor] i bet . so your wife kateryna brought you in , she said you rolled your four-wheeler ?
[patient] yeah . i did . pretty dumb .
[doctor] well , tell me what happened .
[patient] so this was september fifth . we run cattle on our place , about two hundred head , out past des moines , and i was out in the back pasture on the four-wheeler , the atv , checking fence line . part of the farm is real hilly . i was going across the side of a hill , and the front tire dropped into a hole , like a washout , and the whole thing just tipped over on me .
[doctor] okay . so it rolled on top of you ?
[patient] it rolled once , and it kind of came down on my left side . i was pinned under it for a minute , and then i got it pushed off .
[doctor] okay . this was out in the field , not on a road ?
[patient] no , no road . out in the middle of the hay field .
[doctor] okay . and this is your farm , you work it full time ?
[patient] yes sir , that's my living . been farming it my whole life , my dad did before me .
[doctor] were you wearing a helmet ?
[patient] no . nobody wears a helmet out there .
[doctor] okay . did you hit your head , or lose consciousness ?
[patient] no , i do n't think so . i remember everything . it just knocked the wind out of me .
[doctor] okay . and where are you hurting ?
[patient] my left ribs . right along here , on the side and kind of the back . it hurts real bad to take a breath , and coughing , oh , forget it . sneezing about killed me yesterday .
[doctor] how would you rate it ?
[patient] when i'm still , a five , maybe . when i breathe in deep or move , a nine .
[doctor] okay . any shortness of breath ?
[patient] a little bit , mostly because it hurts to breathe .
[doctor] any coughing up blood ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] any pain in your belly , like on the left side , up under the ribs ?
[patient] no , not the belly .
[doctor] any blood in your urine ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] okay . and you waited two days to come in .
[patient] yeah , i figured it was just bruised . but kateryna made me come in after i could n't sleep last night .
[doctor] she was right . what have you been taking ?
[patient] some advil .
[doctor] okay . now , you're also on a cholesterol medicine , right ? the atorvastatin ?
[patient] yeah , 20 milligrams .
[doctor] taking that every day ?
[patient] most days . i forget it sometimes when i'm up early for chores .
[doctor] okay . any muscle aches from it ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] okay . let me take a look at you . i'm gonna listen to your lungs first . take a breath in . and out . okay , breath sounds are present on both sides , a little decreased at the left base because you're not taking a full breath . i'm gonna press gently along the ribs .
[patient] ah , yeah , that's it .

[patient] okay .

[patient] okay .

[patient] my nephew can help out .
[doctor] good . and if you get more short of breath , a fever , or cough up blood , come straight back .
[patient] all right .
[doctor] for your cholesterol , we'll continue the atorvastatin 20 milligrams . try to take it at night , so you do n't miss it in the morning rush . we'll check your lipids at your next visit .
[patient] sounds good .
