dialogue:
[doctor] hey wojciech , i'm doctor whitmore . what's going on with the shoulder ?
[patient] hey doc . so , i had a little accident on a jet ski last weekend .
[doctor] okay , let's hear it .
[patient] so a bunch of us rented a cabin up at dunmore pier for my buddy ingrid's bachelor party , and we rented a couple of jet skis . and we were out on the lake , just cruising around , jumping some wakes , having fun .
[doctor] okay .
[patient] and i was kind of looking back at my buddies and not paying attention , and i ran right into one of those big orange marker buoys . like full speed .
[doctor] oh boy . so the jet ski hit the buoy ?
[patient] yeah , the front of it hit the buoy , and the jet ski stopped dead , and i got launched over the handlebars . i hit the buoy with my right shoulder on the way over , and then i went in the water .
[doctor] okay . were you wearing a life jacket ?
[patient] yes , they make you wear one when you rent them . that's probably a good thing , because my arm was pretty useless .
[doctor] okay . did you hit your head ?
[patient] no , just the shoulder .
[doctor] did you swallow a lot of water , any trouble breathing afterwards ?
[patient] no , i swallowed a little , but i was fine . my buddies pulled me up onto their jet ski and we went back to the dock .
[doctor] okay . had you been drinking at all ?
[patient] no , not then . it was like ten in the morning .
[doctor] okay , fair enough . so tell me about the pain .
[patient] it's right on the top of my shoulder , like at the end of my collarbone . there's a bump there that was n't there before . and when i try to reach across my body , or lift my arm over my head , it really hurts .
[doctor] okay . how would you rate it ?
[patient] when i'm resting it's like a three . reaching across , a seven .
[doctor] any numbness or tingling in your arm ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] any weakness ?
[patient] it feels weak , but i think that's because it hurts .
[doctor] okay . what have you been doing for it ?
[patient] ice , and ibuprofen . i've been wearing my arm in a sling that the urgent care up there gave me .
[doctor] okay . any other medical problems ?
[patient] no , i'm pretty healthy .
[doctor] okay . what do you do for work ?
[patient] i'm a high school chemistry teacher , so mostly i'm writing on the board .
[doctor] okay . let me take a look . so , looking at both shoulders , there's a visible bump at the top of your right shoulder , where the collarbone meets the shoulder blade . that's your ac joint . i'm gonna press here .
[patient] yeah , ow , that's the spot .
[doctor] okay . tender right over the ac joint . i'm gonna bring your arm across your body .
[patient] oh , yeah , that hurts .
[doctor] okay , positive cross arm test . the collarbone moves a little up and down when i push on it . your rotator cuff strength is good when i test it , though it's a little painful . sensation is normal , pulse is normal .
[doctor] so we got x-rays of both shoulders to compare . on the right side , the end of the collarbone is sitting a little higher than the shoulder blade , compared to the left . it's not completely separated , it's partly out of place . there's no fracture .
[patient] okay , so what is it ?
[doctor] so , you have what's called a shoulder separation , or an ac joint subluxation , on the right side . it's a grade two injury , which means the ligaments are stretched and partly torn , but not completely .
[patient] does that need surgery ?
[doctor] no . grade two injuries do really well without surgery . the bump may not go away completely , but it usually does n't affect function .
[patient] okay , good .
[doctor] so , use the sling for comfort for about one to two weeks . then you can start moving it as the pain allows . i'm gonna send you to physical therapy to work on range of motion and strength . ibuprofen 600 milligrams up to three times a day with food , and ice for 20 minutes a few times a day .
[patient] can i still go to the gym ?
[doctor] lower body , sure . no bench press , no pushups , no overhead lifting for about six weeks .
[patient] and the jet skis ?
[doctor] maybe give those a rest for the summer . and keep your eyes forward next time .
[patient] yeah , lesson learned .
[doctor] see you in three weeks .

Wojciech Mendoza is a 20-year-old male who presents with right shoulder pain after a personal watercraft accident on 06/27/2024.

The patient was riding a rented jet ski recreationally on a lake when he collided at full speed with a marker buoy. The jet ski stopped abruptly and he was thrown over the handlebars, striking his right shoulder on the buoy before falling into the water. He was wearing a life jacket. He denies head injury, aspiration symptoms, or difficulty breathing. He denies alcohol use at the time of injury. He reports pain over the top of the right shoulder with a new bump, rated 3/10 at rest and 7/10 with cross-body adduction and overhead reaching. He reports subjective weakness due to pain. He denies numbness or tingling. He was seen at an urgent care, given a sling, and has used ice and ibuprofen.

SOCIAL HISTORY

He works as a high school chemistry teacher.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Right shoulder: Visible prominence of the distal clavicle at the acromioclavicular joint. Tender to palpation over the AC joint. Positive cross-arm adduction test. Mild vertical instability of the distal clavicle. Rotator cuff strength 5/5 with pain. Neurovascularly intact.

RESULTS

Bilateral shoulder x-rays: Elevation of the right distal clavicle relative to the acromion compared to the contralateral side, consistent with partial displacement. No fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Subluxation of the right acromioclavicular joint (grade II AC separation).
- Jet ski collision with a buoy on a lake with fall from the watercraft.
- Nonoperative management. Sling for comfort for 1 to 2 weeks, then range of motion as tolerated.
- Physical therapy referral for range of motion and strengthening.
- Ibuprofen 600 mg up to three times daily with food. Ice 20 minutes several times daily.
- No bench press, pushups, or overhead lifting for 6 weeks.

Follow up in 3 weeks.

Left ankle injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Priya Szymanski is a 34-year-old female with hypothyroidism who presents for evaluation of a left ankle fracture sustained while getting off a train.

The patient was commuting to work by commuter train. While stepping off the train onto the platform at the railway station, her left foot slipped into the gap between the train and the platform, and she sustained an inversion injury to the left ankle with an audible pop. She fell onto the platform and was unable to bear weight. She denies head injury and had minor abrasions to the hands. She was evaluated at urgent care, where x-rays showed a fracture, and she was placed in a splint with crutches. She reports throbbing pain rated 6/10, primarily over the lateral ankle, with mild medial ankle pain. She denies numbness or tingling. She has been taking ibuprofen and elevating.

Regarding her hypothyroidism, she takes levothyroxine 75 mcg daily. She reports increased fatigue over the last 2 months and a 5-pound weight gain. She has been taking levothyroxine with coffee and calcium. She does not smoke.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Works as an accountant.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Left ankle: Lateral swelling and ecchymosis. Tender to palpation over the lateral malleolus. Mild medial tenderness. Toes warm. Pulses intact. Sensation intact.

RESULTS

X-rays of the left ankle: Displaced fracture of the lateral malleolus of the left fibula with approximately 3 mm displacement. Mild widening of the medial clear space, concerning for instability.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Displaced fracture of the lateral malleolus of the left fibula, closed.
- Injury occurred while alighting from a train at the railway station.
- Recommend open reduction and internal fixation within 1 week once swelling improves.
- Splint, non-weight bearing with crutches, elevation.
- Enoxaparin for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis while non-weight bearing.
- Work note provided.

2. Hypothyroidism.
- Symptoms of fatigue and weight gain, possibly related to impaired absorption.
- Counseled to take levothyroxine on an empty stomach 30 to 60 minutes before coffee and food, separated from calcium.
- TSH today; recheck in 6 weeks.

[doctor] okay . and how high up was the shelf ?
[patient] the top rack , so like twelve , fourteen feet .
[doctor] were you wearing any kind of helmet or hard hat ?
[patient] no , we just wear vests and safety shoes .
[doctor] okay . did you get knocked out at all ?
[patient] no , i do n't think so . i went down on one knee , but i remember the whole thing . my supervisor thuy came running over and i was talking to her right away .
[doctor] okay , good . and what symptoms did you have afterwards ?
[patient] right away i was really dizzy and i had a bad headache , right on the top of my head . i felt kind of foggy , like i could n't think straight . and last night i felt sick to my stomach .
[doctor] did you throw up ?
[patient] no , just nauseous .
[doctor] okay . how about now ?
[patient] the headache is still there , maybe a five out of ten . the lights in here are bothering me a little . and i'm still kind of slow , like i'm in a fog .
[doctor] any blurry vision or double vision ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] any weakness or numbness in your arms or legs ? trouble talking ?
[patient] no , nothing like that .
[doctor] any neck pain ?
[patient] a little bit stiff , but not bad .
[doctor] okay . did you sleep okay ?

[patient] just tylenol .
[doctor] good , that's the right choice . try to avoid ibuprofen and aspirin for the first couple of days . now , you're also on a cholesterol medicine , right ?
[patient] yes , the atorvastatin . twenty milligrams .
[doctor] and are you taking it every day ?
[patient] yes , every night .
[doctor] any muscle aches with it ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] okay . your last lipid panel from the spring showed your ldl at one twenty , which is better than it was . we'll keep going with that .
[patient] okay .

MRN: mrn739251
DATE OF SERVICE: 03/02/2019

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left thumb laceration.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Harriet Fitzgerald is a 42-year-old right-hand-dominant female with no significant past medical history who presents with a laceration to the left thumb.

The patient states that last night at approximately 6:30 PM, while preparing dinner in the kitchen of her home, she was cutting a butternut squash with a chef's knife when the knife slipped and cut the palmar aspect of her left thumb. She reports significant bleeding, controlled with direct pressure using a dish towel, but recurrent when pressure was released. She reports mild numbness at the radial aspect of the thumb tip. She is able to flex and extend the thumb. She denies use of anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents. Tetanus status unknown, likely more than 10 years.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Left thumb: 2.5 cm linear laceration over the volar interphalangeal joint, through the dermis into the subcutaneous fat. No exposed tendon. Nail and nail bed not involved. Mild oozing. FPL and thenar flexion intact against resistance. Decreased two-point discrimination over the radial digital tip. Capillary refill brisk.

PROCEDURE

Digital block with 1% lidocaine without epinephrine. Copious irrigation with normal saline. Wound explored under bloodless field; no tendon injury or foreign body identified. Closed with 6 simple interrupted 5-0 nylon sutures. Tetanus-diphtheria-pertussis (Tdap) vaccine administered.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Laceration without foreign body of the left thumb without damage to nail.
• Medical Reasoning: Knife laceration sustained while cutting food in the home kitchen. Possible partial radial digital nerve injury versus neurapraxia from swelling.
• Medical Treatment: Repair as above. Keep dressing clean and dry for 48 hours. Tylenol or ibuprofen as needed. Suture removal in 10 days.
• Specialist Referrals: Hand surgery follow up within 1 week for sensory evaluation.
• Patient Education and Counseling: Return for spreading redness, purulent drainage, fever, or worsening numbness.

Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

[doctor] hey , pedro , how's it going ? i'm doctor kovacs .
[patient] hey . it's going , i guess . my hand is killing me .
[doctor] yeah , let's talk about that . i see it's your right hand . what happened ?
[patient] so i'm a line cook at delta pipefitters local 12 , the restaurant downtown . last night during the dinner rush i was working the saute station , cooking , and i had a cast iron skillet in the oven for a steak . i pulled it out with a towel , set it on the stove , and then like an idiot i grabbed the handle with my bare hand to move it .
[doctor] oh , no .
[patient] yeah . it had been in a five hundred degree oven . i let go right away but it was too late .
[doctor] okay . so the skillet handle was right across your palm ?
[patient] yeah , right across the palm , kind of from here to here .
[doctor] okay . what did you do right after ?
[patient] i ran it under cold water in the prep sink for like ten , fifteen minutes . my chef put some burn gel from the first aid kit on it and wrapped it . i finished the shift , which was probably dumb .
[doctor] it happens a lot in kitchens . and how does it look today compared to last night ?
[patient] it blistered overnight . there's a couple big blisters now , and one of them popped this morning .
[doctor] okay . how's the pain ?
[patient] it's like an eight when it's uncovered . the air hitting it really hurts .
[doctor] okay , that actually tells me the nerve endings are still there , which is a good thing . any burns anywhere else ? your fingers , your wrist , your forearm ?
[patient] no , just the palm . my fingers are okay .
[doctor] okay . any trouble moving your fingers ?
[patient] it hurts to make a fist because it stretches the skin , but i can move them .
[doctor] okay . any fevers or chills ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] do you have any medical problems ? diabetes , anything ?
[patient] no , i'm healthy . i do n't take any meds .
[doctor] any allergies ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] tetanus up to date ?
[patient] yeah , i got one last year .
[doctor] okay , good . let me take a look . go ahead and open your hand for me . so , on your right palm there's a burn that runs across the palm , about six centimeters by two centimeters . there are two large blisters , one intact and one ruptured with a moist pink wound bed underneath . it blanches when i press , and you can feel me touching it ?
[patient] yeah , definitely .
[doctor] okay . so this is a superficial partial thickness burn , what we call a second degree burn , of the right palm . the fingers and the back of your hand are spared . i'd estimate it at less than one percent of your body surface area .
[patient] okay . is it gonna scar ?
[doctor] these usually heal in about two weeks without much scarring , as long as we keep it clean and it does n't get infected . the palm is a high function area , so we want to keep it moving and keep it from getting tight .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so what i'm going to do today is debride the broken blister , clean it up , and leave the intact one alone for now . i'll put on silver sulfadiazine cream and a non-stick dressing with a bulky wrap . you'll change the dressing once a day .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] for pain , ibuprofen six hundred milligrams every six hours with food , and you can add tylenol in between . i'll give you a short course of something stronger for nighttime if you need it .
[patient] the ibuprofen should be fine .
[doctor] okay . for work , you ca n't be in the kitchen with an open burn on your hand . it's a food safety issue and it's an infection risk for you . so i'm writing you off work for one week , and then we'll recheck it .
[patient] my chef is not gonna be happy , but okay .
[doctor] i'll fill out the workers' comp form , since it happened at work . do you know the date it happened ?
[patient] last night , so february second .
[doctor] perfect . watch for spreading redness , pus , fever , or if the pain gets worse instead of better . and keep your fingers moving several times a day .
[patient] will do . thanks , doc .
[doctor] see you in a week .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Burn to the right palm.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Pedro Yoshida is a 77-year-old male with no significant past medical history who presents with a burn to the right palm sustained at work on February Second.

The patient is employed at delta pipefitters local 12. While cooking at the saute station in the restaurant kitchen during the dinner service, he grasped the handle of a cast iron skillet that had just been removed from a 500 degree oven with his bare right hand. He immediately released it and cooled the hand under running cold water for 10 to 15 minutes. Burn gel and a wrap were applied at work. Blisters developed overnight, one of which ruptured this morning. Pain is 8/10 when uncovered. He reports pain with fist formation due to skin stretch but full finger motion. No other burns. Denies fever or chills. Tetanus immunization within the past year. No medications. No known drug allergies.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Skin: Right palm with a 6 x 2 cm transverse burn. Two large bullae, one intact and one ruptured, with a moist pink blanching wound bed. Sensation intact to light touch. Digits, dorsal hand, and wrist spared. Less than 1% TBSA.
Musculoskeletal: Full active range of motion of all digits with discomfort at end flexion.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Second degree burn of the right palm.
• Medical Reasoning: Superficial partial thickness contact burn from a hot skillet handle while working in a restaurant kitchen. Small TBSA but functionally important location.
• Medical Treatment: Ruptured bulla debrided and wound cleansed; intact bulla left in place. Silver sulfadiazine cream with non-adherent dressing and bulky wrap, changed daily. Ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours with food; Tylenol as needed.
• Patient Education and Counseling: Finger range of motion exercises several times daily. Return precautions for signs of infection reviewed.
• Work: Off work for 1 week given food handling and infection risk. Workers' compensation form completed.

Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Follow up in 1 week for wound check.

Ximena Kovacs, MD

dialogue:
[doctor] victor ? hi , i'm doctor goldberg . so i see you came in with a nail in your hand .
[patient] yep . still in there .
[doctor] i can see that . okay , let's hear the story .
[patient] so i do framing for goodwin law offices . we're putting up a new house out in bozeman , it's just studs and plywood right now . this morning i was nailing off a wall section with the nail gun , and i was holding the stud with my left hand , kind of close to where i was shooting . the nail hit a knot or something , and it deflected , came out the side of the board and went right into my hand .
[doctor] okay . so it came through the wood first and then into your hand ?
[patient] yeah . it kind of curved out of the side of the stud .
[doctor] what kind of nail gun was it ?
[patient] a framing nailer , pneumatic . three and a quarter inch nails .
[doctor] okay . and where exactly did it go in ?
[patient] right here , the web between my thumb and my pointer finger , kind of on the palm side . you can see the head of it sticking out .
[doctor] okay , i see it . did anyone try to pull it out ?
[patient] my foreman harriet wanted to , but the safety guy said do n't touch it , so they cut off the strip and wrapped it and drove me here .
[doctor] that was the right call . good . what time did this happen ?
[patient] about nine thirty .
[doctor] okay . how's the pain ?
[patient] honestly it's like a six . it's more weird than painful . it throbs .
[doctor] any numbness or tingling in your fingers ?
[patient] my thumb feels a little bit tingly , but i can feel everything .
[doctor] okay . can you move your fingers ?
[patient] yeah , but moving the thumb hurts .
[doctor] okay , that makes sense . were you wearing gloves ?
[patient] no , not for nailing .
[doctor] okay . any medical problems ?
[patient] no , nothing .
[doctor] medications ?
[patient] nope .
[doctor] allergies ?
[patient] penicillin . i get hives .
[doctor] okay , good to know . and your last tetanus shot ?
[patient] no idea . a long time .
[doctor] okay . let me take a look . so on exam , there's a nail entering the palmar aspect of the left first web space , with about one centimeter of the shank and the head protruding . there's no active bleeding . there's mild swelling around it . your capillary refill is less than two seconds in all fingers . sensation is intact in all fingers , including the thumb . you can flex and extend all your fingers , and thumb opposition is intact though painful . i do n't see any signs of tendon injury .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] we got x-rays of the left hand . the nail goes in about four centimeters , through the soft tissue of the first web space . it's sitting between the first and second metacarpals , and it does n't go into the bone . no fracture . but this one has a barb on it , so i do n't want to just yank it out backwards .
[patient] okay , so how do you get it out ?
[doctor] i'm going to numb the area really well with a nerve block , then make a small incision along the nail so it comes out cleanly without tearing more tissue . then we'll irrigate it and leave it open to drain . we usually do n't stitch puncture wounds like this because of the infection risk .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] because this is a puncture wound with a foreign body , and those nails are not clean , i'm going to start you on an antibiotic . since you're allergic to penicillin , we'll use clindamycin , three hundred milligrams four times a day for five days . and you'll get a tetanus booster today .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] keep the hand elevated , change the dressing daily , and if you see redness spreading up the hand , pus , fever , or you ca n't move your thumb , come back right away . deep hand infections can get serious fast .
[patient] got it .
[doctor] work-wise , no use of the left hand on the job site for a week . no gripping , no power tools . i'll do the workers' comp paperwork since this happened at work on a construction site .
[patient] okay . my foreman's gonna love that .
[doctor] safety first . and wear gloves and keep that hand out of the line of fire next time .
[patient] yeah , lesson learned .
[doctor] i want to recheck it in two to three days . okay ?
[patient] sounds good .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Nail gun injury to the left hand.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Victor Kaminski is a 25-year-old male with no significant past medical history who presents with a nail gun injury to the left hand sustained at work earlier today.

The patient works in framing for Goodwin Law Offices. He was on a residential construction site where a house is under construction in Bozeman. At approximately 9:30 AM, while nailing a wall section with a pneumatic framing nailer, he was stabilizing the stud with his left hand. A 3.25 inch nail deflected off a knot, exited the side of the stud, and penetrated the palmar aspect of his left first web space. The nail was left in place and the collation strip was cut. He reports throbbing pain rated 6/10 and mild tingling of the thumb. No gloves were worn. Allergy to penicillin (hives). Tetanus status unknown.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Left hand: Nail entering the palmar first web space with approximately 1 cm of shank and head protruding. No active bleeding. Mild surrounding swelling. Capillary refill less than 2 seconds in all digits. Sensation intact in all digits. Full flexion and extension of all digits. Thumb opposition intact but painful. No signs of tendon injury.

RESULTS

X-ray of the left hand: Retained nail approximately 4 cm in length within the soft tissues of the first web space between the first and second metacarpals. Barbed tip. No osseous involvement. No fracture.

PROCEDURE

Median and radial nerve block. Small incision along the nail tract; nail removed intact. Wound irrigated and left open to heal by secondary intention. Tdap administered.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Puncture wound with foreign body of the left hand.
• Medical Reasoning: Penetrating nail gun injury while framing a house on a construction site at work. Retained barbed nail removed without complication. No bony or tendon involvement.
• Medical Treatment: Clindamycin 300 mg four times daily for 5 days given penicillin allergy. Elevation, daily dressing changes.
• Patient Education and Counseling: Return for spreading erythema, purulent drainage, fever, or loss of thumb motion.
• Work: No use of the left hand on the job site for 1 week. Workers' compensation paperwork completed.

Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Recheck in 2 to 3 days.

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , jacqueline . nice to meet you , i'm doctor mbeki .
[patient] hi . thanks for squeezing me in .
[doctor] of course . so the nurse said you were bitten by a dog ?
[patient] yes . this morning . i was out walking my dog , biscuit , like i do every morning before work . we were on the sidewalk on elm avenue , about two blocks from my house , and there's a house there where the dog is always behind the fence .
[doctor] okay .
[patient] well , today the gate was open , and this big dog came charging out . i think it was going for biscuit , and i stepped in between them , and it bit me on the back of my right leg . on the calf .
[doctor] oh , that's scary . did it let go on its own ?
[patient] it bit and kind of shook its head and then let go when the owner came out yelling . it was maybe a few seconds .
[doctor] okay . is your dog okay ?
[patient] she's fine , thank goodness . she's a little shaken up .
[doctor] good . do you know the owner ? do you know if the dog is vaccinated ?
[patient] yeah , the owner's name is jorge . she gave me her number and said the dog has all its shots , she's going to send me the rabies certificate .
[doctor] okay , that's really helpful . did you report it to animal control ?
[patient] not yet . should i ?
[doctor] yes , we're required to report dog bites , so we'll file that from here , and they'll arrange for the dog to be observed for ten days .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so how's the leg feeling ?
[patient] it hurts . it's like a five or six . it bled through my jeans , but i washed it with soap and water at home and put a bandage on it .
[doctor] good , washing it out right away is the most important thing . any numbness or tingling in your foot ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] can you walk on it okay ?
[patient] yeah , i'm limping a little because it's sore , but i can walk .
[doctor] okay . any medical problems i should know about ? diabetes , immune problems , anything like that ?
[patient] no , i'm healthy . i just take a multivitamin .
[doctor] any allergies to medications ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] and when was your last tetanus shot ?
[patient] i had a tdap when i was pregnant with my youngest , and he's four now .
[doctor] okay , so that's within five years , you're covered .
[doctor] all right , let me take a look . can you lie on your stomach for me ? okay . so on the posterior right calf there are two puncture wounds from the upper teeth , and below them a curved row of smaller punctures from the lower teeth , and there's a small tear between them , about two centimeters , with some jagged edges . there's mild bruising around it . the wounds are not very deep , they go into the fat but i do n't see any muscle . there's no active bleeding . the calf is soft , and your foot pulses are good .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] can you point your toes for me ? and pull them up ? good . sensation is normal in your foot .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so this is an open bite wound of the right lower leg , from a dog bite . the good news is that it's not too deep and it did n't hit anything important .
[patient] are you going to stitch it ?
[doctor] for dog bites on the leg , we usually do n't stitch the punctures , because closing them up traps bacteria in and increases infection risk . i'm going to irrigate it really well with a lot of saline , trim off a little bit of the jagged edge , and then leave it open with a dressing . the tear might get one or two loose stitches to bring the edges together , but i'd rather leave it open .
[patient] okay , whatever you think is best .
[doctor] i'm also going to start you on augmentin , eight seventy five milligrams twice a day for five days , to prevent infection . dog bites get infected fairly often .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] since the dog is known and vaccinated and will be observed , you do n't need rabies shots right now . if animal control ca n't confirm the vaccination or the dog gets sick , we'd start them .
[patient] that's good to hear .
[doctor] keep it clean , change the dressing every day , and keep the leg elevated when you can . you can take ibuprofen or tylenol for pain . if you see redness spreading , red streaks up the leg , pus , fever , or a lot more pain , call us at 868-242-7081 right away .
[patient] okay , thank you .
[doctor] i'd like to see you in two days for a wound check .
[patient] sounds good .

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , brenda . nice to meet you , i'm doctor castillo .
[patient] hi . thanks for squeezing me in .
[doctor] of course . so the nurse said you were bitten by a dog ?
[patient] yes . this morning . i was out walking my dog , biscuit , like i do every morning before work . we were on the sidewalk on elm avenue , about two blocks from my house , and there's a house there where the dog is always behind the fence .
[doctor] okay .
[patient] well , today the gate was open , and this big dog came charging out . i think it was going for biscuit , and i stepped in between them , and it bit me on the back of my right leg . on the calf .
[doctor] oh , that's scary . did it let go on its own ?
[patient] it bit and kind of shook its head and then let go when the owner came out yelling . it was maybe a few seconds .
[doctor] okay . is your dog okay ?
[patient] she's fine , thank goodness . she's a little shaken up .
[doctor] good . do you know the owner ? do you know if the dog is vaccinated ?
[patient] yeah , the owner's name is simon . she gave me her number and said the dog has all its shots , she's going to send me the rabies certificate .
[doctor] okay , that's really helpful . did you report it to animal control ?
[patient] not yet . should i ?
[doctor] yes , we're required to report dog bites , so we'll file that from here , and they'll arrange for the dog to be observed for ten days .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so how's the leg feeling ?
[patient] it hurts . it's like a five or six . it bled through my jeans , but i washed it with soap and water at home and put a bandage on it .
[doctor] good , washing it out right away is the most important thing . any numbness or tingling in your foot ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] can you walk on it okay ?
[patient] yeah , i'm limping a little because it's sore , but i can walk .
[doctor] okay . any medical problems i should know about ? diabetes , immune problems , anything like that ?
[patient] no , i'm healthy . i just take a multivitamin .
[doctor] any allergies to medications ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] and when was your last tetanus shot ?
[patient] i had a tdap when i was pregnant with my youngest , and he's four now .
[doctor] okay , so that's within five years , you're covered .
[doctor] all right , let me take a look . can you lie on your stomach for me ? okay . so on the posterior right calf there are two puncture wounds from the upper teeth , and below them a curved row of smaller punctures from the lower teeth , and there's a small tear between them , about two centimeters , with some jagged edges . there's mild bruising around it . the wounds are not very deep , they go into the fat but i do n't see any muscle . there's no active bleeding . the calf is soft , and your foot pulses are good .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] can you point your toes for me ? and pull them up ? good . sensation is normal in your foot .
[patient] okay .

[patient] are you going to stitch it ?

[patient] okay .
[doctor] since the dog is known and vaccinated and will be observed , you do n't need rabies shots right now . if animal control ca n't confirm the vaccination or the dog gets sick , we'd start them .
[patient] that's good to hear .

[patient] okay , thank you .
[doctor] i'd like to see you in two days for a wound check .
[patient] sounds good .

dialogue:
[doctor] good morning , eleni . i'm doctor rasmussen with employee health . how are you feeling ?
[patient] honestly , not good . my back is really bad .
[doctor] i'm sorry to hear that . tell me what happened .
[patient] so i'm an rn on the night shift on four west , the med-surg floor here at zenith printing . last night around three in the morning , i was in a patient's room , and we had a gentleman who had slid way down in the bed . he's a big guy , probably two eighty , and he could n't help much . the lift was being used in another room , so me and a tech tried to pull him up in bed using the draw sheet .
[doctor] okay .
[patient] and as we pulled , i was kind of bent over the bed and twisted , and i felt this sharp pull in my lower back , on the right side . like something grabbed .
[doctor] okay . did you finish your shift ?
[patient] i tried . i finished my charting but i could n't do any more lifting , and by the time i got home at seven thirty , i could barely get out of the car .
[doctor] okay . where exactly is the pain ?
[patient] right here , the low back , mostly on the right , just above my belt line .
[doctor] does it go down into your buttock or your leg ?
[patient] no , it stays in my back .
[doctor] any numbness or tingling in your legs or feet ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] any weakness in your legs ? any trouble controlling your bladder or bowels ?
[patient] no , none of that .
[doctor] okay , good . how bad is the pain ?
[patient] it's like a seven when i move , maybe a four if i lie still . bending forward is the worst . and getting up from sitting .
[doctor] have you taken anything for it ?
[patient] i took ibuprofen , four hundred , when i got home , and i used a heating pad . it helped a little .
[doctor] okay . have you ever hurt your back before ?
[patient] i had some back pain years ago after my second pregnancy , but nothing like this , and nothing at work .
[doctor] okay . any other medical problems ?
[patient] just migraines , but they've been quiet . i take sumatriptan if i need it .
[doctor] okay . let's take a look . can you stand up for me ? okay . i can see you're kind of guarding and leaning a little to the left . i'm going to press along your spine . any pain in the middle here ?
[patient] no , not on the bones .
[doctor] okay . and here , to the right ?
[patient] ow , yes , that's it .
[doctor] okay . so you have tenderness and spasm in the right lumbar paraspinal muscles , no midline tenderness . can you bend forward ? okay , you're limited to about forty degrees and it hurts . bending back hurts a little , and side bending to the left pulls on the right side . now lie down for me . i'm going to lift your leg straight . any pain shooting down the leg ?
[patient] no , just in my back .
[doctor] okay , so negative straight leg raise on both sides . your strength in your legs is five out of five , reflexes are normal and equal , and sensation is normal .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so , based on how this happened and your exam , this is a strain of the muscles of your lower back , a lumbar strain , from overexertion while lifting and repositioning a patient . i do n't see any signs of a disc problem or a nerve being pinched , and since there was no fall and no red flags , we do n't need x-rays today .
[patient] okay , that's good .
[doctor] most of these get better in two to four weeks . the most important thing is to stay gently active , do n't stay in bed . you can use ice or heat , whichever feels better . i'm going to give you naproxen , five hundred milligrams twice a day with food , and cyclobenzaprine , five milligrams at bedtime for muscle spasm . since you work nights , be careful , it can make you drowsy .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] i'm also going to refer you to physical therapy , twice a week for four weeks .
[patient] okay . and work ?
[doctor] i'm going to put you on modified duty for two weeks . no lifting over fifteen pounds , no patient transfers or repositioning . you can do charting , med pass , things like that . and when you go back to full duty , please use the lift or call the lift team for heavier patients .
[patient] i know , i know . we were just short staffed .
[doctor] i understand . we'll file this as a work injury , and i'll send the paperwork to workers' comp . come back and see me in one week , or sooner if you get numbness , weakness , or any bladder or bowel changes .
[patient] okay . thank you .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Low back pain after work injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Eleni Lefebvre is a 68-year-old female registered nurse employed at Zenith Printing who presents to employee health with acute low back pain following a work injury on 01/07/2020.

At approximately 3:00 AM during her night shift on the medical-surgical unit, she was in a patient room attempting to reposition a large, minimally mobile patient (approximately 280 pounds) who had slid down in bed. The mechanical lift was unavailable, so she and a coworker pulled the patient up using a draw sheet. While bent over the bed with a twisting motion, she felt a sharp pulling sensation in the right lower back. She completed charting but was unable to perform further lifting. Pain is 7/10 with movement and 4/10 at rest, worse with forward flexion and rising from a seated position. Pain does not radiate. She denies lower extremity numbness, tingling, or weakness, and denies bowel or bladder dysfunction. She took ibuprofen 400 mg and used a heating pad with mild relief. Remote history of postpartum back pain. Past medical history significant for migraine, managed with sumatriptan as needed.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Musculoskeletal: Antalgic posture with lean to the left. No midline lumbar tenderness. Tenderness and palpable spasm of the right lumbar paraspinal muscles. Lumbar flexion limited to 40 degrees with pain. Mild pain with extension. Negative straight leg raise bilaterally.
Neurological: Strength 5/5 in bilateral lower extremities. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric. Sensation intact.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Strain of muscle, fascia and tendon of the lower back.
• Medical Reasoning: Acute lumbar strain from overexertion while lifting and repositioning a patient in a hospital patient room at work. No radicular signs or red flags; imaging not indicated.
• Medical Treatment: Naproxen 500 mg twice daily with food. Cyclobenzaprine 5 mg at bedtime; cautioned about drowsiness given night shift work. Ice or heat as preferred. Remain active.
• Specialist Referrals: Physical therapy twice weekly for 4 weeks.
• Work: Modified duty for 2 weeks; no lifting over 15 pounds, no patient transfers or repositioning. Use of mechanical lift or lift team advised. Workers' compensation report filed.
• Patient Education and Counseling: Return precautions for numbness, weakness, or bowel or bladder changes.

Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Follow up in 1 week.

Patient room in hospital as the place of occurrence of the external cause
Activity, caregiving, lifting
Civilian activity done for income or pay

dialogue:
[doctor] good morning , farah . i'm doctor alvarado with employee health . how are you feeling ?
[patient] honestly , not good . my back is really bad .
[doctor] i'm sorry to hear that . tell me what happened .
[patient] so i'm an rn on the night shift on four west , the med-surg floor here at frontier cable . last night around three in the morning , i was in a patient's room , and we had a gentleman who had slid way down in the bed . he's a big guy , probably two eighty , and he could n't help much . the lift was being used in another room , so me and a tech tried to pull him up in bed using the draw sheet .
[doctor] okay .
[patient] and as we pulled , i was kind of bent over the bed and twisted , and i felt this sharp pull in my lower back , on the right side . like something grabbed .
[doctor] okay . did you finish your shift ?
[patient] i tried . i finished my charting but i could n't do any more lifting , and by the time i got home at seven thirty , i could barely get out of the car .
[doctor] okay . where exactly is the pain ?
[patient] right here , the low back , mostly on the right , just above my belt line .
[doctor] does it go down into your buttock or your leg ?
[patient] no , it stays in my back .
[doctor] any numbness or tingling in your legs or feet ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] any weakness in your legs ? any trouble controlling your bladder or bowels ?
[patient] no , none of that .
[doctor] okay , good . how bad is the pain ?
[patient] it's like a seven when i move , maybe a four if i lie still . bending forward is the worst . and getting up from sitting .
[doctor] have you taken anything for it ?
[patient] i took ibuprofen , four hundred , when i got home , and i used a heating pad . it helped a little .
[doctor] okay . have you ever hurt your back before ?
[patient] i had some back pain years ago after my second pregnancy , but nothing like this , and nothing at work .
[doctor] okay . any other medical problems ?
[patient] just migraines , but they've been quiet . i take sumatriptan if i need it .
[doctor] okay . let's take a look . can you stand up for me ? okay . i can see you're kind of guarding and leaning a little to the left . i'm going to press along your spine . any pain in the middle here ?
[patient] no , not on the bones .
[doctor] okay . and here , to the right ?
[patient] ow , yes , that's it .
[doctor] okay . so you have tenderness and spasm in the right lumbar paraspinal muscles , no midline tenderness . can you bend forward ? okay , you're limited to about forty degrees and it hurts . bending back hurts a little , and side bending to the left pulls on the right side . now lie down for me . i'm going to lift your leg straight . any pain shooting down the leg ?
[patient] no , just in my back .
[doctor] okay , so negative straight leg raise on both sides . your strength in your legs is five out of five , reflexes are normal and equal , and sensation is normal .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so , based on how this happened and your exam , this is a strain of the muscles of your lower back , a lumbar strain , from overexertion while lifting and repositioning a patient . i do n't see any signs of a disc problem or a nerve being pinched , and since there was no fall and no red flags , we do n't need x-rays today .
[patient] okay , that's good .
[doctor] most of these get better in two to four weeks . the most important thing is to stay gently active , do n't stay in bed . you can use ice or heat , whichever feels better . i'm going to give you naproxen , five hundred milligrams twice a day with food , and cyclobenzaprine , five milligrams at bedtime for muscle spasm . since you work nights , be careful , it can make you drowsy .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] i'm also going to refer you to physical therapy , twice a week for four weeks .
[patient] okay . and work ?
[doctor] i'm going to put you on modified duty for two weeks . no lifting over fifteen pounds , no patient transfers or repositioning . you can do charting , med pass , things like that . and when you go back to full duty , please use the lift or call the lift team for heavier patients .
[patient] i know , i know . we were just short staffed .
[doctor] i understand . we'll file this as a work injury , and i'll send the paperwork to workers' comp . come back and see me in one week , or sooner if you get numbness , weakness , or any bladder or bowel changes .
[patient] okay . thank you .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Low back pain after work injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Farah Szymanski is a 19-year-old female registered nurse employed at Frontier Cable who presents to employee health with acute low back pain following a work injury on 10/21/2021.

At approximately 3:00 AM during her night shift on the medical-surgical unit, she was in a patient room attempting to reposition a large, minimally mobile patient (approximately 280 pounds) who had slid down in bed. The mechanical lift was unavailable, so she and a coworker pulled the patient up using a draw sheet. While bent over the bed with a twisting motion, she felt a sharp pulling sensation in the right lower back. She completed charting but was unable to perform further lifting. Pain is 7/10 with movement and 4/10 at rest, worse with forward flexion and rising from a seated position. Pain does not radiate. She denies lower extremity numbness, tingling, or weakness, and denies bowel or bladder dysfunction. She took ibuprofen 400 mg and used a heating pad with mild relief. Remote history of postpartum back pain. Past medical history significant for migraine, managed with sumatriptan as needed.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Musculoskeletal: Antalgic posture with lean to the left. No midline lumbar tenderness. Tenderness and palpable spasm of the right lumbar paraspinal muscles. Lumbar flexion limited to 40 degrees with pain. Mild pain with extension. Negative straight leg raise bilaterally.
Neurological: Strength 5/5 in bilateral lower extremities. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric. Sensation intact.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Strain of muscle, fascia and tendon of the lower back.
• Medical Reasoning: Acute lumbar strain from overexertion while lifting and repositioning a patient in a hospital patient room at work. No radicular signs or red flags; imaging not indicated.
• Medical Treatment: Naproxen 500 mg twice daily with food. Cyclobenzaprine 5 mg at bedtime; cautioned about drowsiness given night shift work. Ice or heat as preferred. Remain active.
• Specialist Referrals: Physical therapy twice weekly for 4 weeks.
• Work: Modified duty for 2 weeks; no lifting over 15 pounds, no patient transfers or repositioning. Use of mechanical lift or lift team advised. Workers' compensation report filed.
• Patient Education and Counseling: Return precautions for numbness, weakness, or bowel or bladder changes.

Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Follow up in 1 week.

dialogue:
[doctor] hello , mr. ortega . i'm doctor yamamoto . what brings you in today ?
[patient] well , doc , i got into a fight with my lawn mower and the lawn mower won .
[doctor] uh oh . tell me about it .
[patient] so yesterday afternoon i was doing yard work at my house , mowing the backyard . i've got a slope back there by the flower beds , and i was pushing the mower across the hill , and it had rained in the morning , so the grass was wet . my right foot slid out from under me and went right under the edge of the mower deck .
[doctor] oh boy . was it a push mower ?
[patient] yeah , a gas push mower . self-propelled .
[doctor] and what were you wearing on your feet ?
[patient] old sneakers . i know , i know . my wife already gave me the lecture .
[doctor] okay . so the blade caught your foot through the shoe ?
[patient] yeah , it cut right through the side of the sneaker . it got the outside of my foot , kind of along the side here , toward the little toe .
[doctor] okay . did you go anywhere yesterday ?
[patient] my wife wanted me to go to the er , but it was n't bleeding that bad once i got the shoe off , so i washed it out with the hose and then in the tub , and wrapped it up . but this morning it was throbbing and she made me come in .
[doctor] okay , good that you came . how's the pain ?
[patient] about a five . it hurts more when i walk on it .
[doctor] any numbness in the toes ?
[patient] no , i can feel them .
[doctor] okay . can you move all your toes ?
[patient] yeah .
[doctor] and you have diabetes , right ? how's that going ?
[patient] yeah , type 2 . i take metformin , a thousand twice a day . my sugars run about one twenty in the morning .
[doctor] okay . your last a1c in the chart was six point eight , which is good . any problems with feeling in your feet from the diabetes ?
[patient] no , my feet have always been fine . the podiatrist checks them every year .
[doctor] okay , good . and when was your last tetanus ?
[patient] probably when i retired from the post office , so maybe eight years ago ?
[doctor] okay , so we'll give you a booster today since this was a dirty wound .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] let me take a look . go ahead and put your foot up here . okay . so on the lateral aspect of your right foot , over the fifth metatarsal , you've got a laceration that's about four centimeters long . the edges are a little ragged and there's some grass and dirt in it . it goes through the skin into the fat . i do n't see any tendon or bone . there's some mild swelling and a little redness right at the edges , but no spreading redness and no pus . can you push your foot out to the side against my hand ? good . your pulses in the foot are good , capillary refill is brisk . i'm going to check your sensation with this monofilament . can you feel that ? and that ?
[patient] yep , yep .
[doctor] okay , sensation is intact . we got an x-ray of the foot to make sure the blade did n't chip the bone or leave anything in there . that was normal , no fracture and no foreign body .
[patient] good .
[doctor] so you have a laceration of the right foot from the lawn mower blade . because it's a dirty wound and it's been almost twenty four hours , and you have diabetes , i'm a little more worried about infection than usual .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] here's what we'll do . i'll numb it up , scrub out all the grass and dirt , and irrigate it really well . i'll trim the ragged edges . then i'm going to close it loosely with a few stitches , leaving some space to drain .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] i'll start you on an antibiotic , cephalexin , five hundred milligrams four times a day for seven days . and you'll get the tetanus booster today .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] for your diabetes , keep taking the metformin . keep a close eye on your sugars , because infections can push them up , and if they're running over two hundred , call me . i'd like you to stay off the foot as much as you can for a few days , keep it elevated , and keep the dressing clean and dry .
[patient] okay . and the lawn ?
[doctor] the lawn can wait , or someone else can mow it . and when you go back to it , wear boots , and mow side to side across a slope , not up and down , and not when it's wet .
[patient] yeah , lesson learned .
[doctor] i want to see you back in three days for a wound check , and the stitches will come out in about ten to fourteen days . if you see any spreading redness , pus , fever , or your sugars go way up , come in sooner .
[patient] thank you , doc .

PATIENT NAME: Yusuf Kensington
DATE OF VISIT: 03/12/2023

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right foot laceration.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Kensington is a 82-year-old male with a past medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, who presents with a laceration to the right foot from a lawn mower.

Yesterday afternoon, the patient was mowing the backyard of his home with a gas-powered self-propelled push mower. While mowing across a wet slope near the flower beds, his right foot slipped under the edge of the mower deck and the blade cut through his sneaker into the lateral aspect of the foot. Bleeding was controlled at home; he irrigated the wound with a garden hose and in the tub and applied a wrap. He presents today due to throbbing pain, rated 5/10, worse with weight bearing. He denies numbness of the toes.

Regarding his type 2 diabetes, he takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily. Fasting glucose around 120. Most recent hemoglobin A1c 6.8%. No known peripheral neuropathy; annual podiatry exams. Last tetanus approximately 8 years ago.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Right foot: 4 cm laceration over the lateral foot at the level of the fifth metatarsal with ragged edges, contaminated with grass and soil. Extends to the subcutaneous tissue. No exposed tendon or bone. Mild edema and erythema limited to the wound margins. No purulence or lymphangitic streaking. Eversion strength intact. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses 2+. Capillary refill brisk. Monofilament sensation intact.

RESULTS

X-ray of the right foot: No fracture. No radiopaque foreign body.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Laceration without foreign body of the right foot.
• Medical Reasoning: Contaminated laceration from a powered lawn mower blade while mowing his yard. Delayed presentation at approximately 24 hours in a patient with diabetes increases infection risk.
• Medical Treatment: Local anesthesia, mechanical debridement of debris, high-volume irrigation, and trimming of devitalized wound edges. Loose closure with simple interrupted sutures. Cephalexin 500 mg four times daily for 7 days. Tdap administered.
• Patient Education and Counseling: Elevation, limited weight bearing, keep dressing clean and dry. Lawn mower safety reviewed, including protective footwear.

2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
• Medical Reasoning: Well controlled. No neuropathy on exam.
• Medical Treatment: Continue metformin 1000 mg twice daily. Monitor glucose closely during wound healing; call if above 200.

Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Wound check in 3 days. Suture removal in 10 to 14 days.

[doctor] hi there , simon . i'm doctor schaefer . i understand something got into your eye ?
[patient] yeah , my right eye . it feels like there's sand in it and i ca n't stop tearing up .

[patient] saturday afternoon . so about two days ago .
[doctor] and what were you doing when it happened ?
[patient] so i do metal sculptures as a hobby , kind of garden art , out of scrap steel . i was out in my garage at home , cleaning up a weld with my angle grinder . i had my safety glasses on , but they're the old kind without the side shields , and i felt something hit my eye from the side . like a little sting .
[doctor] okay . so a piece of metal from the grinder ?
[patient] i think so . sparks were flying everywhere , like they always do . i flushed it with water from the utility sink right away and it felt a little better , so i figured i got it out .
[doctor] okay .
[patient] but yesterday it got worse . it's red , it's watering all the time , and the light really bothers me . and every time i blink it feels like something's scratching .
[doctor] okay . any change in your vision ?
[patient] it's a little blurry on that side , mostly because it's so watery .
[doctor] okay . any pain when you move your eye , or a headache ?
[patient] no , just the scratchy feeling . it's like a four , maybe a five when i'm in the light .
[doctor] okay . do you wear contacts ?
[patient] no , just reading glasses .
[doctor] okay . any eye problems in the past ? surgery ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] any medical problems ?
[patient] no , i'm pretty healthy . i'm an accountant , so i sit at a desk all week , and on weekends i play golf and do my sculptures . that's about it .
[doctor] okay . any allergies ?
[patient] sulfa .
[doctor] okay . let's take a look . first we'll check your vision . cover your left eye and read the lowest line you can .
[patient] okay . e , f , p ... t , o , z ... that's about it .
[doctor] okay , so you're twenty forty in the right eye , and twenty twenty in the left . now i'm going to put in a numbing drop . this will sting for a second .
[patient] oh , that feels so much better .
[doctor] yeah , that's the anesthetic . okay , now some fluorescein dye , and i'm going to look with the slit lamp . look straight ahead at my ear . okay . so i can see a small metallic foreign body embedded in the cornea of your right eye , at about the four o'clock position , outside of the center of your vision . there's a rust ring around it , which happens when a piece of iron sits in the cornea for a day or two . there's a small area of staining around it , and the front chamber of the eye is quiet , i do n't see any cells . the pupil is round and reacts normally . i'm going to flip your upper eyelid to make sure there's nothing else under there . okay , that's clean .
[patient] so it's still in there ?

[patient] okay .

[patient] yeah , i'm ordering a face shield tonight .
[doctor] good . any questions ?
[patient] no , thank you . this was really helpful .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right eye foreign body sensation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Simon Xiong is a 76-year-old male who presents with right eye pain and foreign body sensation for 2 days.

Visual acuity: OD 20/40, OS 20/20.

Anterior chamber deep and quiet, no cells. Pupil round and reactive. Upper lid eversion without additional foreign body. Seidel test negative. Intraocular pressure normal.

PROCEDURE

Removal of corneal foreign body with a 25-gauge needle under slit lamp, followed by rust ring removal with an ophthalmic burr. Small residual corneal epithelial defect.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Foreign body in cornea, right eye.
• Medical Reasoning: Metallic corneal foreign body with rust ring from grinder use while doing metal sculpture in his home garage, no evidence of open globe.
• Medical Treatment: Foreign body and rust ring removed. Erythromycin ophthalmic ointment four times daily for 5 days. Tylenol or ibuprofen as needed. No topical anesthetic prescribed.
• Patient Education and Counseling: Avoid rubbing the eye. Use wraparound safety glasses or a full face shield when grinding. Return immediately for worsening vision, worsening pain, or corneal opacity.

Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Follow up in 2 days for recheck of the epithelial defect and residual rust.

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , yasmin . i'm doctor abernethy . how are you feeling now that you've had some fluids ?
[patient] better . a lot better than when i came in . i still feel kind of weak .
[doctor] okay . that's expected . can you tell me what happened today ?
[patient] so i work for bayside shipyard , picking strawberries . we start at six in the morning . today it was really hot , they said it was going to be ninety eight , and there's no shade out in the field at all , it's just rows and rows .
[doctor] okay .
[patient] i was bent over picking all morning , and around one o'clock i started getting a really bad headache and i felt dizzy . i was sweating like crazy , my shirt was soaked . and then i felt like i was going to throw up . and my legs started cramping .
[doctor] okay . did you pass out ?
[patient] no , i did n't pass out . i felt like i was going to , everything kind of went gray , so i sat down in the dirt between the rows . my crew leader hamid saw me and brought me over to the truck and put the air conditioning on and gave me water . and then they called the ambulance because i threw up the water .
[doctor] okay . how much water were you drinking during the morning ?
[patient] not enough . i had one bottle . the water cooler is at the end of the rows and we get paid by the box , so you do n't want to stop .
[doctor] i understand . did you take any breaks ?
[patient] one break , at like nine thirty .
[doctor] okay . were you confused at all ? did anybody say you were acting strange or not making sense ?
[patient] no , i knew where i was the whole time . i was just really tired and sick .
[doctor] okay , that's important . any chest pain or trouble breathing ?
[patient] my heart was pounding , but no chest pain .
[doctor] okay . any medical problems ?
[patient] no . i'm usually really healthy . i came up from california for the season with my two sisters , and this is my third year doing this .
[doctor] do you take any medicines ? water pills , anything for allergies ?
[patient] no , nothing .
[doctor] any alcohol or drugs ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] okay . and have you had this happen before ?
[patient] last summer i got a little dizzy once , but i just sat in the shade and it went away .
[doctor] okay . so when you came in , the paramedics measured your temperature at one hundred and one point two , your heart rate was one twenty two , and your blood pressure was ninety eight over sixty . you were sweaty and flushed , but you were awake and talking normally .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] we gave you two liters of iv fluid , and some ondansetron for the nausea , and cooled you down with ice packs and the fan . now your temperature is ninety nine point one , your heart rate is eighty eight , and your blood pressure is one twelve over seventy . on exam , your skin is still a little warm , your mouth is a little dry , and your neurological exam is completely normal , you're alert and oriented , no confusion , strength is normal .
[patient] that's good .
[doctor] it is . so we checked some labs . your sodium was a little low at one thirty three , your kidney function is normal , and your muscle enzyme , the ck , was normal , so there's no sign of muscle breakdown . your urine was concentrated , which tells me you were very dehydrated .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so what you had is heat exhaustion . it's from working hard for a long time out in the heat and the sun without enough water and rest . the important part is that you did n't have any confusion and your temperature never got really high , so this was not heat stroke , which is much more dangerous .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] but heat exhaustion can turn into heat stroke if you keep pushing , so we need to take it seriously .
[patient] okay . can i go back to work tomorrow ?
[doctor] i'd like you to take tomorrow off and rest , drink plenty of fluids , and you can use an electrolyte drink . then when you go back , you need to take a break in the shade every hour , and drink a cup of water every fifteen to twenty minutes , even if you're not thirsty . i'm going to write a note for your employer saying that , and that you need access to water and shade .
[patient] thank you . that will help .
[doctor] wear a wide brim hat and light loose clothes , and try to do the hardest work early in the morning . if you start getting a headache , dizziness , cramps , or nausea again , stop , go to the shade , and drink water . and if you get confused , stop sweating , or faint , that's an emergency , call nine one one .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] we'll keep you here for another hour to finish the fluids and make sure you can drink without throwing up . then you can go home . if you need anything , our clinic number is 337-886-3255 .
[patient] okay , thank you so much .

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Heat-related illness.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Yasmin Abernathy is a 41-year-old female with no significant past medical history who presents by ambulance from her workplace on 04/03/2020 with heat-related illness.

The patient is employed by Bayside Shipyard as a strawberry harvester. She began work at 6:00 AM in an open farm field without shade, with ambient temperature reportedly 98 degrees Fahrenheit. She had one bottle of water and one break during the morning. At approximately 1:00 PM, she developed severe headache, dizziness, profuse sweating, nausea, and leg cramps, followed by near-syncope. She did not lose consciousness. She was placed in an air-conditioned vehicle and given water, which she vomited. She reports palpitations but denies chest pain or dyspnea. She denies confusion; she was oriented throughout. No medications, diuretics, alcohol, or drug use. Prior mild heat-related dizziness last summer.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Vital Signs: On EMS arrival, temperature 101.2 F, heart rate 122, blood pressure 98/60. After treatment, temperature 99.1 F, heart rate 88, blood pressure 112/70.
Skin: Warm, mildly flushed. Dry mucous membranes.
Neurological: Alert and oriented x3. No confusion. Strength normal throughout.

RESULTS

Sodium 133 (mildly low). Creatinine within normal limits. Creatine kinase within normal limits. Urinalysis: concentrated urine, elevated specific gravity.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Heat exhaustion.
• Medical Reasoning: Prolonged strenuous agricultural work in a farm field in excessive natural heat with inadequate hydration and rest. Core temperature below 104 F and normal mental status; no evidence of heat stroke. No rhabdomyolysis. Mild hyponatremia consistent with volume depletion.
• Medical Treatment: Normal saline 2 L IV, ondansetron 4 mg IV, active cooling with ice packs and fan. Observe for tolerance of oral intake prior to discharge.
• Patient Education and Counseling: Oral hydration with electrolyte solution. Warning signs of heat stroke reviewed.

2. Occupational exposure to extreme heat.
• Work: Off work for 1 day. On return, hourly rest breaks in the shade, water every 15 to 20 minutes, access to water and shade; work note provided to employer.

Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.
